      "content":"# 248 — Encapsulated map as box\n\n## Status\nin progress · input-side load-time inlining shipped; output-side\n(ext-consumed write boxes), editor UI, and recursion across mixed\next-consumed wires deferred\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput-side encapsulation runs at graph load. The loader recognizes\n`kind: \"map\"` with a `ref` to a sub-map directory. A new pass between\n`load_boxes` and `resolve_topology` walks every BOX_MAP record,\nloads the sub-map's boxes into the parent's arena, prefix-renames\ntheir ids with `<encap_id>__<sub_id>`, splices them into the parent's\nflat box list, then rewires each parent producer's connection that\ntargeted the encapsulating box. The rewire splices THROUGH the\nexternally-supplied data box: each parent wire to `encap.port` is\nreplaced with copies pointing to the matching data box's\ndownstreams, preserving each from_branch tag. Externally-supplied\ndata boxes are matched to the encapsulating box's input ports by\nthe issue's three binding kinds (positional / numbered by index,\nnamed by string).\n\nAfter inlining, the encap box stays in the index but is inert\n(connections cleared, `ref` stripped — the loader skips it on\nsubsequent passes, dispatch's BOX_MAP case is a logged no-op). The\next-supplied data box is also orphaned (its outgoing connections\nwere absorbed into the parent producer; the cache pass skips it so\nthe \"neither value nor path\" check doesn't reject the value-less\nshape).\n\nThe end-to-end fixture `tests/maps/248-encap-input-only/` proves\nthe splice reaches disk: a parent read box wires\n`\"encapsulated-greeting\"` to a BOX_MAP whose sub-map has one\nexternally-supplied data box feeding a write box; the parent's\nbytes land in `/tmp/soramech-248-encap-out.txt`.\n\nOutput-side encapsulation (externally-consumed write boxes\nsurfacing as the encap's output ports) is not yet wired. Wires\nthe user drew from `encap.port_x` to a parent consumer don't fire\nin this slice. The editor toggles, file-browser Encapsulate\naction, and the multi-output exception to issue 218 also remain\nahead.\n\n## Concept\n\nA map directory is normally opened via the map-select UI as the\ntop-level graph being edited. **This issue adds a second way to\nopen a map:** through the file browser, as an *encapsulated box*\non the currently-edited parent map. The opened map becomes a\nsingle box on the parent's canvas. Its inputs come from `data`\nboxes inside the sub-map that have been marked\n**externally-supplied**; its outputs come from `write` boxes\ninside the sub-map that have been marked **externally-consumed**.\nThe two markings are symmetric: one redirects an input from \"file\non disk\" to \"wire from parent,\" the other redirects an output\nfrom \"file on disk\" to \"wire to parent.\"\n\nEncapsulation is a function-like abstraction over a sub-graph.\nThe parent doesn't see the sub-map's internals; it sees one box\nwith declared input ports, declared output ports, and known\nsemantics. The sub-map can be edited independently, reused across\nparent maps, and packaged once for distribution.\n\n**Encapsulated boxes are the documented exception to issue 218's\n\"single output per box\" rule.** Every other box kind has exactly\none output (with fan-out via multiple wires leaving that one\noutput). An encapsulated map has *N* distinct output ports, one\nper `write` box marked externally-consumed. *N* may be zero (the\nmap is a pure side-effect sink), one (matches the common case),\nor many. The exception exists because an encapsulated map's\noutputs are independent values produced by independent\n`write` boxes — packing them into a single blob (the earlier\ndesign in this issue) would have repurposed file-writing\nmachinery to emit strings into wires, which is the wrong shape:\n`write` boxes should keep their semantics (\"terminate a value\")\nand the destination kind (\"file vs. parent wire\") should be a\nmode toggle, not a substitution.\n\n## Marked input ports inside the sub-map\n\nA **data** box inside the sub-map (kind: `data`, the existing\nlanguage-agnostic file-IO source) can be marked as\n**externally-supplied** via a small toggle on the box's\ninspector. Toggling declares: \"this data box's value comes from\nthe encapsulating context, not from its `path` or `value`\nfield.\"\n\nThe toggle is intentionally scoped to `data` boxes — those are\nthe natural entry points for external values into a map. Call\nboxes / read boxes / write boxes don't carry the toggle, which\nkeeps the inspector uncluttered for the common cases. Each\nexternal input becomes a small shared-memory chunk seeded by\nthe encapsulating call's invoke; the marked data box reads from\nthat chunk on each fire, treating it identically to a value\nloaded from disk.\n\nThe toggle records the port's binding kind on the box JSON:\n\n```json\n{\n    \"id\": \"sum_input\",\n    \"kind\": \"data\",\n    \"external\": {\n        \"kind\": \"named\",            // or \"positional\" / \"numbered\"\n        \"name\": \"count\",            // for named\n        \"index\": 0                  // for positional / numbered\n    },\n    \"...\": \"...\"\n}\n```\n\nThree binding kinds capture how the encapsulating box's input\nmaps to this internal port:\n\n- **`positional`** — bound by argument order. The encapsulating\n  box has N input ports; the *k*th port's value flows to the\n  internal box whose `external.index` is *k*. Conceptually\n  matches positional function arguments.\n- **`numbered`** — bound by an explicit integer index. Same shape\n  as positional but the user picks the number (so they can leave\n  gaps, reorder freely, etc.).\n- **`named`** — bound by a string name. The encapsulating box's\n  input port has a label; the matching internal box's\n  `external.name` is the same string.\n\nA single sub-map can mix kinds across its marked boxes — some\npositional, some named — and the parent map's encapsulated box\nexposes the union as its input ports.\n\n## Marked output ports inside the sub-map\n\nA **write** box inside the sub-map (kind: `write`, issue 229's\nfile-write kind) can be marked as **externally-consumed** via a\nsmall toggle on the box's inspector — the mirror of the\nexternally-supplied toggle on data boxes. Toggling declares:\n\"this write box's value goes to the encapsulating context, not\nto its `path` field.\"\n\nThe toggle is intentionally scoped to `write` boxes — those are\nthe natural exit points for values out of a map. Each\nexternally-consumed write box surfaces as one **distinct output\nport** on the encapsulating box. The port carries that one\nvalue, on its own wire, to whichever downstream box(es) the\nparent wires it to.\n\nThe toggle records the port's binding kind on the box JSON, in\nthe same shape as the input-side toggle:\n\n```json\n{\n    \"id\": \"result_value\",\n    \"kind\": \"write\",\n    \"external\": {\n        \"kind\": \"named\",            // or \"positional\" / \"numbered\"\n        \"name\": \"result\",           // for named\n        \"index\": 0                  // for positional / numbered\n    },\n    \"...\": \"...\"\n}\n```\n\nThree binding kinds — same vocabulary as the input side:\n\n- **`positional`** — bound by argument order. The encapsulating\n  box's *k*th output port is the externally-consumed write box\n  whose `external.index` is *k*.\n- **`numbered`** — bound by an explicit integer index, allowing\n  gaps and reordering.\n- **`named`** — bound by a string name. The encapsulating box's\n  output port carries that label.\n\nA write box marked externally-consumed **also** writes to its\n`path` if one is set — the two destinations are independent. The\nwrite box can opt out of the file write (set `path: null`) if it\nexists solely to surface a value to the parent.\n\nEach externally-consumed write box's emitted value becomes an\nindependent output wire on the encapsulating box. The earlier\ndesign in this issue packed all write-box outputs into a single\nbyte-blob with a leading size index; that design is rejected —\nsee the \"Concept\" section for why. No packing, no unpacking\nlibrary; the wire format is the same per-port wire format every\nother box uses.\n\n## File layout in the parent map\n\n**The encapsulating box is a normal `call` box.** From the\neditor's perspective it has the same JSON shape as any other\ncall box — `kind: \"call\"`, `lang`, `ref`, `fn`, `inputs`,\n`connections`, `routing`. What makes it an encapsulation is\nthat its `lang` is `map` and its `ref` points to a sub-map\ndirectory rather than a source file. The map-language spec\n(`langs/map/spec.so`) is responsible for the \"behind the\nscenes\" processing — running the sub-graph and packing the\noutputs.\n\n```json\n{\n    \"id\": \"stats_pipeline\",\n    \"kind\": \"call\",\n    \"lang\": \"map\",\n    \"ref\": \"../shared-maps/stats-pipeline\",\n    \"fn\": null,                                  // unused for map kind\n    \"inputs\": [\n        { \"name\": \"count\", \"type\": \"int\" },\n        { \"name\": \"label\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n    ],\n    \"outputs\": [\n        { \"name\": \"mean\",  \"type\": \"float\" },\n        { \"name\": \"stdev\", \"type\": \"float\" },\n        { \"name\": \"n\",     \"type\": \"int\" }\n    ],\n    \"...\": \"...\"\n}\n```\n\nThe `outputs` array on the encapsulating box JSON is the\ndocumented exception to the single-output-per-box rule. The\ngraph loader treats each entry as a distinct output slot,\nallocates one ring buffer per output port (same machinery as\ninput slots, but on the producer side), and lets the parent\nwire each output independently.\n\nThe map-language spec is registered in the spec registry the\nsame way `lua` / `c` / `bash` are. Its `file_ext` is `.map`\n(or no extension if the ref points to a directory). The graph\nloader resolves the `ref`, the map spec's `init` (per worker)\nloads the sub-graph, and its `invoke` runs the sub-graph and\npacks the outputs. From the dispatch layer's view, an\nencapsulating call is just another spec invocation.\n\nThe sub-map's input ports (derived from its marked data boxes)\nand output ports (derived from its marked write boxes) are\nexposed on the encapsulating box's JSON as `inputs` and `outputs`\narrays. The user doesn't write either array themselves — the\neditor generates them from the sub-map on first encapsulation\nand re-syncs them when the sub-map changes.\n\n## Editor UI\n\n### File browser\n\nThe file browser (issue 207's source-file-browser, or its\ndescendant) shows map directories with a distinct icon — a\nfolder-like glyph annotated to suggest \"this is a runnable\ngraph, not a source file.\" Clicking opens a small menu:\n\n- **Edit this map** — switches the editor's active map (the\n  existing map-select behaviour).\n- **Encapsulate** — adds the map as a `kind: \"map\"` box to the\n  currently-edited parent map. The new box appears on the\n  canvas at the cursor position; the user wires it in like any\n  other box.\n\n### External-binding toggle (inputs and outputs)\n\nThe inspector for a `data` box's value-input grows a small\ntoggle that marks it externally-supplied; the inspector for a\n`write` box's value-input grows the same toggle that marks it\nexternally-consumed. Both surface in the same visual idiom:\n\n```\n  ┌─────────────────────────────┐\n  │ count   [● external]        │ ← toggle on, port is externally-bound\n  │   kind:    named            │\n  │   name:    \"count\"          │\n  └─────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nWhen the toggle is on, the inspector reveals the kind selector\n(positional / numbered / named) and the name / index field.\nWhen off, the port behaves normally (wires-in / literal value on\nthe data box; `path` write on the write box).\n\nA map with no marked data boxes encapsulates to a no-input box\n(just a source of values). A map with no externally-consumed\nwrite boxes encapsulates to a box with no output (side-effecting\nonly — legal but unusual; useful for \"fire and forget\"\nsub-pipelines).\n\n### Visual on the canvas\n\nThe encapsulating box renders distinctly — different border,\nmaybe a small \"sub-map\" badge — so the user sees at a glance\nthat this isn't a leaf call. Hovering shows the sub-map's name\nand a small thumbnail of its graph.\n\n## Runtime model — two paths, needs a decision\n\nTwo implementation paths exist. The encapsulating box being a\nnormal `call` box from the editor's perspective doesn't pick\nbetween them; the choice lives in what the map-language spec\ndoes behind the scenes and what (if anything) the compile\npipeline does at build time.\n\n### Path A — Compile-time inlining\n\nThe compile pipeline (issue 309) recognizes encapsulating call\nboxes and **expands them into their sub-graphs at build time**.\nSteps the compile step takes per encapsulating box:\n\n1. Load the sub-map's graph from `ref`.\n2. Rename every internal box with a parent-namespaced id:\n   `stats_pipeline__compute`, `stats_pipeline__filter`, etc.\n3. Copy every internal wire across, with the renamed ids.\n4. For each marked data box inside the sub-map: replace it with\n   a wire that brings the encapsulating box's matching input\n   value directly to wherever the data box's output was wired.\n5. For each externally-consumed write box inside the sub-map:\n   route its emitted value to the matching output port on the\n   encapsulating box (so downstream consumers in the parent map\n   see the value on a distinct wire per write box). The write\n   box still performs its disk-write if `path` is set.\n6. Remove the encapsulating call box from the parent's graph.\n\nAfter expansion, the compiled artifact is **one flat graph**.\nThe runtime never sees `lang: \"map\"`. The map-language spec\nexists only for the editor's sake (validating refs, listing\nthe sub-map's inputs/outputs for the inspector).\n\n**Pros:**\n\n- No new runtime machinery. The dispatch, slot store, and spec\n  registry all operate on flat graphs as today.\n- Best per-call performance — no sub-graph startup cost, no\n  nested dispatch.\n- **Composes cleanly with issue 313** (whole-program same-\n  language merge). The inlined sub-graph's same-language regions\n  merge into the parent's merge as if they were always one map.\n- Debugging stack traces inside the inlined region point to\n  flat box ids — readable once you know the naming convention.\n\n**Cons:**\n\n- The sub-map gets baked into every parent that uses it. Edit\n  the sub-map → every parent must recompile.\n- No hot-reload of sub-maps. The editor would have to\n  re-expand on every parent map edit, or accept that the\n  parent's last-compiled artifact lags the sub-map source.\n- Compile time grows with sub-map size × number of\n  encapsulations.\n- Deep recursion (sub-maps inside sub-maps inside sub-maps)\n  inflates the parent's compiled output proportionally.\n- The multi-output exception to issue 218 has to be carried\n  through compile-time inlining as well: after expansion, the\n  parent's flat graph has wires going from internal sub-graph\n  boxes directly to whichever parent consumers were wired to\n  the encapsulating box's output ports. The compile-time\n  artifact loses the \"encapsulated box\" identity entirely but\n  preserves the per-output routing.\n\n### Path B — Runtime sub-graph dispatch\n\nThe encapsulating box stays as one box in the parent's flat\ngraph. The map-language spec's `invoke` runs the sub-graph at\ncall time:\n\n1. **`map_init(worker_idx)`** — load every sub-map referenced\n   by the running program (or lazily on first invoke). Each\n   worker gets its own copy of the sub-graph state (slot store,\n   dispatch context).\n2. **`map_invoke(handle, sub_map_dir, ..., inputs, ..., outputs, ...)`** —\n   for each input, write the bytes into the shared-memory chunk\n   that the matching marked data box reads from. Then drive the\n   sub-graph to quiescence using the existing pool's dispatch\n   loop (the sub-graph's tasks are normal pool tasks distinguished\n   by a nested namespace). When quiescent, walk each\n   externally-consumed write box and push its emitted value onto\n   the matching output port of the encapsulating box. Each output\n   port surfaces on its own wire to the parent — no packing.\n\nThe sub-graph's parallelism uses the same thread pool as the\nparent's. A sub-graph's tasks compete for workers alongside the\nparent's tasks. From the pool's perspective, the difference is\njust box-id prefix.\n\n**Pros:**\n\n- Sub-map loaded once per worker, reused across many parent\n  invocations and across many parent maps.\n- Hot-reload friendly: change the sub-map, parent picks up the\n  new version on next run (no parent recompile).\n- The multi-output boundary is clean — each externally-consumed\n  write box pushes onto its own output port wire as it would\n  if it were a leaf box in the parent graph, no packing or\n  unpacking required.\n- Debugging stack traces preserve the sub-map identity (the\n  task's namespace says \"this came from `stats-pipeline`\").\n- Recursion is natural — the spec's invoke can nest-invoke its\n  own spec for a sub-sub-map.\n\n**Cons:**\n\n- New runtime machinery: the map spec's `invoke` runs a nested\n  dispatch loop. Either the dispatch layer grows a re-entrancy\n  contract, or the map spec replicates enough of the dispatch\n  machinery to drive the sub-graph itself.\n- Each encapsulating-box call pays sub-graph startup cost —\n  seeding inputs, possibly resetting slot state from a previous\n  invocation, collecting outputs at the end. Small but real.\n- Does NOT compose with issue 313's same-language merge — the\n  sub-map's source can't merge with the parent's, because at\n  build time they're separate compilation units. (313 could be\n  extended to merge across encapsulation boundaries, but that's\n  a separate design.)\n- Re-using the sub-graph across invocations requires reset\n  semantics. Either the sub-graph's slots and counters get\n  reset between invocations (cost), or each invocation gets a\n  fresh sub-graph instance (allocation cost).\n\n### What to weigh\n\nThe choice turns on whether encapsulation is **a build-time\nabstraction (like a C macro or a Lua-function-inlined-by-LuaJIT)**\nor **a runtime composition (like calling a function in a shared\nlibrary)**.\n\nPath A treats it as a build-time abstraction. Encapsulation is\nhow the user organizes source; the compiled artifact is one\nflat program. Best for raw performance and integration with\nthe existing machinery. Cost: rebuild propagation.\n\nPath B treats it as a runtime composition. Encapsulation is a\nreal boundary at execution time, with the packed-blob output\nas the wire format across the boundary. Best for modularity,\nhot-reload, and clear semantics. Cost: per-call overhead and\nloss of cross-boundary optimization.\n\nA third option exists — **support both, picked per encapsulating\nbox** via a small flag in the box JSON (`encap_mode: \"inline\" |\n\"runtime\"`). The compile pipeline expands inline-mode boxes;\nruntime-mode boxes stay encapsulated. Each user picks per\nencapsulation based on their needs. Higher implementation cost\nbut maximally flexible. Probably not in the first slice; flag it\nfor later if either A or B alone proves too narrow.\n\nRecursion (a sub-map encapsulates another sub-map) works under\neither path. Cycles between maps are a compile-time (or\nload-time, under B) error.\n\n## Relationship to existing issues\n\n- **Issue 207 (source-file-browser)** — the file browser is the\n  entry point for the \"encapsulate\" action.\n- **Issue 239 (literal port shrinks to nodule)** — the\n  external-input slider reuses the same visual idiom on the\n  input-port row.\n- **Issue 229 (data box as language-agnostic file IO)** —\n  encapsulation adds an \"externally-supplied\" toggle to data\n  boxes and an \"externally-consumed\" toggle to write boxes. The\n  boxes' default behaviour (read from / write to disk) is\n  unchanged; the toggles route the value through a parent-wire\n  instead of (or in addition to) the disk file.\n\n- **Issue 218 (single output per box)** — the encapsulated\n  `kind: \"map\"` box is the documented exception. Every other box\n  has exactly one output; an encapsulated box has one per\n  externally-consumed write box (zero or more).\n- **Issue 309 (build system / compile pipeline)** — the\n  compile-time inlining path (option A above) extends the\n  pipeline with an \"encapsulation expansion\" step.\n- **Issue 313 (whole-program same-language merge)** — composes\n  with compile-time inlining; the inlined sub-graph's same-\n  language regions merge into the parent's merge as if they\n  were always part of one map.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — box state, the `kind: \"map\"` box,\n  the per-input-port external-binding state.\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — file browser; menu with Edit /\n  Encapsulate actions.\n- `assets/index.html` — inspector UI for the external-binding\n  toggle.\n- `src/006-server-main.lua` — HTTP backend; resolving sub-map\n  paths, validating bindings.\n- `src/010-graph-loader.{c,h}` — graph loader; recognise\n  `kind: \"map\"`, resolve the sub-map, build the encapsulated\n  shape.\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — encapsulating-box dispatch (runtime\n  path) or compile-time expansion (compile path).\n- `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` — encapsulation expansion if the\n  compile-time path wins.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. **Box JSON schema**: add `kind: \"map\"`, the `ref` field, and\n   the per-input `external` block. Graph loader rejects with a\n   clear error if any field is missing where required.\n2. **External-binding toggles**: inspector toggle on data boxes\n   (externally-supplied) and write boxes (externally-consumed);\n   kind / name / index selectors when on. Same visual idiom for\n   both.\n3. **File browser \"Encapsulate\" action**: adds a `kind: \"map\"`\n   box to the parent at the cursor position. Reads the sub-map's\n   marked data boxes and marked write boxes to populate the new\n   box's `inputs` and `outputs` arrays.\n4. **Graph loader sub-map resolution**: load the sub-map's\n   `meta.json` and `boxes/`; record its marked-input and\n   marked-output lists on the parent box record.\n5. **Multi-output slot allocation**: the encapsulated box gets\n   one output slot per externally-consumed write box (the\n   documented exception to issue 218). Graph loader and slot\n   store accept this shape only for `lang: \"map\"` boxes.\n6. **Pick A or B**: compile-time inlining or runtime sub-graph\n   dispatch. Prototype the simpler of the two end-to-end on a\n   trivial sub-map (`maps/encap-trivial`).\n7. **Recursion**: nested encapsulation; cycle detection at\n   compile (or load) time.\n8. **Editor visualization**: distinct canvas rendering for\n   encapsulating boxes; tooltip / thumbnail.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Sub-map identity for the editor**: when the parent\n  encapsulates `maps/<sub>`, what happens if the user later\n  renames or moves `<sub>`? The reference path is brittle.\n  Options: store a stable id in the sub-map's `meta.json` and\n  reference that, plus a path hint; or require the sub-map to\n  live inside the parent's map directory tree.\n- **Re-sync behaviour when the sub-map changes**: if the user\n  edits the sub-map and changes its marked inputs, the parent's\n  encapsulating box's `inputs` array drifts out of date. Likely\n  resolution: on parent map load, the loader re-derives the\n  inputs from the sub-map and warns the user if wiring needs\n  fixing.\n- **`.map` packaging format**: this issue assumes sub-maps are\n  directories. A single-file `.map` archive (tarball / zip)\n  would be more portable for distribution. Out of scope here;\n  separate ticket if it becomes relevant.\n- **Output naming consistency**: outputs use the same\n  positional / numbered / named binding kinds as inputs. The\n  question is whether a single encapsulated box can mix kinds\n  across outputs (e.g. two named, one positional), or whether\n  all outputs must share a kind. Inputs already allow mixing —\n  preferable to keep outputs symmetric.\n- **Side-effect ordering**: the sub-map's write boxes run as\n  part of the sub-graph and write to disk. The encapsulating\n  box's output emits *after* those side effects complete. If\n  the parent wires the encapsulating box's output forward, the\n  downstream task can rely on the writes having happened. Worth\n  documenting; not a design choice so much as a consequence of\n  the existing dispatch model.\n\n## Design history\n\nThe original 2026-05-21 design packed all write-box outputs into\na single byte-blob with a leading null-terminated size index, and\nthe encapsulated box had a single output wire carrying that blob:\n\n> \"the write data slots are the outputs, written to a chunk of\n> heap memory. At the beginning is an array of sizes — null\n> terminated. Then, immediately afterwards, is the first index\n> of data...\" — 2026-05-21\n\nThat design was reconsidered on 2026-05-23 while specifying the\nself-construction built-ins (issue 319). The reconsideration:\nboxes never \"return\" values to the outside world under the\nexisting model — they push values onto wires that other boxes\nconsume, and `write` boxes specifically terminate values to\nfiles. Repurposing the file-writing destination to emit strings\ninto wires would have been a substitution of one mechanism for\nanother. The symmetric design — mark write boxes\nexternally-consumed, surface each as its own output port —\npreserves the `write` box's semantics (\"terminate a value\") and\ntreats the destination as a mode toggle. Cost: multi-output boxes\nexist for this kind alone; benefit: one mechanism does both jobs\ncleanly.\n",
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/248-encapsulated-map-as-box.md"
    }
  },

Several design questions need user resolution\nbefore implementation can begin. See **Open design questions**\nbelow.\n\n## Concept\n\nA map should be able to build more of itself while running.\nTwo built-in primitives, exposed by the runtime to every language\nspec, are enough to bootstrap that capability:\n\n- **`create_box(filepath, function_name) -> box_handle`**\n  Spawn a new box on the currently-running map. The first argument\n  is the file holding the function the box will run; the second is\n  the name of that function inside the file.         "text":"Here's where we left off on the encapsulated-map-as-box issue, and what I think the next move is.\n\n**Input side is done and on disk.** The most recent commit shipped load-time inlining: when the graph loader sees a sub-map referenced as a box, it slurps the sub-map's boxes into the parent's arena with prefixed ids, then rewrites every parent wire that targeted the encapsulating box so it goes *through* the matching externally-supplied data box and lands on whatever the data box was feeding inside the sub-map. There's an end-to-end fixture under `tests/maps/248-encap-input-only/` that proves bytes from the parent reach a write box inside the sub-map.\n\n**Three things are still deferred** — listed in the issue's status header and now on the todo list:\n\n1. **Output-side encapsulation.** Wires the user drew *from* the encapsulating box's output ports don't fire yet. The symmetric splice — every externally-consumed write box inside the sub-map surfaces as its own distinct output port on the parent's view of the encap box — is the natural next slice, since it mirrors the machinery the input side already proves out.\n2. **Editor UI.** The inspector toggle (externally-supplied on data boxes, externally-consumed on write boxes) and the file-browser \"Encapsulate\" action that drops a `kind: \"map\"` box onto the parent at cursor position.\n3. **Recursion** across nested encapsulations + cycle detection at load time.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\n- The decision to inline at *load time* rather than compile time (path A in the issue) or with a true nested dispatch loop (path B) is a third path — splicing happens after the parent's JSON is read but before topology is resolved, so the runtime never sees `kind: \"map\"`. It gets path-A's flat-graph simplicity without depending on issue 309's compile pipeline being in shape.\n- The reason encapsulated maps are the *one* documented exception to issue 218's \"single output per box\" rule is that each externally-consumed write box is genuinely an independent value with its own semantics — bundling them into a packed blob would have been file-write machinery doing wire-emit work, the wrong shape. Keeping the multi-output exception on this one kind preserves both invariants.\n- Reference-counted artifacts (issue 315) and self-construction (319) are blockers for a real release because together they're what lets *other programs* hold onto a SoraMech artifact across time and let a running map mutate itself — until those land, SoraMech is single-user, single-shot.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\nI also queued 319 and 315 on the todo list as you asked. Want me to dive into the **output-side splice** for 248 next? That's the smallest self-contained step that unblocks the rest of 248 (the editor toggle is mostly a UI affordance over data the loader already needs to read), and it'll let me show you a fixture where a wire leaving the encap box actually carries a value into the parent. Or would you rather I poke at 319 / 315 first since those are the release blockers?"

    "role":"assistant",
    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "input":{
          "content":"# 250 — Routing kind: nonlinearity (squash)\n\n## Status\nopen · design carried forward from issues 240 / 241 / 242 / 243\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe routing kinds shipped or queued so far — `plain`, `comparator`,\n`iterator`, `randomizer` (240), `weighted` (241), `distributor`\n(242), `multi-band-comparator` (243) — all pick a **branch** and\nforward the producer's value to the consumer **unchanged**. The\nschema (`src/001-schema.lua`) and the dispatch picker\n(`src/012-dispatch.c`) treat the wire payload as opaque on the\nway out; routing has only ever decided *where* a value goes, never\n*what* it is.\n\nThere is no routing kind that **transforms the value** on the way\nthrough. A user who wants the producer's output remapped into a\nnew numeric range — for feeding a UI slider, an audio level, a\nheat-map cell — has to insert a dedicated call box that runs a\nLua / C function whose entire job is one arithmetic expression.\nThat's a lot of box for one knob.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA new routing kind, **`nonlinearity`** (working name; \"squash\"\nis the alternative — see open questions), maps each numeric value\nthat flows through the box into a bounded output range via a\nchosen unary function (default: logistic sigmoid). The input is\nnormalised against either:\n\n- **`auto`** — the running min and max observed on this wire\n  during the current run, OR\n- **`fixed`** — two user-supplied numeric bounds (`min`, `max`).\n\nAfter normalisation the value lands in `[0, 1]` (or `[-1, 1]` for\ntanh — see open questions), the chosen non-linearity is applied,\nand the result is forwarded on the box's single output port. The\nrouting kind has exactly one output — fan-out happens the same\nway every other single-output box's fan-out happens (multiple\nwires leaving one port).\n\n### Schema\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\":     \"nonlinearity\",\n  \"shape\":    \"sigmoid\",        // or \"tanh\" / \"linear\" / \"softsign\"\n  \"mode\":     \"auto\",           // or \"fixed\"\n  \"min\":      0,                // present only when mode == \"fixed\"\n  \"max\":      100,              // present only when mode == \"fixed\"\n  \"out_range\":\"unit\"            // or \"signed\" — see open questions\n}\n```\n\n`mode: \"auto\"` requires no bounds — the dispatch picker maintains\na running min and max in two slot-store cells (issue 302) per\nnonlinearity box, updated atomically on each fire. `mode:\n\"fixed\"` requires both `min` and `max`; schema rejects either\nmissing or `min >= max`.\n\n### Branch picker (dispatch layer)\n\nThere is no branch to pick — the kind always emits on the single\noutput. The dispatch code path differs from the existing\nrouting kinds in that it **mutates the value** rather than\n**selecting an index**. Pseudocode:\n\n```c\ndouble x = coerce_to_number(value_in);     // hard-error path on failure\n\ndouble lo, hi;\nif (mode == AUTO) {\n    lo = slot_min_load(min_slot);\n    hi = slot_max_load(max_slot);\n    slot_min_cas_update(min_slot, x);      // best-effort widen\n    slot_max_cas_update(max_slot, x);\n} else {\n    lo = box->fixed_min;\n    hi = box->fixed_max;\n}\n\ndouble t = (hi == lo) ? 0.5 : (x - lo) / (hi - lo);   // bootstrap case\n\ndouble y;\nswitch (shape) {\n    case SIGMOID:  y = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp(-k * (t - 0.5))); break;\n    case TANH:     y = tanh(k * (t - 0.5));               break;\n    case LINEAR:   y = t;                                 break;\n    case SOFTSIGN: y = (t - 0.5) / (1.0 + fabs(t - 0.5)); break;\n}\n\nemit_number(out_port, y);\n```\n\n`k` is a steepness constant (see open questions). The bootstrap\ncase (`hi == lo`, true on the very first value seen under `auto`\nmode) maps to `t = 0.5` so the sigmoid emits 0.5 — a defensible\n\"no information yet\" value.\n\n### Coercion and the hard-error path\n\nThe kind operates on numbers only. The dispatch picker tries to\ncoerce the inbound value:\n\n- **number on the wire** — used directly.\n- **string** — parsed as a number (`strtod`). On parse failure,\n  the box raises a hard error matching the project's \"errors over\n  fallbacks\" rule. The error names the box id, the offending\n  string, and the wire it arrived on.\n- **other types** (boolean, blob, sentinel) — hard error,\n  unconditional. No silent coercion.\n\nHard errors stop the box from emitting. No \"skip on bad input\"\nfallback — that's a warning shape this project treats as an\nerror.\n\n### Inspector UI\n\nMode dropdown on the routing inspector gains a `nonlinearity`\noption (same row as the other routing kinds). When selected, the\ninspector body shows:\n\n- **Shape** dropdown: sigmoid / tanh / linear / softsign.\n- **Bounds mode** dropdown: auto / fixed.\n- **Min** and **Max** number inputs (visible only when bounds\n  mode is fixed).\n- A small **live preview** plot — the chosen shape rendered into\n  a thumbnail SVG so the user sees what they're picking. (Stretch\n  goal; not blocking the first slice.)\n\nThe box's single output port keeps the plain-routing name\n(`out`) so wires drawn before the kind was changed don't need\nrenaming.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `kind: \"nonlinearity\"`; validate\n   `shape`, `mode`, the `min` / `max` pair when `mode == fixed`,\n   and the `out_range` choice.\n2. `src/302-wire-value-slot-store.*` — add `SLOT_MIN_DOUBLE` and\n   `SLOT_MAX_DOUBLE` slot kinds with CAS-update semantics\n   (compare-and-swap loop that retries if another worker widened\n   the slot between the load and the store). Reuse if such slots\n   already exist; otherwise extend.\n3. `src/010-graph-loader.c` — read the nonlinearity routing\n   fields into the box record; allocate the two slot cells when\n   `mode == auto`.\n4. `src/012-dispatch.c` — implement the value-transform path.\n   This is the first routing kind that **writes a new value** to\n   the output wire instead of forwarding the input unchanged; the\n   dispatch code currently passes the input slot pointer through.\n   Generalise so a routing kind can supply a transformed value.\n5. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add `nonlinearity` to the mode\n   dropdown; render the shape / mode / min / max controls.\n6. `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — single output port named `out`,\n   same as plain routing.\n7. The dispatch code path differs from the existing\nrouting kinds in that it **mutates the value** rather than\n**selecting an index**. The first is more flexible, the second is less surprising.\n- **The first value seen under `auto`** has no `[min, max]` yet. I picked \"emit 0.5\" as the bootstrap; alternatives are \"emit input unchanged\" or \"suppress the emit\" (breaks the \"every fire emits one value\" contract every other routing kind upholds).\n- **Hard-error on non-numeric input** matches your preferences exactly — no silent coercion, no skip-on-bad-input fallback. `strtod` is \"good enough\" but accepts `\"3.14abc\"` as 3.14; strict parse (reject trailing junk) is the more consistent choice.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\n- Generalising the dispatch layer from \"routing picks a branch\" to \"routing may also rewrite the value\" is the architectural shift this issue introduces. If you ever want **square**, **log**, **abs**, or **quantise** as routing kinds, factor that path as a first-class concept now rather than special-casing this one kind.\n- The auto-mode running min/max is the first slot kind in the project (that I'm aware of) where CAS-update semantics are load-bearing on shared state. Per-worker bounds would be faster but produce drifting output streams — shared with atomic CAS is the right shape but worth knowing it's the precedent it sets.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\n**Which open question do you want to nail down first?** My read is the name (`nonlinearity` / `squash` / `remap`) and the bounds-mode default (`auto` vs `fixed`) are the two that have to settle before any code lands — everything else can be tuned after the first fixture runs."
      }],

{
  "uuid":"3b539f85-93be-4208-95b7-1489aa28b5e8",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T17:03:29.324Z",
  "sourceToolAssistantUUID":"006148ba-ae6d-4e2f-ac00-5a5c6b1ddc34",

  "version":"2.1.121",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "content":"1\t/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n2\t *\n3\t * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n4\t * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n5\t * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n6\t * to drive a run.\n7\t *\n8\t * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n9\t * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n10\t * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n11\t * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n12\t * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n13\t *\n14\t * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n15\t * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n16\t * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n17\t * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n18\t * one call.\n19\t *\n20\t * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n21\t * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n22\t * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n23\t * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n24\t * whether to abort or surface the error.\n25\t *\n26\t * Pipeline: directory walk, JSON parse, per-box schema validation,\n27\t * topology resolution (string refs → integer indices), non-iterator\n28\t * cycle rejection, per-edge same-language classification (issue 312),\n29\t * entry-box detection. graph_attach_runtime then allocates input\n30\t * slots sized per the feeders' declared output_capacity, resolves\n31\t * each call box's language spec, and enumerates the distinct\n32\t * languages and slot size classes the map uses.\n33\t *\n34\t * Errors out of any phase abort the load and return NULL with a\n35\t * diagnostic via *err.\n36\t */\n37\t\n38\t#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n39\t#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n40\t\n41\t#include <stddef.h>\n42\t#include <stdatomic.h>\n43\t\n44\t#ifdef __cplusplus\n45\textern \"C\" {\n46\t#endif\n47\t\n48\t/* {{{ Box kinds */\n49\ttypedef enum {\n50\t    BOX_CALL,        /* runs a function via a language spec                */\n51\t    BOX_READ,        /* value source — inline literal or file at `path`    */\n52\t    BOX_WRITE,       /* file sink — writes one input, emits \"true\" downstream */\n53\t    /* Runtime self-construction (issue 319, design-correction follow-on\n54\t     * to 319d/319e). These are language-agnostic box kinds — the same\n55\t     * shape as read/write boxes, no `lang` field. Their `do_*`\n56\t     * implementations live in the dispatch layer and call\n57\t     * runtime_create_box / runtime_connect internally.\n58\t     *\n59\t     * The per-language wrappers (langs/lua/spec.c's\n60\t     * `soramech.create_box`, langs/c/soramech.h's\n61\t     * `soramech_create_box`) remain as backwards-compatible\n62\t     * convenience entry points; the box-kind path is the new idiomatic\n63\t     * way and the only path that works uniformly across every\n64\t     * language (including Bash, which has no per-language wrapper). */\n65\t    BOX_CREATE_BOX,  /* construct a new box from a spec on the input wire  */\n66\t    BOX_CONNECT,     /* attach a wire described by a connection-entry input */\n67\t    /* Issue 248: encapsulated map. A box of this kind names a\n68\t     * sub-map directory via `ref`; at graph load the loader\n69\t     * recursively loads the sub-map's boxes, splices them into\n70\t     * the parent with id prefixes, and rewires the parent's\n71\t     * wires that reach this box to instead reach the sub-map's\n72\t     * externally-marked data / write boxes.       "content":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * Pipeline: directory walk, JSON parse, per-box schema validation,\n * topology resolution (string refs → integer indices), non-iterator\n * cycle rejection, per-edge same-language classification (issue 312),\n * entry-box detection. graph_attach_runtime then allocates input\n * slots sized per the feeders' declared output_capacity, resolves\n * each call box's language spec, and enumerates the distinct\n * languages and slot size classes the map uses.\n *\n * Errors out of any phase abort the load and return NULL with a\n * diagnostic via *err.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,        /* runs a function via a language spec                */\n    BOX_READ,        /* value source — inline literal or file at `path`    */\n    BOX_WRITE,       /* file sink — writes one input, emits \"true\" downstream */\n    /* Runtime self-construction (issue 319, design-correction follow-on\n     * to 319d/319e). These are language-agnostic box kinds — the same\n     * shape as read/write boxes, no `lang` field. Their `do_*`\n     * implementations live in the dispatch layer and call\n     * runtime_create_box / runtime_connect internally.\n     *\n     * The per-language wrappers (langs/lua/spec.c's\n     * `soramech.create_box`, langs/c/soramech.h's\n     * `soramech_create_box`) remain as backwards-compatible\n     * convenience entry points; the box-kind path is the new idiomatic\n     * way and the only path that works uniformly across every\n     * language (including Bash, which has no per-language wrapper). */\n    BOX_CREATE_BOX,  /* construct a new box from a spec on the input wire  */\n    BOX_CONNECT,     /* attach a wire described by a connection-entry input */\n    /* Issue 248: encapsulated map. A box of this kind names a\n     * sub-map directory via `ref`; at graph load the loader\n     * recursively loads the sub-map's boxes, splices them into\n     * the parent with id prefixes, and rewires the parent's\n     * wires that reach this box to instead reach the sub-map's\n     * externally-marked data / write boxes. After inlining the\n     * box itself becomes inert — it never dispatches. */\n    BOX_MAP,\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* Weighted routing: arena-owned double array of n_outputs\n     * entries. Normalised at runtime. NULL for other kinds. */\n    const double  *weights;\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n    /* Per-port custom translation shim (issue 246). When non-NULL,\n     * names a file relative to the map dir that contains a\n     * user-written shim. The shim runs at the start of the\n     * consumer's task and replaces the default decode for THIS\n     * port only — other ports keep the default path. The shim's\n     * language is implied by the box's `lang` field; the file is\n     * compiled / loaded by the appropriate spec's machinery. */\n    const char *custom_translation;\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;     /* destination port name                   */\n    const char *from_branch;  /* NULL for plain output; else branch name */\n    int         to_box_idx;   /* resolved index into graph->boxes        */\n    int         to_input_idx; /* resolved index into target's inputs[]   */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ External binding (issue 248)\n *\n * A `data` box marked externally-supplied OR a `write` box marked\n * externally-consumed carries one of these. Lua / Bash boxes leave these at NULL / 0. All\n     * point into the graph's arena; no separate ownership. */\n    const char    *cflags;        /* extra flags appended to `cc`   */\n    int            n_link_libs;\n    const char   **link_libs;     /* each becomes `-l<name>`        */\n    int            n_headers;\n    const char   **headers;       /* `#include`d by generated wrappers */\n\n    /* Read boxes */\n    const char    *path;          /* file path (read only; ignored if value set) */\n    const char    *value;         /* inline literal; if set, read emits this directly */\n\n    /* Issue 248 — externally-supplied / externally-consumed binding.\n     * Present on `data` boxes inside a sub-map that should source\n     * their value from the parent's encapsulating box's input, OR\n     * on `write` boxes whose `value` should also surface back to\n     * the parent. EXTERNAL_NONE means \"not bound to the parent.\"\n     * The loader's encapsulation pass reads this to rewire wires;\n     * the dispatch never looks at it (the rewiring happens\n     * entirely at load time). */\n    external_binding_t external;\n\n    /* Read-box value cache (issue 244): the bytes a downstream consumer\n     * pulls when it needs this read box's value. Populated at graph\n     * load — inline `value` is strdup'd; file `path` is read and the\n     * file's bytes are owned here. Always present on BOX_READ; NULL on\n     * call / write boxes. Freed by graph_destroy. */\n    char          *cached_value;\n    int            cached_size;\n\n    /* Common */\n    int            n_inputs;\n    input_decl_t  *inputs;\n    /* Connections grow at runtime via runtime_connect (issue 319d).\n     * Writers allocate a new array, copy + append, atomic-store the\n     * new connections pointer, then atomic-store the new count;\n     * old arrays are parked on the graph's stale list and freed at\n     * graph_destroy. Drives the consumer's\n     * decoder choice on single-ring slots and seeds the\n     * `input_native[i]` flag that the spec's invoke consults.\n     *\n     * One bit per outgoing connection (not per output port — a\n     * single output may fan to consumers of different languages):\n     * true iff the consumer on the other end of that connection\n     * shares this box's language. When set, the producer pushes\n     * native bytes to the consumer slot's `ring_native`; when\n     * cleared, the producer calls `native_to_json` first and\n     * pushes JSON to `ring_json`. */\n    int           *input_edge_native;   /* n_inputs entries, or NULL              */\n    int           *output_edge_native;  /* n_connections entries, or NULL         */\n\n    /* 244 per-port read-box predecessor lists.\n     *\n     * A consumer's input port may be fed by one or more BOX_READ\n     * value sources. Under the pull-on-demand model these don't push\n     * at startup; instead, when the consumer fires and finds the\n     * slot empty, the dispatch layer pulls the next read box's\n     * cached value into the input buffer directly. With more than\n     * one predecessor on the same port the dispatch rotates via the\n     * counter slot (atomic increment, mod count).\n     *\n     * Allocated by graph_load: n_inputs entries each; entries with\n     * zero read predecessors hold NULL / 0 / -1. Returns NULL on any\n * failure and sets *err to a malloc'd \"<file>:<line>: <message>\"\n * diagnostic. The pool's spec init can use this\n * to skip workers for specs the map doesn't actually use. */\nint          graph_n_languages (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_language    (const graph_t *g, int i);\n\n/* Entry-box set: indices into graph->boxes of boxes the pool runner\n * submits as initial tasks. A box qualifies when it is BOX_CALL or\n * BOX_WRITE AND every non-optional input is fed only by BOX_READ\n * value sources (or has zero inputs). Filled in by graph_load. */\nint          graph_n_entry_boxes(const graph_t *g);\nint          graph_entry_box    (const graph_t *g, int i);\n\n/* Distinct input-slot cell sizes the graph uses. Filled in by\n * graph_attach_runtime after the per-port slot widths are picked.\n * The slot store can use this to pre-populate free lists. */\nint          graph_n_size_classes(const graph_t *g);\nint          graph_size_class    (const graph_t *g, int i);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime mutation primitives (issue 319d)\n *\n * graph_add_box appends a pre-built box record to the graph's\n * index. The caller owns the box record's construction — fills in\n * id / kind / lang / ref / fn / inputs / etc. — and hands the\n * malloc'd `box` pointer to this function. After the call the box\n * is owned by the graph; graph_destroy will free it. Returns the\n * new box's index (>= 0) or -1 on allocation failure.\n *\n * box_add_connection appends a connection entry to the given box's\n * `connections` array via atomic copy-and-publish: a new array is\n * allocated at current_n+1 entries, the old entries are copied in,\n * the new entry is appended, and the new array pointer is published\n * before the new count. The old array is parked on the graph's\n * stale-list and freed at graph_destroy. Concurrent dispatch reads\n * of the producer's connections see either the pre-append snapshot\n * or the post-append snapshot, never a half-published state.\n *\n * Single-spawn box invariant: the dispatch never reads a producer's\n * connections concurrently from two workers (single-spawn CAS guard\n * in dispatch). The common case for box_add_connection is a spec\n * calling `connect()` from inside its own invoke; the producer\n * isn't firing on any other worker at that moment.\n *\n * Returns 0 on success, -1 on allocation failure. */\nint graph_add_box       (graph_t *g, box_t *box);\nint box_add_connection  (graph_t *g, box_t *b, connection_t conn);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime attach\n *\n * Allocates one input slot per input port for every box and resolves\n * each call box's language spec from the registry. The dispatch reads these per-cell to\n     * pick the producer's push ring (native vs JSON) and to set\n     * the consumer's `input_native[i]` flag at read time. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = g->boxes[i];\n        b->input_edge_native  = NULL;\n        b->output_edge_native = NULL;\n        if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) continue;\n\n        /* Allocate per-port input bits and per-connection output\n         * bits. malloc rather than calloc — we fill every entry\n         * explicitly below. */\n        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n            b->input_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->input_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) b->input_edge_native[j] = 0;\n        }\n        if (b->n_connections > 0) {\n            b->output_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_connections * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->output_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) b->output_edge_native[j] = 0;\n        }\n\n        /* Outgoing edges: for each connection, the consumer's lang\n         * is native iff it's also a call box in this box's\n         * language. Read / write consumers are not native\n         * (they don't carry a language). */\n        int all_outs_native = 1;\n        for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) {\n            int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n            if (dst < 0) { all_outs_native = 0; continue; }\n            const box_t *c = g->boxes[dst];\n            int native = (c->kind == BOX_CALL && c->lang\n                          && strcmp(c->lang, b->lang) == 0);\n            b->output_edge_native[j] = native;\n            if (!native) all_outs_native = 0;\n        }\n\n        (void)all_outs_native;   /* slice 5 of 312 removed the per-box bit */\n\n        /* Incoming edges: for each input port the port is native iff\n         * it has at least one feeder AND every feeder is a call box\n         * sharing this box's language. i < sz; i++) {\n                    json_node_t *e = json_array_at(hd_n, i);\n                    if (!e || json_kind(e) != JSON_STRING) {\n                        free(arr);\n                        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: headers[%d] is not a string\",\n                                       box->id, i);\n                        return -1;\n                    }\n                    arr[i] = json_string_value(e);\n                }\n                box->headers   = arr;\n                box->n_headers = sz;\n            }\n        }\n    } else if (box->kind == BOX_READ) {\n        /* read accepts EITHER an inline `value` literal OR a `path`\n         * field. value takes precedence at run time (the canvas\n         * hides the path input port when value is set, per issue\n         * 229). BOX_READ never runs\n         * as a task (it's pull-on-demand per issue 244). */\n        if (b->kind != BOX_CALL && b->kind != BOX_WRITE &&\n            b->kind != BOX_CREATE_BOX && b->kind != BOX_CONNECT) continue;\n\n        int qualifies = 1;\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            if (b->inputs[port].optional) continue;\n            input_feeders_t f = scan_input_feeders(g, i, port, NULL);\n            if (f.n_non_read > 0) { qualifies = 0; break; }\n        }\n        if (qualifies) ids[count++] = i;\n    }\n    g->n_entry_boxes = count;\n    g->entry_box_ids = (count > 0) ? ids : (free(ids), NULL);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ resolve_topology() — phase 4 (partial: endpoints only) */\n/* Walks every outgoing connection on every box. Cycle detection lands in a\n * later iteration. */\nstatic int resolve_topology(graph_t *g, char **err)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *src = g->boxes[i];\n        for (int j = 0; j < src->n_connections; j++) {\n            connection_t *c = &src->connections[j];\n            c->to_box_idx   = -1;\n            c->to_input_idx = -1;\n\n            int found_box = -1;\n            for (int k = 0; k < g->n_boxes; k++) {\n                if (strcmp(g->boxes[k]->id, c->to_box) == 0) { found_box = k; break; }\n            }\n            if (found_box < 0) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s' has a connection to nonexistent box '%s'\",\n                               src->id, c->to_box);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            c->to_box_idx = found_box;\n\n            const box_t *dst = g->boxes[found_box];\n            int found_in = -1;\n            for (int k = 0; k < dst->n_inputs; k++) {\n                if (strcmp(dst->inputs[k].name, c->to_input) == 0) {\n                    found_in = k; break;\n                }\n            }\n            if (found_in < 0) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s' has a connection to box '%s' on \"\n                               \"nonexistent input '%s'\",\n                               src->id, dst->id, c->to_input);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            c->to_input_idx = found_in;\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ track_owned_str() — remember a heap string to free at destroy */\nstatic int track_owned_str(graph_t *g, char *s)\n{\n    struct owned_str *o = malloc(sizeof *o);\n    if (!o) return -1;\n    o->str  = s;\n    o->next = g->owned_strs;",
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.c"
    }

No literal, no optional, no custom shim;\n * an output port is just a labelled wire endpoint on the encap\n * box. Absent or empty array means the encap exposes no outputs,\n * which is legal (a sub-map that's purely side-effecting from the\n * parent's perspective). */\nstatic int parse_outputs(json_node_t *node, box_t *box,\n                         const char *box_id, char **err)\n{\n    if (!node) {\n        box->n_outputs = 0;\n        box->outputs   = NULL;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (json_kind(node) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': 'outputs' is not an array\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int n = json_array_size(node);\n    box->n_outputs = n;\n    if (n == 0) { box->outputs = NULL; return 0; }\n\n    box->outputs = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(input_decl_t));\n    if (!box->outputs) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        json_node_t *item = json_array_at(node, i);\n        if (!item || json_kind(item) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': output port %d is not an object\",\n                           box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        json_node_t *name_n = json_object_get(item, \"name\");\n        if (!name_n || json_kind(name_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': output port %d missing 'name'\",\n                           box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->outputs[i].name = json_string_value(name_n);\n        json_node_t *type_n = json_object_get(item, \"type\");\n        box->outputs[i].type = (type_n && json_kind(type_n) == JSON_STRING)\n                                 ? json_string_value(type_n) : \"string\";\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_connections() — outgoing connection array */",

    "oldString":"/* {{{ parse_connections() — outgoing connection array */",
    "newString":"/* {{{ parse_outputs() — output port array, issue 248 BOX_MAP only\n *\n * Mirrors parse_inputs but with the smaller field set output ports\n * carry — name and type. No literal, no optional, no custom shim;\n * an output port is just a labelled wire endpoint on the encap\n * box. Absent or empty array means the encap exposes no outputs,\n * which is legal (a sub-map that's purely side-effecting from the\n * parent's perspective). */\nstatic int parse_outputs(json_node_t *node, box_t *box,\n                         const char *box_id, char **err)\n{\n    if (!node) {\n        box->n_outputs = 0;\n        box->outputs   = NULL;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (json_kind(node) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': 'outputs' is not an array\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int n = json_array_size(node);\n    box->n_outputs = n;\n    if (n == 0) { box->outputs = NULL; return 0; }\n\n    box->outputs = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(input_decl_t));\n    if (!box->outputs) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        json_node_t *item = json_array_at(node, i);\n        if (!item || json_kind(item) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': output port %d is not an object\",\n                           box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        json_node_t *name_n = json_object_get(item, \"name\");\n        if (!name_n || json_kind(name_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': output port %d missing 'name'\",\n                           box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->outputs[i].name = json_string_value(name_n);\n        json_node_t *type_n = json_object_get(item, \"type\");\n        box->outputs[i].type = (type_n && json_kind(type_n) == JSON_STRING)\n                                 ? json_string_value(type_n) : \"string\";\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_connections() — outgoing connection array */",
    "userModified":false,

    "oldString":"    /* Orphan the encap box. Its outgoing connections (if any) were\n     * the output-side wiring path which this slice doesn't implement\n     * yet; dropping them means any wires the user drew from encap's\n     * output ports won't fire. The box itself stays in the index\n     * (so its slot id remains valid for any unfixed references) but\n     * becomes inert — BOX_MAP has a no-op dispatch case. */\n    int n_old_out = atomic_load_explicit(&encap->n_connections,\n                                         memory_order_relaxed);\n    connection_t *old_out =\n        atomic_load_explicit(&encap->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n    (void)n_old_out;\n    if (old_out) {\n        free(old_out);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&encap->connections, NULL,\n                              memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&encap->n_connections, 0,\n                              memory_order_release);\n    }",
    "newString":"    /* OUTPUT-side rewiring. Walk every wire the parent drew leaving\n     * the encap box; each one's from_branch names an output port on\n     * the encap, which maps to an externally-consumed write box\n     * inside the sub-map. Splice the wire onto that write box's\n     * connections array so that when the write box fires, its value\n     * surfaces to whichever parent consumers the user wired.\n     *\n     * The wires are originally on the encap's own connections array\n     * (the encap is the producer). After the splice they live on the\n     * matching write box's connections array; the encap's array is\n     * cleared. */\n    int n_encap_out = atomic_load_explicit(&encap->n_connections,\n                                           memory_order_relaxed);\n    connection_t *encap_out =\n        atomic_load_explicit(&encap->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n    for (int k = 0; k < n_encap_out; k++) {\n        connection_t *c = &encap_out[k];\n        int port_idx = find_output_port_index(encap, c->from_branch);\n        if (port_idx < 0) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"encap '%s': outgoing wire to '%s.%s' references \"\n                           \"unknown output port '%s'\",\n                           encap->id, c->to_box, c->to_input,\n                           c->from_branch ? c->from_branch : \"(default)\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box_t *W = find_ext_consumed_for_port(sub_boxes, sub_n,\n                                              encap, port_idx);\n        if (!W) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"encap '%s': output port '%s' has no matching \"\n                           \"externally-consumed write box in sub-map\",\n                           encap->id, encap->outputs[port_idx].name);\n            return -1;\n        }\n\n        /* The find returns a sub_boxes[] pointer, but the sub-boxes\n         * were just appended to g->boxes — same record, same heap\n         * address. Append the encap wire to the write box's\n         * connections via copy-and-grow. */\n        int w_n = atomic_load_explicit(&W->n_connections,\n                                       memory_order_relaxed);\n        connection_t *w_old =\n            atomic_load_explicit(&W->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n        connection_t *w_new = calloc((size_t)(w_n + 1), sizeof(connection_t));\n        if (!w_new) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (w_n > 0) memcpy(w_new, w_old, (size_t)w_n * sizeof(connection_t));\n        w_new[w_n].to_box       = c->to_box;\n        w_new[w_n].to_input     = c->to_input;\n        w_new[w_n].from_branch  = NULL;       /* write boxes have one output */\n        w_new[w_n].to_box_idx   = -1;\n        w_new[w_n].to_input_idx = -1;\n        if (w_old) free(w_old);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&W->connections, w_new, memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&W->n_connections, w_n + 1,\n                              memory_order_release);\n    }\n    if (encap_out) {\n        free(encap_out);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&encap->connections, NULL,\n                              memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&encap->n_connections, 0,\n                              memory_order_release);\n    }",

    "content":[{
        "name":"Edit",
        "input":{
          "old_string":"    /* Orphan the encap box. Its outgoing connections (if any) were\n     * the output-side wiring path which this slice doesn't implement\n     * yet; dropping them means any wires the user drew from encap's\n     * output ports won't fire. The box itself stays in the index\n     * (so its slot id remains valid for any unfixed references) but\n     * becomes inert — BOX_MAP has a no-op dispatch case. */\n    int n_old_out = atomic_load_explicit(&encap->n_connections,\n                                         memory_order_relaxed);\n    connection_t *old_out =\n        atomic_load_explicit(&encap->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n    (void)n_old_out;\n    if (old_out) {\n        free(old_out);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&encap->connections, NULL,\n                              memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&encap->n_connections, 0,\n                              memory_order_release);\n    }",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"    /* OUTPUT-side rewiring. Walk every wire the parent drew leaving\n     * the encap box; each one's from_branch names an output port on\n     * the encap, which maps to an externally-consumed write box\n     * inside the sub-map. Splice the wire onto that write box's\n     * connections array so that when the write box fires, its value\n     * surfaces to whichever parent consumers the user wired.\n     *\n     * The wires are originally on the encap's own connections array\n     * (the encap is the producer). After the splice they live on the\n     * matching write box's connections array; the encap's array is\n     * cleared. */\n    int n_encap_out = atomic_load_explicit(&encap->n_connections,\n                                           memory_order_relaxed);\n    connection_t *encap_out =\n        atomic_load_explicit(&encap->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n    for (int k = 0; k < n_encap_out; k++) {\n        connection_t *c = &encap_out[k];\n        int port_idx = find_output_port_index(encap, c->from_branch);\n        if (port_idx < 0) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"encap '%s': outgoing wire to '%s.%s' references \"\n                           \"unknown output port '%s'\",\n                           encap->id, c->to_box, c->to_input,\n                           c->from_branch ? c->from_branch : \"(default)\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box_t *W = find_ext_consumed_for_port(sub_boxes, sub_n,\n                                              encap, port_idx);\n        if (!W) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"encap '%s': output port '%s' has no matching \"\n                           \"externally-consumed write box in sub-map\",\n                           encap->id, encap->outputs[port_idx].name);\n            return -1;\n        }\n\n        /* The find returns a sub_boxes[] pointer, but the sub-boxes\n         * were just appended to g->boxes — same record, same heap\n         * address. Append the encap wire to the write box's\n         * connections via copy-and-grow. */\n        int w_n = atomic_load_explicit(&W->n_connections,\n                                       memory_order_relaxed);\n        connection_t *w_old =\n            atomic_load_explicit(&W->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n        connection_t *w_new = calloc((size_t)(w_n + 1), sizeof(connection_t));\n        if (!w_new) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (w_n > 0) memcpy(w_new, w_old, (size_t)w_n * sizeof(connection_t));\n        w_new[w_n].to_box       = c->to_box;\n        w_new[w_n].to_input     = c->to_input;\n        w_new[w_n].from_branch  = NULL;       /* write boxes have one output */\n        w_new[w_n].to_box_idx   = -1;\n        w_new[w_n].to_input_idx = -1;\n        if (w_old) free(w_old);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&W->connections, w_new, memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&W->n_connections, w_n + 1,\n                              memory_order_release);\n    }\n    if (encap_out) {\n        free(encap_out);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&encap->connections, NULL,\n                              memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&encap->n_connections, 0,\n                              memory_order_release);\n    }",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.c"
        },

    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n    # the same worker).\n    local workers_env=\"\"\n    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n    fi\n    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    else\n        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    fi\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]];
