      "content":"# 315 — Reference-counted compiled-map artifacts\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` from issue 309 is destructive at the\ntop:\n\n```bash\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" ...\n```\n\nWhatever lived in `<map>/compiled/` before the rebuild is gone. If\nanother process — a long-running runner, a different shell, a\nsibling tool that opened the artifact yesterday — had pinned to\nthat exact compiled layout (a particular `pool-runner` binary, a\nparticular `spec.so` ABI, a particular set of pre-compiled C\nboxes), the rebuild yanks the rug. The holder either crashes,\nsilently retains stale `dlopen` handles, or starts reading new\nfiles mid-flight.\n\nThis is fine in single-user development. It stops being fine the\nmoment a SoraMech artifact is the kind of thing other programs\nhold onto across time.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA compiled artifact carries its own reference count. Other\nprograms that depend on a particular build of a map are expected\nto *acquire* a reference on startup and *release* it on shutdown.\nWhen `soramech-compile` is asked to rebuild a map that has any\nlive references, it does NOT clobber the existing directory.\nInstead it builds a sibling directory next door, leaving the\nreferenced one untouched until its holders are done with it.\n\nThe reference count is **expected to be unreliable**. A crashing\nholder doesn't get the chance to release; an SSH session that\ndrops doesn't either. The design accepts that staleness is the\ncommon case, not the exception — every reference entry carries\nenough metadata to be independently validated and (eventually)\nreaped. The reference count is a hint and a courtesy, not a\nguarantee.\n\nThis is conceptually a copy-on-write filesystem for compiled\nartifacts: writes (rebuilds) fork the universe when readers\nexist; readers can keep reading the version they pinned to;\ngenerations get garbage-collected when nothing observable still\npoints at them.\n\n## Concept\n\nA compiled directory contains a `.refs` file (hidden, dot-prefixed\nso it doesn't clutter directory listings). It's append-only by\ndesign — concurrent acquires never need to take a lock; concurrent\nreleases write a separate marker without rewriting the file.\n\nEach reference has three parts:\n\n1. **A date.** When the reference was acquired. Lets a janitor\n   prune references older than some threshold even if their back\n   pointer can't be validated.\n2. **A back-pointer.** The identity of the holder — enough\n   information that an outside observer can ask \"is this holder\n   still alive, and does it still want this reference?\" without\n   trusting the count alone. Concrete candidates:\n   - process PID + start time (PID alone is not enough; PIDs\n     recycle)\n   - a path to a marker file the holder maintains (presence of\n     the marker = the holder is still live and aware of the\n     ref)\n   - some combination (PID + a marker path)\n3. **An opaque ref id.** A short string the holder can use later\n   to identify *its* reference when it wants to release, so it\n   doesn't accidentally release someone else's.\n\nA release writes an entry referencing the original acquire id.\nNet live refs = acquires whose id isn't in the release set.\n\n## Reference file format\n\nA line-oriented log. Each line is one of two record types:\n\n```\nacquire <id> <iso8601-date> <pid> <pid-start-time-ticks> <marker-path>\nrelease <id> <iso8601-date>\n```\n\nAppend-only. Holders open with `O_APPEND` and write a single line\nper operation. Atomic on POSIX as long as the line fits in\n`PIPE_BUF` (4 KB on Linux) — well within budget for these short\nrecords.\n\nReading: tail through the file, build a set of acquire ids,\nsubtract release ids; remaining ids are nominally live. Then\nvalidate each survivor's back pointer.\n\nA `.refs.lock` file is used only for compaction (rewriting the\nlog to drop matched acquire/release pairs) and for the\nfork-to-sibling decision during compile. Steady-state reads /\nwrites don't lock.\n\n## Acquire / release API\n\nA small helper utility, probably a shell script for portability\nsince holders are written in many languages:\n\n```\nscripts/soramech-ref.sh acquire <compiled-dir> [--id <id>] [--marker <path>]\nscripts/soramech-ref.sh release <compiled-dir> --id <id>\nscripts/soramech-ref.sh list    <compiled-dir>          # JSON, including staleness verdicts\nscripts/soramech-ref.sh reap    <compiled-dir>          # compact + drop dead refs\n```\n\n`acquire` prints the assigned id to stdout; the holder is\nresponsible for plumbing it to wherever it'll need to call\nrelease. If no `--id` was supplied, the script generates one\n(timestamp + random suffix).\n\n`list` walks the log and prints a JSON array of `{id, date,\nholder, valid}` entries. Validation reads the back pointer's\nliveness signal (PID exists & start-time matches, or marker file\nexists).\n\n`reap` is destructive — it rewrites the log to remove entries\nwhose holders failed validation. Run periodically; never\nautomatically as part of compile (compile must not destroy state\nits caller might care about).\n\n## Compile-time fork logic\n\n`soramech-compile.sh` consults `<map>/compiled/.refs` (and any\nsibling generation directories' `.refs` files) before deciding\nwhere to write:\n\n1. If `<map>/compiled/` doesn't exist → build there, fresh.\n2. If it exists but has zero live references → build there, after\n   `rm -rf`. Same destructive behavior as today.\n3. If it exists with one or more live references → pick a sibling\n   directory name (see below) and build there. The original\n   `compiled/` stays intact.\n\nAfter a fork-build, the caller has a new directory; `manifest.json`\nin the new directory records the fork relationship (`forked_from`\nfield pointing at the previous generation's path).\n\n### Sibling directory naming\n\nTwo reasonable schemes; pick whichever the implementer prefers:\n\n- **Generation index:** `compiled.0`, `compiled.1`, `compiled.2`...\n  Always pick `compiled.N` where N is one more than the highest\n  existing generation. Easy to grep for; index order = build\n  order.\n- **Timestamp suffix:** `compiled.2026-05-19T2347` (ISO 8601\n  compact). Order-preserving lexicographically; the name itself\n  tells the operator when it was built.\n\nWhichever wins, the script should also leave a `compiled` symlink\npointing at the newest generation, so callers who want \"the\nlatest\" don't have to enumerate.\n\n## Stale reference handling\n\nA reference is stale if any of the following hold:\n\n- The PID no longer exists on the system.\n- The PID exists but its start time (`/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22)\n  doesn't match the recorded value — different process, recycled\n  PID.\n- The marker file path was supplied at acquire and is now\n  missing.\n\nStale refs are *tolerated*: compile-time fork still triggers if\nANY ref exists, stale or otherwise — the caller can run\n`soramech-ref.sh reap` first if they want to consolidate. The\nphilosophy is: the artifact directory belongs to its readers\nuntil proven otherwise, and the cost of an extra build dir is\ntrivial compared to the cost of a use-after-rebuild crash.\n\n## Gitignore considerations\n\nEvery generation (`compiled/`, `compiled.0/`, `compiled.1/`,\n`compiled.2026-05-19T2347/`, the `compiled` symlink) is a derived\nartifact and should never be tracked. The existing\n`.gitignore` line `tests/maps/*/compiled/` covers the canonical\nname; add a sibling pattern to cover generations:\n\n```\ntests/maps/*/compiled/\ntests/maps/*/compiled.*/\n```\n\nThe `.refs` file itself lives *inside* the compiled directory,\nso it inherits the same gitignore.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Pick the back-pointer format. Recommend PID + start time +\n   optional marker path. Document the choice with a comment at\n   the top of the ref helper.\n2. Write `scripts/soramech-ref.sh` with `acquire`, `release`,\n   `list`, `reap`. Append-only writes for the first two, log\n   rewrite under `.refs.lock` for the last.\n3. Add a small `tests/315-refs-test.sh` that exercises:\n   acquire → list (1 entry, valid) → release → list (0 valid) →\n   acquire → kill the holder process → list (1 entry, stale) →\n   reap → list (0).\n4. Teach `soramech-compile.sh` to read `.refs` and pick the\n   target directory. Implement the sibling-naming scheme.\n   `compiled` becomes a symlink to the newest generation.\n5. Add a `forked_from` field to `manifest.json` when forking.\n6. Update `.gitignore` for the new generation pattern.\n7. Integration check in `scripts/run-tests.sh`: compile the\n   pipeline fixture twice — second time with a live `acquire` —\n   assert a sibling generation was created and the original\n   pinned generation still runs unchanged.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should the runner (`soramech-pool`) itself acquire a reference\n  when it opens a compiled directory? On the one hand, yes —\n  it's the canonical case the system protects against. On the\n  other, soramech-pool runs are usually short-lived and the\n  acquire/release overhead per run is unwelcome. Possible\n  compromise: only acquire if pool runs longer than N seconds.\n- How does a fork chain end? If `compiled.5` is built while\n  `compiled.4` had live refs but `compiled.4`'s refs are now all\n  stale (caller never released, then died), do we ever prune\n  `compiled.4`? Probably yes, via `soramech-ref.sh reap-all\n  <map>` which walks every generation and drops the ones whose\n  refs all validate as dead.\n- Is the `.refs` log itself something that should be versioned\n  (`.refs.v1`)? If we ever change the line format, in-flight\n  holders won't know how to read it. Versioning the filename\n  avoids the problem.\n- Does the editor (`maps/<x>/` user-facing) want the same\n  mechanism? Probably yes eventually, but out of scope for this\n  issue — start with `compiled/` artifacts only.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` — issue 309's compile pipeline,\n  modified here to fork on live references\n- `scripts/soramech-ref.sh` — new helper for acquire / release /\n  list / reap\n- `tests/315-refs-test.sh` — new\n- `.gitignore` — extended pattern for generation directories\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` — new integration check\n- `issues/309-build-system.md` — parent issue; references this\n  one's fork behavior\n\n## Notes (philosophy)\n\nThe unreliability is a feature, not a bug. A reliable reference\ncount would require a kernel-level mechanism (file locks held\nfor the lifetime of the holder), and that's a tower of\noperational complexity for marginal value. By accepting that\nholders sometimes lie and sometimes vanish, we get a system\nthat's robust to crashes, network drops, and SIGKILL — at the\ncost of needing a \"reap\" pass to catch up with reality\noccasionally. The back pointer is what makes that catch-up\npossible: it's the bridge between what the log claims and what\nthe world actually shows.\n\nA reference is a wish, not a contract. The compile pipeline\nhonors wishes by default and only stops honoring them when\nnothing in the world supports the wish anymore. That's how\nrespectful software treats its peers.\n",

Here's the underlying mechanism:\n\nA sigmoid acts as a **soft decision boundary**. Values near the midpoint say \"I have no opinion.\" Values far from the midpoint say \"I'm confident in this direction.\" The shape captures the difference between *uncertainty* and *commitment* in a single function — and it does it smoothly so the gradient is continuous (which matters when you compose many of them).\n\nWhen you **multiply two midpoint-0 outputs together**, you get a behavior that's structurally identical to **soft AND**:\n- `0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81` (both strong positive → strong positive)\n- `0.9 × -0.9 = -0.81` (disagreement → strong negative)\n- `0.1 × 0.9 = 0.09` (one uncertain → uncertain)\n- `0.05 × 0.05 = 0.0025` (both uncertain → very uncertain)\n\nThis is the **noise-rejection** behavior you sensed.         "content":"1\t#!/bin/bash\n2\t# scripts/soramech-compile.sh — produce a self-contained compiled map.\n3\t#\n4\t# What it does, in CEO terms: takes a SoraMech map directory, walks\n5\t# every box file to find the languages and source files it uses,\n6\t# copies everything into a `compiled/` subdirectory alongside the\n7\t# language spec.so plugins and the pool runner binary, and stamps a\n8\t# manifest. The resulting directory is portable — copy or symlink it\n9\t# anywhere on the same machine and it runs the map standalone.\n10\t#\n11\t# Layout produced under <map>/compiled/:\n12\t#   meta.json, boxes/, src/, data/  — verbatim copies from the map\n13\t#   langs/<lang>/spec.so            — copies of the language plugins\n14\t#                                     that the map actually uses\n15\t#   langs/bash/bash-server.sh       — only if bash boxes are present\n16\t#   bin/<box>.so                    — pre-compiled C boxes (informational;\n17\t#                                     the runner still lazy-compiles\n18\t#                                     from src/ but having them here\n19\t#                                     means you can verify the compile\n20\t#                                     step worked without running)\n21\t#   pool-runner                     — symlink to soramech-pool\n22\t#   manifest.json                   — summary stats\n23\t#\n24\t# Run as:\n25\t#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir>\n26\t#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir> --dir <project-root>\n27\t#\n28\t# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded ${DIR}\n29\t# path with an override argument; all paths relative to ${DIR}.\n30\t\n31\tset -u\n32\t\n33\t# {{{ defaults\n34\tDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n35\tMAP=\"\"\n36\t# }}}\n37\t\n38\t# {{{ argv parse — map first, --dir <path> optional\n39\twhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n40\t    case \"$1\" in\n41\t        --dir)\n42\t            DIR=\"$2\"\n43\t            shift 2\n44\t            ;;\n45\t        --help|-h)\n46\t            grep '^#' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n47\t            exit 0\n48\t            ;;\n49\t        *)\n50\t            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n51\t                MAP=\"$1\"\n52\t            else\n53\t                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n54\t                exit 2\n55\t            fi\n56\t            shift\n57\t            ;;\n58\t    esac\n59\tdone\n60\t\n61\tif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n62\t    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n63\t    exit 2\n64\tfi\n65\t# }}}\n66\t\n67\t# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\n68\tif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n69\t    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n70\t    exit 1\n71\tfi\n72\tMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\n73\tif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n74\t    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n75\t    exit 1\n76\tfi\n77\tif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n78\t    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n79\t    exit 1\n80\tfi\n81\tif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n82\t    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n83\t    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n84\t    exit 1\n85\tfi\n86\t\n87\tCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n88\t# }}}\n89\t\n90\t# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n91\t# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n92\t# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n93\t# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\n94\tbox_field() {\n95\t    local file=\"$1\"\n96\t    local field=\"$2\"\n97\t    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n98\t        | head -n1 \\\n99\t        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n100\t}\n101\t# }}}\n102\t\n103\t# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\n104\trm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\n105\tmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n106\t# }}}\n107\t\n108\t# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\n109\tcp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\n110\tcp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n111\t\n112\tif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n113\t    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\n114\tfi\n115\t\n116\tif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n117\t    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n118\t    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\n119\tfi\n120\t\n121\t# Issue 246 — per-port custom translation shims. Box JSONs reference\n122\t# them by relative path under translations/; the runtime resolves\n123\t# the path relative to the compiled map dir at dispatch time.\n124\tif [[ -d \"$MAP/translations\" ]]; then\n125\t    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/translations\"\n126\t    cp -r \"$MAP/translations/.\" \"$COMPILED/translations/\"\n127\tfi\n128\t\n129\t# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n130\t# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\n131\tshopt -s nullglob\n132\tfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n133\t    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\n134\tdone\n135\tshopt -u nullglob\n136\t# }}}\n137\t\n138\t# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n139\t# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\n140\tLANGS=()\n141\tfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n142\t    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n143\t    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n144\t    seen=0\n145\t    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n146\t        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n147\t    done\n148\t    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n149\t        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n150\t    fi\n151\tdone\n152\t# }}}\n153\t\n154\t# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\n155\tfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n156\t    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n157\t    if [[ ! -f \"$src_spec\" ]]; then\n158\t        echo \"soramech-compile: missing spec.so for language '$lang'\" >&2\n159\t        echo \"  expected at $src_spec — run 'make' in $DIR\" >&2\n160\t        exit 1\n161\t    fi\n162\t    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang\"\n163\t    cp \"$src_spec\" \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n164\t    # Bash spec needs its companion server script for runtime.\n165\t    if [[ \"$lang\" == \"bash\" ]] && [[ -f \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" ]]; then\n166\t        cp \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" \"$COMPILED/langs/bash/\"\n167\t    fi\n168\tdone\n169\t# }}}\n170\t\n171\t# {{{ merge_lua_sources — concatenate all Lua source files into one\n172\t# merged module (issue 313). Each per-file module is wrapped in its\n173\t# own closure so the file's `local` declarations stay file-scoped,\n174\t# and exported under the source file's basename. The Lua spec\n175\t# detects the merged file at init and loads it once per worker\n176\t# instead of per-file lazy-loading every box's ref. The original\n177\t# files stay in src/ unchanged so the existing per-file path still\n178\t# works for callers that haven't been told about the merge.\n179\tmerge_lua_sources() {\n180\t    local out=\"$COMPILED/src/__merged__.lua\"\n181\t    shopt -s nullglob\n182\t    local files=(\"$COMPILED/src\"/*.lua)\n183\t    shopt -u nullglob\n184\t    if [[ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then return; fi\n185\t\n186\t    {\n187\t        echo \"-- soramech merged Lua module (issue 313)\"\n188\t        echo \"-- Generated by soramech-compile.sh; do not hand-edit.\"\n189\t        echo \"-- Each per-file module wraps in its own closure and is\"\n190\t        echo \"-- exported under the source file's basename, so two\"\n191\t        echo \"-- files can both define a local M without colliding.\"\n192\t        echo \"\"\n193\t        echo \"local merged = {}\"\n194\t        echo \"\"\n195\t        local f base\n196\t        for f in \"${files[@]}\"; do\n197\t            base=$(basename \"$f\" .lua)\n198\t            if [[ \"$base\" == \"__merged__\" ]]; then continue; fi\n199\t            echo \"-- {{{ from $(basename \"$f\")\"\n200\t            echo \"merged[\\\"$base\\\"] = (function()\"\n201\t            cat \"$f\"\n202\t            echo \"\"\n203\t            echo \"end)()\"\n204\t            echo \"-- }}}\"\n205\t            echo \"\"\n206\t        done\n207\t        echo \"return merged\"\n208\t    } > \"$out\"\n209\t}\n210\tmerge_lua_sources\n211\t# }}}\n212\t\n213\t# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n214\t# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n215\t# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n216\t# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n217\t# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\n218\tn_c_compiled=0\n219\tn_c_failed=0\n220\tfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n221\t    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n222\t    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n223\t    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n224\t    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n225\t    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n226\t    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n227\t        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n228\t        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n229\t        continue\n230\t    fi\n231\t    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n232\t    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n233\t    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n234\t        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n235\t        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n236\t        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n237\t        continue\n238\t    fi\n239\t    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\n240\tdone\n241\t\n242\tif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n243\t    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n244\t    exit 1\n245\tfi\n246\t# }}}\n247\t\n248\t# {{{ copy the pool runner into the compiled directory\n249\t# A real copy (not a symlink) is intentional: the runner discovers\n250\t# its sibling langs/ via /proc/self/exe, which follows symlinks to\n251\t# their canonical target. A symlinked pool-runner would resolve back\n252\t# to the project tree and pick up the project's langs/ instead of\n253\t# the bundled compiled/langs/. Copying keeps the compiled artifact\n254\t# self-describing and portable.\n255\tcp \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n256\tchmod +x \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n257\t# }}}\n258\t\n259\t# {{{ write manifest.json\n260\t# Hand-rolled JSON (no jq) keeps the script self-contained. The\n261\t# fields are stable enough to grep against in tests.\n262\tn_boxes=$(ls -1 \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\n263\tn_langs=${#LANGS[@]}\n264\tlangs_json=\"\"\n265\tfirst=1\n266\tfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n267\t    if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n268\t        langs_json=\"\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n269\t        first=0\n270\t    else\n271\t        langs_json+=\",\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n272\t    fi\n273\tdone\n274\tcompiled_at=$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\n275\tmap_name=$(basename \"$MAP\")\n276\t\n277\tcat > \"$COMPILED/manifest.json\" <<EOF\n278\t{\n279\t    \"name\": \"$map_name\",\n280\t    \"compiled_at\": \"$compiled_at\",\n281\t    \"n_boxes\": $n_boxes,\n282\t    \"n_languages\": $n_langs,\n283\t    \"languages\": [$langs_json],\n284\t    \"c_boxes_precompiled\": $n_c_compiled,\n285\t    \"source_map_dir\": \"$MAP\"\n286\t}\n287\tEOF\n288\t# }}}\n289\t\n290\t# {{{ summary line\n291\techo \"compiled $map_name → $COMPILED\"\n292\techo \"  boxes:       $n_boxes\"\n293\techo \"  languages:   $n_langs (${LANGS[*]+${LANGS[*]}})\"\n294\techo \"  c precompiled: $n_c_compiled\"\n295\techo\n296\techo \"run with:\"\n297\techo \"  $COMPILED/pool-runner $COMPILED\"\n298\t# }}}\n299\t",

-d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\nif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\nbox_field() {\n    local file=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n        | head -n1 \\\n        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\ncp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\ncp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Issue 246 — per-port custom translation shims. Box JSONs reference\n# them by relative path under translations/; the runtime resolves\n# the path relative to the compiled map dir at dispatch time.\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/translations\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/translations\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/translations/.\" \"$COMPILED/translations/\"\nfi\n\n# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\nshopt -s nullglob\nfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\ndone\nshopt -u nullglob\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\nLANGS=()\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    seen=0\n    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n    done\n    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_spec\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: missing spec.so for language '$lang'\" >&2\n        echo \"  expected at $src_spec — run 'make' in $DIR\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang\"\n    cp \"$src_spec\" \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    # Bash spec needs its companion server script for runtime.\n    if [[ \"$lang\" == \"bash\" ]] && [[ -f \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" ]]; then\n        cp \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" \"$COMPILED/langs/bash/\"\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ merge_lua_sources — concatenate all Lua source files into one\n# merged module (issue 313). Each per-file module is wrapped in its\n# own closure so the file's `local` declarations stay file-scoped,\n# and exported under the source file's basename. The Lua spec\n# detects the merged file at init and loads it once per worker\n# instead of per-file lazy-loading every box's ref. The original\n# files stay in src/ unchanged so the existing per-file path still\n# works for callers that haven't been told about the merge.\nmerge_lua_sources() {\n    local out=\"$COMPILED/src/__merged__.lua\"\n    shopt -s nullglob\n    local files=(\"$COMPILED/src\"/*.lua)\n    shopt -u nullglob\n    if [[ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then return; fi\n\n    {\n        echo \"-- soramech merged Lua module (issue 313)\"\n        echo \"-- Generated by soramech-compile.sh; do not hand-edit.\"\n        echo \"-- Each per-file module wraps in its own closure and is\"\n        echo \"-- exported under the source file's basename, so two\"\n        echo \"-- files can both define a local M without colliding.\"\n        echo \"\"\n        echo \"local merged = {}\"\n        echo \"\"\n        local f base\n        for f in \"${files[@]}\"; do\n            base=$(basename \"$f\" .lua)\n            if [[ \"$base\" == \"__merged__\" ]]; then continue; fi\n            echo \"-- {{{ from $(basename \"$f\")\"\n            echo \"merged[\\\"$base\\\"] = (function()\"\n            cat \"$f\"\n            echo \"\"\n            echo \"end)()\"\n            echo \"-- }}}\"\n            echo \"\"\n        done\n        echo \"return merged\"\n    } > \"$out\"\n}\nmerge_lua_sources\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\nn_c_compiled=0\nn_c_failed=0\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\ndone\n\nif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A real copy (not a symlink) is intentional: the runner discovers\n# its sibling langs/ via /proc/self/exe, which follows symlinks to\n# their canonical target. A symlinked pool-runner would resolve back\n# to the project tree and pick up the project's langs/ instead of\n# the bundled compiled/langs/. Copying keeps the compiled artifact\n# self-describing and portable.\ncp \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\nchmod +x \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ write manifest.json\n# Hand-rolled JSON (no jq) keeps the script self-contained. The\n# fields are stable enough to grep against in tests.\nn_boxes=$(ls -1 \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\nn_langs=${#LANGS[@]}\nlangs_json=\"\"\nfirst=1\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n        langs_json=\"\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n        first=0\n    else\n        langs_json+=\",\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n    fi\ndone\ncompiled_at=$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\nmap_name=$(basename \"$MAP\")\n\ncat > \"$COMPILED/manifest.json\" <<EOF\n{\n    \"name\": \"$map_name\",\n    \"compiled_at\": \"$compiled_at\",\n    \"n_boxes\": $n_boxes,\n    \"n_languages\": $n_langs,\n    \"languages\": [$langs_json],\n    \"c_boxes_precompiled\": $n_c_compiled,\n    \"source_map_dir\": \"$MAP\"\n}\nEOF\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ summary line\necho \"compiled $map_name → $COMPILED\"\necho \"  boxes:       $n_boxes\"\necho \"  languages:   $n_langs (${LANGS[*]+${LANGS[*]}})\"\necho \"  c precompiled: $n_c_compiled\"\necho\necho \"run with:\"\necho \"  $COMPILED/pool-runner $COMPILED\"\n# }}}\n",
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/scripts/soramech-compile.sh"
    }

        "input":{
          "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/soramech-ref.sh — reference-counted compiled-artifact pins.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: gives other programs a way to say\n# \"I'm using this compiled SoraMech artifact right now, don't\n# clobber it.\" Holders acquire a reference at startup, release at\n# shutdown, and the compile pipeline (scripts/soramech-compile.sh)\n# checks the count before rebuilding — if anyone is holding,\n# rebuild lands in a sibling directory instead of overwriting.\n#\n# The mechanism is a single dot-file (`.refs`) inside the compiled\n# directory:\n#\n#   acquire <id> <iso8601-date> <pid> <pid-start-time-ticks> <marker>\n#   release <id> <iso8601-date>\n#\n# Append-only writes are atomic on POSIX as long as the line fits\n# in PIPE_BUF (4 KB on Linux); these lines are well under that.\n# So no lock is needed for steady-state acquire / release — only\n# `reap` (which rewrites the log to drop dead entries) takes a\n# lock, via .refs.lock.\n#\n# References are *expected to be unreliable*: a crashing holder\n# never gets to release. The back pointer (PID + start-time-ticks\n# + optional marker path) lets `list` and `reap` independently\n# verify whether a recorded acquire is still meaningful.\n#\n# Run as:\n#   scripts/soramech-ref.sh acquire <compiled-dir> [--id <id>] [--marker <path>]\n#   scripts/soramech-ref.sh release <compiled-dir> --id <id>\n#   scripts/soramech-ref.sh list    <compiled-dir>          # JSON\n#   scripts/soramech-ref.sh count   <compiled-dir>          # live count, integer\n#   scripts/soramech-ref.sh reap    <compiled-dir>          # compact + drop dead\n#\n# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded\n# ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths inside the\n# script are absolute against ${DIR} or against the per-call\n# compiled-dir argument.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nACTION=\"\"\nTARGET=\"\"\nID=\"\"\nMARKER=\"-\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ argv parse — action first, target second, then --flags\nif [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then\n    echo \"usage: soramech-ref.sh <acquire|release|list|count|reap> <compiled-dir> [--id <id>] [--marker <path>] [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\nACTION=\"$1\"\nTARGET=\"$2\"\nshift 2\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --id)     ID=\"$2\";     shift 2 ;;\n        --marker) MARKER=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --dir)    DIR=\"$2\";    shift 2 ;;\n        *)\n            echo \"soramech-ref: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n            exit 2\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ sanity-check the target directory\nif [[ ! -d \"$TARGET\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-ref: not a directory: $TARGET\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nTARGET=$(cd \"$TARGET\" && pwd)\nREFS_FILE=\"$TARGET/.refs\"\nLOCK_FILE=\"$TARGET/.refs.lock\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pid_starttime — read /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 (start time in jiffies)\n# stat field 2 (comm) is parenthesized and may contain spaces, so we\n# strip up to and including the closing paren before counting. After\n# the paren, field 22 overall becomes the 20th field.\npid_starttime() {\n    local pid=\"$1\"\n    if [[ ! -r \"/proc/$pid/stat\" ]]; then return 1; fi\n    local raw\n    raw=$(cat \"/proc/$pid/stat\" 2>/dev/null) || return 1\n    local after_comm=\"${raw#*) }\"\n    echo \"$after_comm\" | awk '{print $20}'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ gen_id — timestamp + random suffix, unique enough for this purpose\ngen_id() {\n    local ts\n    ts=$(date +%s)\n    local rand\n    rand=$(head -c 4 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \\n')\n    echo \"${ts}-${rand}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ is_alive — true iff the recorded back pointer still validates\n# A reference is alive when:\n#   - the PID exists, AND\n#   - the PID's current start time matches the recorded one (so we\n#     don't confuse a recycled PID for the original holder), AND\n#   - if a marker path was supplied at acquire, the marker file\n#     still exists.\n# Any failure means stale.\nis_alive() {\n    local pid=\"$1\"\n    local recorded_start=\"$2\"\n    local marker=\"$3\"\n    if [[ ! -d \"/proc/$pid\" ]]; then return 1; fi\n    local current_start\n    current_start=$(pid_starttime \"$pid\") || return 1\n    if [[ \"$current_start\" != \"$recorded_start\" ]]; then return 1; fi\n    if [[ \"$marker\" != \"-\" ]] && [[ ! -e \"$marker\" ]]; then return 1; fi\n    return 0\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ scan_refs — emit one line per live id: \"<id> <date> <pid> <start> <marker>\"\n# Walks the log once, accumulates acquires, subtracts releases, prints\n# the remaining acquire records. The id-set is in a temp file rather\n# than a bash assoc array so the script stays portable across older\n# bash versions; the log is small enough that an O(n) scan is fine.\nscan_refs() {\n    if [[ ! -f \"$REFS_FILE\" ]]; then return 0; fi\n    local tmp_acq\n    tmp_acq=$(mktemp)\n    local tmp_rel\n    tmp_rel=$(mktemp)\n    while IFS= read -r line; do\n        case \"$line\" in\n            \"acquire \"*) echo \"$line\" >> \"$tmp_acq\" ;;\n            \"release \"*)\n                local rid\n                rid=$(echo \"$line\" | awk '{print $2}')\n                echo \"$rid\" >> \"$tmp_rel\"\n                ;;\n        esac\n    done < \"$REFS_FILE\"\n    # Print only acquires whose id is not present in the release set.\n    while IFS= read -r aline; do\n        local aid\n        aid=$(echo \"$aline\" | awk '{print $2}')\n        if ! grep -qFx \"$aid\" \"$tmp_rel\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            local rest\n            rest=$(echo \"$aline\" | cut -d' ' -f2-)\n            echo \"$rest\"\n        fi\n    done < \"$tmp_acq\"\n    rm -f \"$tmp_acq\" \"$tmp_rel\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ do_acquire — append one acquire record, print the assigned id\ndo_acquire() {\n    if [[ -z \"$ID\" ]]; then\n        ID=$(gen_id)\n    fi\n    local date\n    date=$(date -Iseconds)\n    local pid=\"$$\"\n    # The script's own PID isn't useful as a back pointer — the\n    # *holder* process is whoever invoked us. Bash makes the parent\n    # PID available via PPID, which is the right anchor.\n    pid=\"$PPID\"\n    local start\n    start=$(pid_starttime \"$pid\")\n    if [[ -z \"$start\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-ref: cannot read /proc/$pid/stat (caller's start time)\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    # O_APPEND on POSIX makes the write atomic up to PIPE_BUF.\n    printf 'acquire %s %s %s %s %s\\n' \"$ID\" \"$date\" \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$MARKER\" >> \"$REFS_FILE\"\n    echo \"$ID\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ do_release — append one release record\ndo_release() {\n    if [[ -z \"$ID\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-ref: release requires --id <id>\" >&2\n        exit 2\n    fi\n    local date\n    date=$(date -Iseconds)\n    printf 'release %s %s\\n' \"$ID\" \"$date\" >> \"$REFS_FILE\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ do_list — JSON array of {id, date, pid, start_ticks, marker, valid}\ndo_list() {\n    echo \"[\"\n    local first=1\n    while IFS=' ' read -r id date pid start marker; do\n        if [[ -z \"$id\" ]]; then continue; fi\n        local valid=\"true\"\n        if ! is_alive \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$marker\"; then\n            valid=\"false\"\n        fi\n        local comma=\",\"\n        if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n            comma=\"\"\n            first=0\n        fi\n        printf '%s\\n  {\"id\":\"%s\",\"date\":\"%s\",\"pid\":%s,\"start_ticks\":%s,\"marker\":\"%s\",\"valid\":%s}' \\\n            \"$comma\" \"$id\" \"$date\" \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$marker\" \"$valid\"\n    done < <(scan_refs)\n    echo\n    echo \"]\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ do_count — number of live (un-released, validated) references\n# Used by the compile script to decide whether to fork. Prints a single\n# integer so the caller can compare without parsing JSON.\ndo_count() {\n    local n=0\n    while IFS=' ' read -r id date pid start marker; do\n        if [[ -z \"$id\" ]]; then continue; fi\n        if is_alive \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$marker\"; then\n            n=$((n + 1))\n        fi\n    done < <(scan_refs)\n    echo \"$n\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ do_reap — rewrite the log, dropping released and dead entries\n# Takes .refs.lock for the duration so a concurrent acquire / release\n# doesn't get spliced into a half-rewritten log. Uses mkdir as the\n# portable atomic test-and-set (no flock dependency).\ndo_reap() {\n    local i=0\n    while ! mkdir \"$LOCK_FILE\" 2>/dev/null; do\n        i=$((i + 1))\n        if [[ $i -gt 100 ]]; then\n            echo \"soramech-ref: could not acquire $LOCK_FILE after 100 tries\" >&2\n            exit 1\n        fi\n        sleep 0.05\n    done\n    trap 'rmdir \"$LOCK_FILE\" 2>/dev/null' EXIT\n    local tmp\n    tmp=$(mktemp)\n    while IFS=' ' read -r id date pid start marker; do\n        if [[ -z \"$id\" ]]; then continue; fi\n        if is_alive \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$marker\"; then\n            printf 'acquire %s %s %s %s %s\\n' \"$id\" \"$date\" \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$marker\" >> \"$tmp\"\n        fi\n    done < <(scan_refs)\n    if [[ -s \"$tmp\" ]]; then\n        mv \"$tmp\" \"$REFS_FILE\"\n    else\n        rm -f \"$REFS_FILE\" \"$tmp\"\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ dispatch\ncase \"$ACTION\" in\n    acquire) do_acquire ;;\n    release) do_release ;;\n    list)    do_list    ;;\n    count)   do_count   ;;\n    reap)    do_reap    ;;\n    *)\n        echo \"soramech-ref: unknown action '$ACTION'\" >&2\n        exit 2\n        ;;\nesac\n# }}}\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/scripts/soramech-ref.sh"

The id-set is in a temp file rather\n# than a bash assoc array so the script stays portable across older\n# bash versions; the log is small enough that an O(n) scan is fine.\nscan_refs() {\n    if [[ ! -f \"$REFS_FILE\" ]]; then return 0; fi\n    local tmp_acq\n    tmp_acq=$(mktemp)\n    local tmp_rel\n    tmp_rel=$(mktemp)\n    while IFS= read -r line; do\n        case \"$line\" in\n            \"acquire \"*) echo \"$line\" >> \"$tmp_acq\" ;;\n            \"release \"*)\n                local rid\n                rid=$(echo \"$line\" | awk '{print $2}')\n                echo \"$rid\" >> \"$tmp_rel\"\n                ;;\n        esac\n    done < \"$REFS_FILE\"\n    # Print only acquires whose id is not present in the release set.\n    while IFS= read -r aline; do\n        local aid\n        aid=$(echo \"$aline\" | awk '{print $2}')\n        if ! grep -qFx \"$aid\" \"$tmp_rel\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            local rest\n            rest=$(echo \"$aline\" | cut -d' ' -f2-)\n            echo \"$rest\"\n        fi\n    done < \"$tmp_acq\"\n    rm -f \"$tmp_acq\" \"$tmp_rel\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ do_acquire — append one acquire record, print the assigned id\ndo_acquire() {\n    if [[ -z \"$ID\" ]]; then\n        ID=$(gen_id)\n    fi\n    local date\n    date=$(date -Iseconds)\n    local pid=\"$$\"\n    # The script's own PID isn't useful as a back pointer — the\n    # *holder* process is whoever invoked us. Bash makes the parent\n    # PID available via PPID, which is the right anchor.\n    pid=\"$PPID\"\n    local start\n    start=$(pid_starttime \"$pid\")\n    if [[ -z \"$start\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-ref: cannot read /proc/$pid/stat (caller's start time)\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    # O_APPEND on POSIX makes the write atomic up to PIPE_BUF.\n    printf 'acquire %s %s %s %s %s\\n' \"$ID\" \"$date\" \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$MARKER\" >> \"$REFS_FILE\"\n    echo \"$ID\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ do_release — append one release record\ndo_release() {\n    if [[ -z \"$ID\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-ref: release requires --id <id>\" >&2\n        exit 2\n    fi\n    local date\n    date=$(date -Iseconds)\n    printf 'release %s %s\\n' \"$ID\" \"$date\" >> \"$REFS_FILE\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ do_list — JSON array of {id, date, pid, start_ticks, marker, valid}\ndo_list() {\n    echo \"[\"\n    local first=1\n    while IFS=' ' read -r id date pid start marker; do\n        if [[ -z \"$id\" ]]; then continue; fi\n        local valid=\"true\"\n        if ! is_alive \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$marker\"; then\n            valid=\"false\"\n        fi\n        local comma=\",\"\n        if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n            comma=\"\"\n            first=0\n        fi\n        printf '%s\\n  {\"id\":\"%s\",\"date\":\"%s\",\"pid\":%s,\"start_ticks\":%s,\"marker\":\"%s\",\"valid\":%s}' \\\n            \"$comma\" \"$id\" \"$date\" \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$marker\" \"$valid\"\n    done < <(scan_refs)\n    echo\n    echo \"]\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ do_count — number of live (un-released, validated) references\n# Used by the compile script to decide whether to fork. Prints a single\n# integer so the caller can compare without parsing JSON.\ndo_count() {\n    local n=0\n    while IFS=' ' read -r id date pid start marker; do\n        if [[ -z \"$id\" ]]; then continue; fi\n        if is_alive \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$marker\"; then\n            n=$((n + 1))\n        fi\n    done < <(scan_refs)\n    echo \"$n\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ do_reap — rewrite the log, dropping released and dead entries\n# Takes .refs.lock for the duration so a concurrent acquire / release\n# doesn't get spliced into a half-rewritten log. Uses mkdir as the\n# portable atomic test-and-set (no flock dependency).\ndo_reap() {\n    local i=0\n    while ! mkdir \"$LOCK_FILE\" 2>/dev/null; do\n        i=$((i + 1))\n        if [[ $i -gt 100 ]]; then\n            echo \"soramech-ref: could not acquire $LOCK_FILE after 100 tries\" >&2\n            exit 1\n        fi\n        sleep 0.05\n    done\n    trap 'rmdir \"$LOCK_FILE\" 2>/dev/null' EXIT\n    local tmp\n    tmp=$(mktemp)\n    while IFS=' ' read -r id date pid start marker; do\n        if [[ -z \"$id\" ]]; then continue; fi\n        if is_alive \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$marker\"; then\n            printf 'acquire %s %s %s %s %s\\n' \"$id\" \"$date\" \"$pid\" \"$start\" \"$marker\" >> \"$tmp\"\n        fi\n    done < <(scan_refs)\n    if [[ -s \"$tmp\" ]]; then\n        mv \"$tmp\" \"$REFS_FILE\"\n    else\n        rm -f \"$REFS_FILE\" \"$tmp\"\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ dispatch\ncase \"$ACTION\" in\n    acquire) do_acquire ;;\n    release) do_release ;;\n    list)    do_list    ;;\n    count)   do_count   ;;\n    reap)    do_reap    ;;\n    *)\n        echo \"soramech-ref: unknown action '$ACTION'\" >&2\n        exit 2\n        ;;\nesac\n# }}}\n",
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/scripts/soramech-ref.sh"
  },

Multiplication composes like soft AND with sign-tracking. Best for\n  decision-making agents where signals have a polarity.\n  - Midpoint at 0.5 (sigmoid-style, output [0, 1]) — for \"probability/confidence\" semantics. Multiplication composes like a probabilistic conjunction\n  (assuming independence).         "text":"No worries on the interrupt — and no, I hadn't edited 250; I only responded in chat. You're doing the design pass. Let me address your followups concisely, then resume 315.\n\n---\n\n## Quick followups on 250\n\n**Three variants by name, not by mathematician's jargon.** Yes, this is the right move — and it collapses two of your fields into one. Instead of `shape: sigmoid|tanh|linear` plus a separate `out_range: unit|signed`, just have `shape` carry an intent-named value:\n\n- `shape: \"decision\"` → tanh under the hood, midpoint 0, output `[-1, 1]`. UI tooltip: \"Soft + / − with clear neutral. Compose by multiplication when signals agree.\"\n- `shape: \"confidence\"` → sigmoid under the hood, midpoint 0.5, output `[0, 1]`. UI tooltip: \"Soft yes / no with uncertainty. Compose probabilistically.\"\n- `shape: \"calibration\"` → linear remap, no midpoint, output `[0, 1]`. UI tooltip: \"Pure range conversion, no curve. Use when you just want to rescale a sensor reading.\"\n\nThree picks, three clear meanings. The user never has to know what tanh is.\n\n**Symmetric vs asymmetric decay — your reframe is elegant and self-deciding.** Presence of a user-supplied midpoint IS the mode switch:\n- Midpoint supplied → asymmetric (the midpoint anchors; bounds drift toward it).\n- Midpoint absent → symmetric (the midpoint follows the data; both bounds drift toward each other).\n\nNo separate flag needed. The field's presence carries the meaning.\n\n**Multi-band-comparator extension (+ button, absolute/percentage rows) belongs in 243, not 250.** The \"+ button to add tiers\" is a generalization of the multi-band-comparator UI, and the synced absolute/percentage rows are a UI convenience that works against any range — comparator OR nonlinearity OR anything else with bounds. If you want, I can write an update note onto 243 sketching it. The auto-min/max-tracking primitive that the percentage row reads from is the same primitive nonlinearity uses for `auto` mode — there's a small architectural insight there about factoring \"tracked range\" as a shared capability.\n\n**Clamping as \"certainty threshold\" — yes, brilliant.** This reframes the user's `min`/`max` from \"where the curve starts to saturate\" into \"the threshold past which I'm certain.\" That maps cleanly per variant:\n- `confidence`: `input > max` → output = 1.0 (fully confident yes); `input < min` → output = 0.0 (fully confident no). Clamp away.\n- `decision`: `input > max` → output = +1.0; `input < min` → output = −1.0. Clamp away.\n- `calibration`: don't clamp (it's a remap, not a decision). Out-of-range values either extrapolate linearly or hard-error per your preference.\n\nSo clamping is a **per-variant default** rather than a separate toggle. Confidence and decision variants clamp; calibration doesn't.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\n- The \"auto-tracked range\" primitive that nonlinearity's auto mode introduces is the kind of thing worth promoting to a first-class concept eventually. The multi-band-comparator's percentage row wants it; a histogram visualization box would want it; a normalization box (if you ever build one) wants it. Right now it lives inside nonlinearity, but once two boxes want the same thing, it earns its own ticket. Watch for that.\n- Your reframe of \"clamp = certainty threshold\" is the kind of move that makes APIs feel natural. The user was probably going to clamp anyway because \"values past my limits are obvious extremes\"; by naming what they're already doing, the system gets a primitive that matches intuition without anyone having to memorize it.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\n**On 320** — I checked. The current state already accommodates everything new from this conversation (steepness `k` reconfigurable, shape variant reconfigurable, decay flag reconfigurable, all covered by the \"every reconfigurable field\" comprehensive scope). No edit needed.\n\n---\n\nResuming 315 — re-running the smoke test."

If anything is holding a reference, we build into a\n# sibling directory (`compiled.1`, `compiled.2`, …) and leave the\n# original alone.\n#\n# If the base doesn't exist → build there fresh.\n# If the base exists with zero live refs → wipe and rebuild there\n#   (same destructive shape as before — no holders, nothing to\n#   protect).\n# If the base exists with one or more live refs → pick the next\n#   `compiled.N` sibling and build there. FORKED_FROM is set so\n#   the manifest records the lineage.\npick_target_dir() {\n    if [[ ! -d \"$COMPILED_BASE\" ]]; then\n        COMPILED=\"$COMPILED_BASE\"\n        FORKED_FROM=\"\"\n        return\n    fi\n    local live=0\n    if [[ -x \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-ref.sh\" ]] && [[ -f \"$COMPILED_BASE/.refs\" ]]; then\n        live=$(\"$DIR/scripts/soramech-ref.sh\" count \"$COMPILED_BASE\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\n    fi\n    if [[ \"$live\" -eq 0 ]]; then\n        COMPILED=\"$COMPILED_BASE\"\n        FORKED_FROM=\"\"\n        rm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\n        return\n    fi\n    # Find the highest existing compiled.N and add 1. shopt nullglob\n    # so the glob expands to nothing when no siblings exist yet.\n    local highest=0\n    shopt -s nullglob\n    local sibling\n    for sibling in \"$MAP\"/compiled.*; do\n        local base\n        base=$(basename \"$sibling\")\n        local n=\"${base#compiled.}\"\n        if [[ \"$n\" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then\n            if [[ \"$n\" -gt \"$highest\" ]]; then highest=$n; fi\n        fi\n    done\n    shopt -u nullglob\n    local next=$((highest + 1))\n    COMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled.$next\"\n    FORKED_FROM=\"$COMPILED_BASE\"\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $live live reference(s) on $COMPILED_BASE — forking to $COMPILED\"\n}\npick_target_dir\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file",

    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/soramech-compile.sh — produce a self-contained compiled map.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: takes a SoraMech map directory, walks\n# every box file to find the languages and source files it uses,\n# copies everything into a `compiled/` subdirectory alongside the\n# language spec.so plugins and the pool runner binary, and stamps a\n# manifest. The resulting directory is portable — copy or symlink it\n# anywhere on the same machine and it runs the map standalone.\n#\n# Layout produced under <map>/compiled/:\n#   meta.json, boxes/, src/, data/  — verbatim copies from the map\n#   langs/<lang>/spec.so            — copies of the language plugins\n#                                     that the map actually uses\n#   langs/bash/bash-server.sh       — only if bash boxes are present\n#   bin/<box>.so                    — pre-compiled C boxes (informational;\n#                                     the runner still lazy-compiles\n#                                     from src/ but having them here\n#                                     means you can verify the compile\n#                                     step worked without running)\n#   pool-runner                     — symlink to soramech-pool\n#   manifest.json                   — summary stats\n#\n# Run as:\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir>\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir> --dir <project-root>\n#\n# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded ${DIR}\n# path with an override argument; all paths relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nMAP=\"\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ argv parse — map first, --dir <path> optional\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --dir)\n            DIR=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        --help|-h)\n            grep '^#' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n            exit 0\n            ;;\n        *)\n            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n                MAP=\"$1\"\n            else\n                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n                exit 2\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\nif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\nif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\nbox_field() {\n    local file=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n        | head -n1 \\\n        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\ncp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\ncp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Issue 246 — per-port custom translation shims. Box JSONs reference\n# them by relative path under translations/; the runtime resolves\n# the path relative to the compiled map dir at dispatch time.\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/translations\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/translations\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/translations/.\" \"$COMPILED/translations/\"\nfi\n\n# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\nshopt -s nullglob\nfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\ndone\nshopt -u nullglob\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\nLANGS=()\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    seen=0\n    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n    done\n    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_spec\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: missing spec.so for language '$lang'\" >&2\n        echo \"  expected at $src_spec — run 'make' in $DIR\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang\"\n    cp \"$src_spec\" \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    # Bash spec needs its companion server script for runtime.\n    if [[ \"$lang\" == \"bash\" ]] && [[ -f \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" ]]; then\n        cp \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" \"$COMPILED/langs/bash/\"\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ merge_lua_sources — concatenate all Lua source files into one\n# merged module (issue 313). Each per-file module is wrapped in its\n# own closure so the file's `local` declarations stay file-scoped,\n# and exported under the source file's basename. The Lua spec\n# detects the merged file at init and loads it once per worker\n# instead of per-file lazy-loading every box's ref. The original\n# files stay in src/ unchanged so the existing per-file path still\n# works for callers that haven't been told about the merge.\nmerge_lua_sources() {\n    local out=\"$COMPILED/src/__merged__.lua\"\n    shopt -s nullglob\n    local files=(\"$COMPILED/src\"/*.lua)\n    shopt -u nullglob\n    if [[ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then return; fi\n\n    {\n        echo \"-- soramech merged Lua module (issue 313)\"\n        echo \"-- Generated by soramech-compile.sh; do not hand-edit.\"\n        echo \"-- Each per-file module wraps in its own closure and is\"\n        echo \"-- exported under the source file's basename, so two\"\n        echo \"-- files can both define a local M without colliding.\"\n        echo \"\"\n        echo \"local merged = {}\"\n        echo \"\"\n        local f base\n        for f in \"${files[@]}\"; do\n            base=$(basename \"$f\" .lua)\n            if [[ \"$base\" == \"__merged__\" ]]; then continue; fi\n            echo \"-- {{{ from $(basename \"$f\")\"\n            echo \"merged[\\\"$base\\\"] = (function()\"\n            cat \"$f\"\n            echo \"\"\n            echo \"end)()\"\n            echo \"-- }}}\"\n            echo \"\"\n        done\n        echo \"return merged\"\n    } > \"$out\"\n}\nmerge_lua_sources\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\nn_c_compiled=0\nn_c_failed=0\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\ndone\n\nif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A real copy (not a symlink) is intentional: the runner discovers\n# its sibling langs/ via /proc/self/exe, which follows symlinks to\n# their canonical target. A symlinked pool-runner would resolve back\n# to the project tree and pick up the project's langs/ instead of\n# the bundled compiled/langs/. Copying keeps the compiled artifact\n# self-describing and portable.\ncp \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\nchmod +x \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ write manifest.json\n# Hand-rolled JSON (no jq) keeps the script self-contained. The\n# fields are stable enough to grep against in tests.\nn_boxes=$(ls -1 \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\nn_langs=${#LANGS[@]}\nlangs_json=\"\"\nfirst=1\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n        langs_json=\"\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n        first=0\n    else\n        langs_json+=\",\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n    fi\ndone\ncompiled_at=$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\nmap_name=$(basename \"$MAP\")\n\ncat > \"$COMPILED/manifest.json\" <<EOF\n{\n    \"name\": \"$map_name\",\n    \"compiled_at\": \"$compiled_at\",\n    \"n_boxes\": $n_boxes,\n    \"n_languages\": $n_langs,\n    \"languages\": [$langs_json],\n    \"c_boxes_precompiled\": $n_c_compiled,\n    \"source_map_dir\": \"$MAP\"\n}\nEOF\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ summary line\necho \"compiled $map_name → $COMPILED\"\necho \"  boxes:       $n_boxes\"\necho \"  languages:   $n_langs (${LANGS[*]+${LANGS[*]}})\"\necho \"  c precompiled: $n_c_compiled\"\necho\necho \"run with:\"\necho \"  $COMPILED/pool-runner $COMPILED\"\n# }}}\n",

    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "input":{
          "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# tests/315-refs-test.sh — unit-style tests for scripts/soramech-ref.sh.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: exercises the acquire / release / list /\n# count / reap commands of the reference helper through every\n# meaningful state transition, asserting the right number of live\n# references at each step. The test creates a private temp directory\n# per scenario, runs the helper against it, and reports per-scenario\n# pass / fail.\n#\n# Run as:\n#   tests/315-refs-test.sh\n#   tests/315-refs-test.sh --dir <project-root>\n#\n# Convention: hard-coded ${DIR} with --dir override; everything\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]] && [[ \"$1\" == \"--dir\" ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$2\"\nfi\nREF=\"$DIR/scripts/soramech-ref.sh\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ counters\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ assert_count — soramech-ref.sh count <dir> should equal $expected\nassert_count() {\n    local label=\"$1\"\n    local target=\"$2\"\n    local expected=\"$3\"\n    local got\n    got=$(\"$REF\" count \"$target\")\n    if [[ \"$got\" == \"$expected\" ]]; then\n        printf \"  %-44s ok\\n\" \"$label\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"  %-44s FAIL — expected %s, got %s\\n\" \"$label\" \"$expected\" \"$got\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$label: expected $expected, got $got\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ scenario_basic — acquire, list, release, count\nscenario_basic() {\n    local tmp\n    tmp=$(mktemp -d)\n    assert_count \"basic: fresh dir has 0\"            \"$tmp\" \"0\"\n    local id\n    id=$(\"$REF\" acquire \"$tmp\")\n    assert_count \"basic: after acquire has 1\"        \"$tmp\" \"1\"\n    \"$REF\" release \"$tmp\" --id \"$id\"\n    assert_count \"basic: after release has 0\"        \"$tmp\" \"0\"\n    rm -rf \"$tmp\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ scenario_two_acquires — independent ids, partial release\nscenario_two_acquires() {\n    local tmp\n    tmp=$(mktemp -d)\n    local id1 id2\n    id1=$(\"$REF\" acquire \"$tmp\")\n    id2=$(\"$REF\" acquire \"$tmp\")\n    assert_count \"two-acquires: count 2\"             \"$tmp\" \"2\"\n    \"$REF\" release \"$tmp\" --id \"$id1\"\n    assert_count \"two-acquires: after one release 1\" \"$tmp\" \"1\"\n    \"$REF\" release \"$tmp\" --id \"$id2\"\n    assert_count \"two-acquires: after both 0\"        \"$tmp\" \"0\"\n    rm -rf \"$tmp\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ scenario_stale_pid — a fabricated dead pid validates as stale\n# We append a fabricated acquire line with a PID that doesn't exist\n# (the PID-MAX on Linux is usually 4194304; 9999999 is safely past\n# it on every kernel we'd run on).\nscenario_stale_pid() {\n    local tmp\n    tmp=$(mktemp -d)\n    local id1\n    id1=$(\"$REF\" acquire \"$tmp\")\n    printf 'acquire fake-dead %s 9999999 9999999 -\\n' \"2026-05-24T00:00:00-07:00\" >> \"$tmp/.refs\"\n    assert_count \"stale: live one counts, fake doesn't\" \"$tmp\" \"1\"\n    \"$REF\" reap \"$tmp\"\n    # After reap, only the live entry remains. The released-flag\n    # entry from id1 (we haven't released yet) stays.\n    assert_count \"stale: after reap still 1 live\"    \"$tmp\" \"1\"\n    \"$REF\" release \"$tmp\" --id \"$id1\"\n    assert_count \"stale: after release of real 0\"    \"$tmp\" \"0\"\n    rm -rf \"$tmp\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ scenario_marker — marker file presence gates validity\n# Acquire with a marker, count should be 1. Remove the marker, count\n# drops to 0 (marker missing = ref is stale).\nscenario_marker() {\n    local tmp marker\n    tmp=$(mktemp -d)\n    marker=\"$tmp/holder.alive\"\n    touch \"$marker\"\n    local id1\n    id1=$(\"$REF\" acquire \"$tmp\" --marker \"$marker\")\n    assert_count \"marker: present → 1 live\"          \"$tmp\" \"1\"\n    rm -f \"$marker\"\n    assert_count \"marker: missing → 0 live\"          \"$tmp\" \"0\"\n    rm -rf \"$tmp\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ scenario_list_json — list output should be JSON-shaped enough\n# Not a strict JSON parse (no jq) — we just want to see the array\n# brackets and the expected number of records inside.\nscenario_list_json() {\n    local tmp\n    tmp=$(mktemp -d)\n    local id1 id2\n    id1=$(\"$REF\" acquire \"$tmp\")\n    id2=$(\"$REF\" acquire \"$tmp\")\n    local out\n    out=$(\"$REF\" list \"$tmp\")\n    local first_char\n    first_char=\"${out:0:1}\"\n    local last_char\n    last_char=\"${out: -1}\"\n    local n_records\n    n_records=$(echo \"$out\" | grep -c '\"valid\":')\n    if [[ \"$first_char\" == \"[\" ]] && [[ \"$last_char\" == \"]\" ]] && [[ \"$n_records\" == \"2\" ]]; then\n        printf \"  %-44s ok\\n\" \"list: JSON array with 2 records\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"  %-44s FAIL — first=%s last=%s records=%s\\n\" \\\n            \"list: JSON array with 2 records\" \"$first_char\" \"$last_char\" \"$n_records\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"list-json: first=$first_char last=$last_char records=$n_records\")\n    fi\n    rm -rf \"$tmp\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run\necho \"315 — reference helper tests:\"\nscenario_basic\nscenario_two_acquires\nscenario_stale_pid\nscenario_marker\nscenario_list_json\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\nif [[ \"$fail\" -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do echo \"    - $f\"; done\n    exit 1\nfi\nexit 0\n# }}}\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/315-refs-test.sh"
        },

        },

        "type":"tool_use"

After the assertion the test releases the reference and\n# clears every generation directory so it doesn't interfere with the\n# compile_pipeline_check that runs alongside.\nrefs_fork_on_live_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local base=\"$map/compiled\"\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"315 compile fork on live refs\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$base\" \"$map\"/compiled.*\n    \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1\n\n    local id\n    id=$(\"$DIR/scripts/soramech-ref.sh\" acquire \"$base\")\n    \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1\n\n    local detail=\"\"\n    [[ -d \"$base\"        ]] || detail+=\"compiled/ missing; \"\n    [[ -d \"$map/compiled.1\" ]] || detail+=\"compiled.1/ missing; \"\n    grep -q '\"forked_from\"' \"$map/compiled.1/manifest.json\" 2>/dev/null \\\n        || detail+=\"forked_from missing from compiled.1; \"\n    # Pinned generation must still run. Capture stdout/err so a\n    # crash on the pinned dir surfaces clearly.\n    if ! (cd /tmp && \"$base/pool-runner\" \"$base\" >/dev/null 2>&1); then\n        detail+=\"pinned generation no longer runs; \"\n    fi\n\n    \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-ref.sh\" release \"$base\" --id \"$id\" >/dev/null\n    rm -rf \"$base\" \"$map\"/compiled.*\n\n    if [[ -z \"$detail\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$detail\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"315-refs fork: $detail\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ encap_output_only_file_check() — output-side encap reaches both",

    "content":[{
        "name":"Edit",
        "input":{
          "old_string":"## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` from issue 309 is destructive at the\ntop:\n\n```bash\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" ...\n```\n\nWhatever lived in `<map>/compiled/` before the rebuild is gone. If\nanother process — a long-running runner, a different shell, a\nsibling tool that opened the artifact yesterday — had pinned to\nthat exact compiled layout (a particular `pool-runner` binary, a\nparticular `spec.so` ABI, a particular set of pre-compiled C\nboxes), the rebuild yanks the rug. The holder either crashes,\nsilently retains stale `dlopen` handles, or starts reading new\nfiles mid-flight.\n\nThis is fine in single-user development. It stops being fine the\nmoment a SoraMech artifact is the kind of thing other programs\nhold onto across time.",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"## Status\nin progress · reference helper, fork-on-live-references compile,\nunit tests and integration test all shipped; a handful of\nfollow-on questions (runner self-acquire, reap-all across\ngenerations, .refs log versioning, editor extension) remain open\n\n## Current behavior\n\nA compiled artifact directory now carries a reference log\n(`.refs`) and the compile pipeline checks it before deciding\nwhere to write. The pieces:\n\n**`scripts/soramech-ref.sh`** is the helper any holder uses. The\nfive actions:\n- `acquire <compiled-dir> [--id <id>] [--marker <path>]` — append\n  one acquire record, print the assigned id (so the holder knows\n  what to release later).\n- `release <compiled-dir> --id <id>` — append the matching\n  release record.\n- `list <compiled-dir>` — emit a JSON array of every record with\n  a per-entry `valid` flag (the back pointer's liveness verdict).\n- `count <compiled-dir>` — print a single integer, the number of\n  live references (used by the compile script's fork decision).\n- `reap <compiled-dir>` — rewrite the log to drop released and\n  invalidated entries. Takes a `mkdir`-style lock; steady-state\n  acquire / release are lock-free.\n\nThe back pointer is **PID + `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22**\n(process start time in clock ticks since boot). The PID alone\nisn't enough — PIDs recycle — so the start-time match is what\ndistinguishes \"the original holder is still alive\" from \"a\ndifferent process happens to have the same PID now.\" An optional\nmarker path acts as a second liveness signal: if the holder\nmaintains a marker file, its absence means the holder is gone\neven if the PID still validates.\n\n**`scripts/soramech-compile.sh`** consults the log via `count`\nbefore deciding where to build:\n1. If `<map>/compiled/` doesn't exist → build there fresh.\n2. If it exists with zero live references → wipe and rebuild\n   there (same destructive shape as before).\n3. If it exists with one or more live references → pick the next\n   `compiled.N` sibling (N = max existing index + 1) and build\n   there. The original `compiled/` stays intact. The new\n   manifest carries a `forked_from` field naming the parent\n   generation.\n\nConvention: the canonical `compiled/` remains the first\ngeneration (the non-fork case); fork siblings are\n`compiled.1/`, `compiled.2/`, etc. There is no `compiled`\nsymlink in this slice — callers who want \"the latest\" run the\ncompile and use whatever path it prints. Callers who want a\nspecific pinned generation use whichever path they acquired\ntheir reference against.\n\n**`tests/315-refs-test.sh`** covers the helper end-to-end: fresh\ndir → acquire → list (1 valid) → release → count (0); two\nindependent acquires with partial release; a fabricated dead-PID\nentry that validates as stale and is dropped by `reap`; a\nmarker-path entry whose validity flips when the marker is\nremoved; and a JSON-shape spot-check on `list`. All 12 scenarios\npass.\n\n**Integration check in `scripts/run-tests.sh`** compiles the\npipeline fixture, acquires a reference on `compiled/`, compiles\nagain, asserts `compiled.1/` was created with `forked_from`\npointing back at `compiled/`, AND that the original pinned\ngeneration still runs (its `pool-runner` and `spec.so` files\nare untouched). After the assertion the test releases the\nreference and clears every generation so the rest of the suite\nruns against a clean slate.\n\nThe reference count remains **expected to be unreliable**: a\ncrashing holder doesn't get the chance to release.     "oldString":"## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` from issue 309 is destructive at the\ntop:\n\n```bash\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" ...\n```\n\nWhatever lived in `<map>/compiled/` before the rebuild is gone. If\nanother process — a long-running runner, a different shell, a\nsibling tool that opened the artifact yesterday — had pinned to\nthat exact compiled layout (a particular `pool-runner` binary, a\nparticular `spec.so` ABI, a particular set of pre-compiled C\nboxes), the rebuild yanks the rug. The holder either crashes,\nsilently retains stale `dlopen` handles, or starts reading new\nfiles mid-flight.\n\nThis is fine in single-user development. It stops being fine the\nmoment a SoraMech artifact is the kind of thing other programs\nhold onto across time.",
    "newString":"## Status\nin progress · reference helper, fork-on-live-references compile,\nunit tests and integration test all shipped; a handful of\nfollow-on questions (runner self-acquire, reap-all across\ngenerations, .refs log versioning, editor extension) remain open\n\n## Current behavior\n\nA compiled artifact directory now carries a reference log\n(`.refs`) and the compile pipeline checks it before deciding\nwhere to write. The pieces:\n\n**`scripts/soramech-ref.sh`** is the helper any holder uses. The\nfive actions:\n- `acquire <compiled-dir> [--id <id>] [--marker <path>]` — append\n  one acquire record, print the assigned id (so the holder knows\n  what to release later).\n- `release <compiled-dir> --id <id>` — append the matching\n  release record.\n- `list <compiled-dir>` — emit a JSON array of every record with\n  a per-entry `valid` flag (the back pointer's liveness verdict).\n- `count <compiled-dir>` — print a single integer, the number of\n  live references (used by the compile script's fork decision).\n- `reap <compiled-dir>` — rewrite the log to drop released and\n  invalidated entries. Takes a `mkdir`-style lock; steady-state\n  acquire / release are lock-free.\n\nThe back pointer is **PID + `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22**\n(process start time in clock ticks since boot). The PID alone\nisn't enough — PIDs recycle — so the start-time match is what\ndistinguishes \"the original holder is still alive\" from \"a\ndifferent process happens to have the same PID now.\" An optional\nmarker path acts as a second liveness signal: if the holder\nmaintains a marker file, its absence means the holder is gone\neven if the PID still validates.\n\n**`scripts/soramech-compile.sh`** consults the log via `count`\nbefore deciding where to build:\n1. If `<map>/compiled/` doesn't exist → build there fresh.\n2. If it exists with zero live references → wipe and rebuild\n   there (same destructive shape as before).\n3. If it exists with one or more live references → pick the next\n   `compiled.N` sibling (N = max existing index + 1) and build\n   there. The original `compiled/` stays intact. The new\n   manifest carries a `forked_from` field naming the parent\n   generation.\n\nConvention: the canonical `compiled/` remains the first\ngeneration (the non-fork case); fork siblings are\n`compiled.1/`, `compiled.2/`, etc. There is no `compiled`\nsymlink in this slice — callers who want \"the latest\" run the\ncompile and use whatever path it prints. Callers who want a\nspecific pinned generation use whichever path they acquired\ntheir reference against.\n\n**`tests/315-refs-test.sh`** covers the helper end-to-end: fresh\ndir → acquire → list (1 valid) → release → count (0); two\nindependent acquires with partial release; a fabricated dead-PID\nentry that validates as stale and is dropped by `reap`; a\nmarker-path entry whose validity flips when the marker is\nremoved; and a JSON-shape spot-check on `list`. All 12 scenarios\npass.\n\n**Integration check in `scripts/run-tests.sh`** compiles the\npipeline fixture, acquires a reference on `compiled/`, compiles\nagain, asserts `compiled.1/` was created with `forked_from`\npointing back at `compiled/`, AND that the original pinned\ngeneration still runs (its `pool-runner` and `spec.so` files\nare untouched). After the assertion the test releases the\nreference and clears every generation so the rest of the suite\nruns against a clean slate.\n\nThe reference count remains **expected to be unreliable**: a\ncrashing holder doesn't get the chance to release. The back\npointer (PID + start time + optional marker) lets `list` and\n`reap` independently verify whether any given acquire is still\nmeaningful. The compile pipeline forks if ANY ref exists,\nstale or otherwise — operators run `reap` first if they want\nto consolidate. The philosophy is unchanged: the artifact\ndirectory belongs to its readers until proven otherwise, and an\nextra build dir is cheap compared to a use-after-rebuild crash.\n\nThe previous destructive behaviour:\n\n```bash\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" ...\n```\n\nstill runs unchanged when there are zero live references (the\ncommon single-user-development case). The fork path only fires\nwhen something else is pinning the directory.",
