        "type":"text",
        "text":"315 shipped. Five files changed:\n- **`scripts/soramech-ref.sh`** (new) — the acquire/release/list/count/reap helper. Back pointer is PID + `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 (start time in clock ticks). Optional marker file path as a second liveness signal. Append-only log; `mkdir`-style lock only on `reap`.\n- **`scripts/soramech-compile.sh`** — consults the log via the new `count` action. Zero live refs → destructive rebuild on `compiled/` (the old behaviour, unchanged). One or more live refs → fork to the next `compiled.N` sibling. Forked manifest carries `forked_from` pointing back at the parent generation.\n- **`.gitignore`** — extended with `tests/maps/*/compiled.*/` for the sibling pattern.\n- **`tests/315-refs-test.sh`** (new) — 12 unit scenarios: fresh/acquire/release/count cycles, two-acquires partial-release, fabricated-dead-PID stale detection + reap, marker-file presence gating, JSON shape of `list`.\n- **`scripts/run-tests.sh`** — folds the unit suite into the integration suite, plus an end-to-end fork check that compiles, acquires, compiles again, and asserts the pinned generation still runs.\n\nSuite: **23 passed, 4 pre-existing failed** (all 319-series, unchanged). Both new 315 tests green; the existing `compile_pipeline_check` still passes alongside.\n\n**Todo recap.** Three of five done (both 248 sub-tasks I could finish + 315). Two left:\n- **#2 — 248 editor toggles + Encapsulate action.** JS/HTML in `assets/`. I can read the existing inspector + file-browser code and make changes, but verifying needs you in a browser with the dev server.\n- **#4 — 319.** \"Open — planning stub\" with several design questions you'd need to resolve before code lands; better tackled in conversation than solo.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\n- The `count` action I added to the ref helper (beyond the issue's spec of `list` / `acquire` / `release` / `reap`) is the load-bearing piece for the compile script's fork decision. Returning JSON from `list` is great for diagnostics but bad for shell logic — parsing JSON with grep is fragile, and the compile script's question is a yes-or-no. A separate integer-emitting action means the script's check is one `[[ \"$live\" -eq 0 ]]` comparison instead of a regex over a JSON blob. Small API addition; big simplification at the call site.\n- The PID + start-time-ticks back pointer is the cheapest reliable \"is this process still the same one\" verification on Linux. The PID alone is a recycling hazard (kernels reuse PIDs in days); the start-time-ticks anchor pins the identity to a specific process incarnation. Match both → \"yes it's the same holder\"; mismatch → \"the PID got reused by something else, treat this ref as stale.\" No kernel calls, no parent tracking, just `/proc/<pid>/stat` parsing.\n- The \"compile/ vs compile.N/\" naming asymmetry (the first generation is `compiled/`, forks are `compiled.1/`, `compiled.2/`) is a deliberate divergence from the issue's \"symlink + always-indexed\" suggestion. The reason: single-user development never forks, so the canonical name should be the canonical path, not a symlink that resolves to `compiled.0/`. The fork path only adds artifacts when the system genuinely needs them. The cost is no \"latest\" pointer — callers have to track which generation they want — but in practice each caller already knows which generation they acquired against, so the pointer wouldn't have helped them.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\nFor next direction: do you want me to dive into the editor toggles for 248 (I'll need you to verify in the browser), tee up the 319 design conversation, or pause here so you can review what's landed across 248 / 315 / 320 and decide what to commit? The diff is getting sizeable across three issues; a checkpoint might be useful before more changes pile on."

The inspector shows inputs (a\n    // single input wire feeds the routing) plus an n_outputs\n    // number control; the output ports themselves are fixed as\n    // out_0..out_<n-1>, not user-renameable (issue 224 rule\n    // extended to the output side).\n    if (routing_kind(box) === 'iterator') {\n      const in_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      in_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n      in_sec.textContent = 'inputs';\n      fields.appendChild(in_sec);\n      fields.appendChild(mk_port_display(box.inputs));\n\n      const out_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      out_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n      out_sec.textContent = 'outputs (round-robin)';\n      fields.appendChild(out_sec);\n\n      const n_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      n_inp.type        = 'number';\n      n_inp.min         = '1';\n      n_inp.value       = String((box.routing && box.routing.n_outputs) || 2);\n      n_inp.style.cssText = 'width:80px;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      n_inp.addEventListener('change', () => {\n        const v = parseInt(n_inp.value, 10);\n        if (!isNaN(v) && v >= 1) set_n_outputs(v);\n      });\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('n_outputs', n_inp));\n      return;\n    }\n\n\n    // ref: read-only display showing just the basename (no path, no\n    // extension), plus browse / view buttons. Full path stored on the\n    // box still — the display is just a UI tightening since paths can\n    // be long enough to overflow the sidebar.\n    const ref_wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    ref_wrap.style.cssText = 'display:flex;gap:4px;align-items:center;';\n    const ref_disp = document.createElement('span');\n    ref_disp.className = 'ref-display';\n    ref_disp.title     = box.ref || '';   // full path on hover\n    ref_disp.textContent = basename_no_ext(box.ref) || '(none)';\n    const browse_btn = document.createElement('button');\n    browse_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n    browse_btn.textContent = 'browse';\n    browse_btn.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n    browse_btn.onclick = open_browser;\n    // \"view\" button opens a floating, draggable read-only window with\n    // the current ref's source content (issue 215). Hidden when ref\n    // is empty since there's nothing to fetch (issue 227).\n    const view_btn = document.createElement('button');\n    view_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n    view_btn.textContent = 'view';\n    view_btn.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n    view_btn.hidden = !box.ref;\n    view_btn.onclick = () => {\n      if (!current_box || !current_box.ref) {\n        status_msg('view source: no ref set', 'error');\n        return;\n      }\n      SourceView.open_source_view(current_box.ref, current_box);\n    };\n    ref_wrap.appendChild(ref_disp);\n    ref_wrap.appendChild(browse_btn);\n    ref_wrap.appendChild(view_btn);\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('ref', ref_wrap));\n",

Used for both\n645\t  // first-time load (no map stored yet) and switching maps later. The\n646\t  // picker carries its own server-URL input so it works before any\n647\t  // server has been configured; nothing here reads from API state.\n648\t  function show_map_picker() {\n649\t    Inspector.show_content('maps', (container) => {\n650\t      container.innerHTML = '';\n651\t\n652\t      // -- helper: collapsible group with a body element\n653\t      function mk_group(label) {\n654\t        let collapsed = false;\n655\t        const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n656\t        const hdr  = document.createElement('div');\n657\t        hdr.className = 'fb-group-hdr';\n658\t        const toggle = document.createElement('span');\n659\t        toggle.className   = 'fb-group-toggle';\n660\t        toggle.textContent = '▼';\n661\t        hdr.appendChild(toggle);\n662\t        const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n663\t        lbl.className   = 'fb-header';\n664\t        lbl.textContent = label;\n665\t        hdr.appendChild(lbl);\n666\t        const body = document.createElement('div');\n667\t        hdr.onclick = () => {\n668\t          collapsed = !collapsed;\n669\t          toggle.textContent = collapsed ? Routing kind also gates whether\n        -- ref/fn are required: iterator is a pure routing\n        -- primitive with no language function attached; plain\n        -- and comparator boxes need a function to invoke.\n        local r = box.routing\n        local is_routing_primitive = false\n        if r == nil then\n            err(errors, \"call box missing 'routing' field (issue 233)\")\n        elseif type(r) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'routing' must be a table\")\n        elseif type(r.kind) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'routing.kind' must be a string\")\n        elseif not valid_routing_kinds[r.kind] then\n            err(errors, \"'routing.kind' = '\" .. r.kind ..\n                \"' is not one of 'plain'/'comparator'/'iterator' \" ..\n                \"(other kinds belong to follow-on issues 240–243)\")\n        else\n            if r.kind == \"comparator\" then\n                if type(r.comparand) ~= \"number\" then\n                    err(errors, \"comparator routing requires numeric 'routing.comparand'\")\n                end\n            elseif r.kind == \"iterator\" then\n                is_routing_primitive = true\n                if type(r.n_outputs) ~= \"number\"\n                   or r.n_outputs < 1\n                   or r.n_outputs ~= math.floor(r.n_outputs) then\n                    err(errors, \"iterator routing requires 'routing.n_outputs' to be a positive integer\")\n                end\n            end\n        end\n\n        -- Legacy fields are explicitly rejected (issue 233 ships\n        -- no in-loader migration). The editor or a one-off script\n        -- rewrites old maps to the new shape; reading the old\n        -- shape with this schema is meant to fail loudly.\n        if box.comparand ~= nil then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' is a legacy field — use routing = \" ..\n                \"{ kind = 'comparator', comparand = <number> } instead (issue 233)\")\n        end\n        if box.iterator_outputs ~= nil then\n            err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs' is a legacy field — use routing = \" ..\n                \"{ kind = 'iterator', n_outputs = <integer> } instead (issue 233)\")\n        end\n\n        if not is_routing_primitive then\n            if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n                err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n            end\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- variadic_inputs: optional list of base names; each name must\n        -- correspond to a series of inputs named \"<base>_<index>\" in\n        -- box.inputs (the editor maintains this; we only check the\n        -- shape here). See issue 217 part B.\n        if box.variadic_inputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.variadic_inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.variadic_inputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- has_output: optional; absence means \"true\" (default behavior).\n        -- false marks a sink box whose function has no return values\n        -- (issue 226); the runtime treats such boxes as terminal and the\n        -- editor hides the output port and inspector output section.\n        if box.has_output ~= nil and type(box.has_output) ~= \"boolean\" then\n            err(errors, \"'has_output' must be a boolean\")\n        end\n        -- Per-port `optional` flag (issue 230). Absent means false: the\n        -- port is required and must be either wired or carry a literal\n        -- value. The wire/literal/optional triple-check happens at the\n        -- graph level (validate-map.lua and the editor's compile path),\n        -- not here — this only validates per-port shape.\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) == \"table\" then\n            for i, p in ipairs(box.inputs) do\n                if type(p) == \"table\" and p.optional ~= nil and type(p.optional) ~= \"boolean\" then\n                    err(errors, \"'inputs[\" .. i .. \"].optional' must be a boolean\")\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- read / write: dispatch-layer IO primitives (issue 229). Shape\n    -- check is intentionally permissive — the graph loader does the\n    -- \"has a value or a path\" semantic check.\n    if box.kind == \"read\" or box.kind == \"write\" then\n        if box.value ~= nil and type(box.value) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'value' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.path ~= nil and type(box.path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'path' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_input_bindings\n-- Graph-level check from issue 230: every input port on every box\n-- must be in one of three states by compile time —\n--   1. a wire is connected to it\n--   2. a literal `value` is set on it\n--   3. it carries `optional: true`\n-- Otherwise the box would silently receive a missing arg at runtime\n-- and the bug would only surface where the function happens to\n-- reference it. The check fails loud and points at the exact box +\n-- port instead.\n--\n-- `boxes` is a table mapping box-id → box record (the shape the\n-- editor cache and the phase 2 loader's graph use). Returns an\n-- array of error strings; empty array means OK.\nfunction M.check_input_bindings(boxes)\n    local errors = {}\n\n    -- precompute: for each (to_box, to_input) → true if a wire targets it.\n    -- Connections live on both endpoints (issue 228), so scanning every\n    -- box's connection list overcounts but doesn't miss anything.\n    local wired = {}\n    for _, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.to_box and c.to_input then\n                wired[c.to_box .. \"\\0\" .. c.to_input] = true\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- stable per-box iteration for predictable error ordering\n    local ids = {}\n    for id, _ in pairs(boxes) do ids[#ids + 1] = id end\n    table.sort(ids)\n\n    for _, id in ipairs(ids) do\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        for _, p in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n            local has_wire    = wired[id .. \"\\0\" .. p.name] == true\n            local has_literal = p.value ~= nil and p.value ~= \"\"\n            local is_optional = p.optional == true\n            if not (has_wire or has_literal or is_optional) then\n                err(errors, \"box '\" .. id .. \"': input '\" .. tostring(p.name) ..\n                    \"' has no wire, no literal, and is not optional\")\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/001-schema.lua"
    }
  },

          "new_string":"    -- read / write: dispatch-layer IO primitives (issue 229). Shape\n    -- check is intentionally permissive — the graph loader does the\n    -- \"has a value or a path\" semantic check.\n    if box.kind == \"read\" or box.kind == \"write\" then\n        if box.value ~= nil and type(box.value) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'value' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.path ~= nil and type(box.path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'path' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n        -- Issue 248: optional `external` block. Marks a read box as\n        -- externally-supplied (its value comes from the encapsulating\n        -- parent's wire) or a write box as externally-consumed (its\n        -- emitted value surfaces back to the parent on a wire). The\n        -- block carries a binding kind plus either a name or an\n        -- index, matched by the loader's encapsulation splice.\n        if box.external ~= nil then\n            if type(box.external) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'external' must be a table\")\n            else\n                if type(box.external.kind) ~= \"string\"\n                   or not valid_external_kinds[box.external.kind] then\n                    err(errors, \"'external.kind' must be 'positional', 'numbered', or 'named'\")\n                elseif box.external.kind == \"named\" then\n                    if type(box.external.name) ~= \"string\" or #box.external.name == 0 then\n                        err(errors, \"'external.kind' = 'named' requires non-empty 'external.name'\")\n                    end\n                else\n                    if type(box.external.index) ~= \"number\"\n                       or box.external.index < 0\n                       or box.external.index ~= math.floor(box.external.index) then\n                        err(errors, \"'external.kind' = '\" .. box.external.kind ..\n                            \"' requires non-negative integer 'external.index'\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- Issue 248: encapsulated sub-map box. `ref` points at a sub-map\n    -- directory (relative to the parent map, or absolute). `inputs`\n    -- and `outputs` declare the encap box's port set on the canvas;\n    -- they're matched at graph load to the sub-map's\n    -- externally-supplied / externally-consumed marked boxes by\n    -- name or index. The C loader's encapsulation pass is the\n    -- canonical resolver; this schema only checks lexical shape.\n    if box.kind == \"map\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" or #box.ref == 0 then\n            err(errors, \"map box missing 'ref' (path to sub-map directory)\")\n        end\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.outputs ~= nil and type(box.outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'outputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end",

    "role":"assistant",
    "content":[{
        "name":"Edit",
        "input":{
          "old_string":"      // -- helper: clickable map row\n      function mk_map_row(name, subtitle, onclick) {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className   = 'fb-file-row';\n        row.textContent = name;\n        if (subtitle) {\n          const s = document.createElement('span');\n          s.style.cssText = 'font-size:9px;color:#3a3f55;margin-left:6px;font-family:monospace;';\n          s.textContent   = subtitle;\n          row.appendChild(s);\n        }\n        row.onclick = onclick;\n        return row;\n      }",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"      // -- helper: clickable map row, plus an inline \"encap\" button\n      // (issue 248) that drops the row's map onto the currently-edited\n      // parent map as a single BOX_MAP. The row's click still\n      // switches the active map (the familiar behaviour); the encap\n      // button is suppressed when `same_server` is false because the\n      // sub-map fetch and the file-path reference assume the picker\n      // and the editor are talking to the same server.\n      function mk_map_row(name, subtitle, onclick, same_server) {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className   = 'fb-file-row';\n        row.style.cssText = 'display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;';\n\n        const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n        lbl.style.cssText = 'flex:1;cursor:pointer;';\n        lbl.textContent = name;\n        if (subtitle) {\n          const s = document.createElement('span');\n          s.style.cssText = 'font-size:9px;color:#3a3f55;margin-left:6px;font-family:monospace;';\n          s.textContent   = subtitle;\n          lbl.appendChild(s);\n        }\n        lbl.onclick = onclick;\n        row.appendChild(lbl);\n\n        // The encap button is intentionally suppressed when the row\n        // refers to a map on a DIFFERENT server. Encapsulation needs\n        // to fetch the sub-map's box list to derive port shapes, and\n        // the convention of `../<name>` as a ref string only holds\n        // when both maps live as siblings under one filesystem root.\n        if (same_server && API.list_boxes_for) {\n          const encap_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          encap_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n          encap_btn.textContent = 'encap';\n          encap_btn.style.cssText = 'padding:2px 6px;font-size:10px;';\n          encap_btn.title       = 'drop ' + name + ' onto the current map as a sub-map box';\n          encap_btn.onclick = (e) => {\n            e.stopPropagation();\n            encapsulate_map(name);\n          };\n          row.appendChild(encap_btn);\n        }\n\n        return row;\n      }\n\n      // -- encapsulate_map: implements the file-browser \"Encapsulate\"\n      // action from issue 248. Fetches the target sub-map's boxes,\n      // derives the encap box's `inputs` / `outputs` arrays from\n      // every externally-supplied read box and every\n      // externally-consumed write box, and PUTs the new box at the\n      // current viewport's center.\n      async function encapsulate_map(sub_name) {\n        let sub_boxes;\n        try {\n          sub_boxes = await API.list_boxes_for(sub_name);\n        } catch (e) {\n          status_msg('encapsulate: cannot fetch ' + sub_name + ': ' + e.message, 'error');\n          return;\n        }\n\n        // Derive inputs from externally-supplied reads, outputs from\n        // externally-consumed writes. The `external.name` (named\n        // binding) becomes the encap port's name; positional /\n        // numbered bindings synthesize a default name from the kind\n        // and index so the canvas has something readable.\n        const inputs  = [];\n        const outputs = [];\n        const port_name = (b) => {\n          if (b.external && b.external.kind === 'named' && b.external.name) {\n            return b.external.name;\n          }\n          const i = (b.external && b.external.index) || 0;\n          return (b.kind === 'read' ? 'in_' : 'out_') + i;\n        };\n        for (const b of (sub_boxes || [])) {\n          if (!b.external || !b.external.kind) continue;\n          if (b.kind === 'read')  inputs.push({ name: port_name(b), type: 'string' });\n          if (b.kind === 'write') outputs.push({ name: port_name(b), type: 'string' });\n        }\n\n        // Drop the new box at the visible viewport center so the\n        // user sees it immediately rather than having to pan to find\n        // a fixed (0,0) origin.\n        const cw = Canvas.el.clientWidth, ch = Canvas.el.clientHeight;\n        const center = Canvas.screen_to_world(cw / 2, ch / 2);\n\n        const id = 'encap-' + Date.now().toString(36);\n        const box = {\n          id,\n          label: sub_name,\n          kind:  'map',\n          ref:   '../' + sub_name,\n          inputs,\n          outputs,\n          connections: [],\n          ui: { x: Math.round(center.x - 90), y: Math.round(center.y - 40) },\n        };\n        try {\n          await API.put_box(id, box);\n          Boxes.boxes[id] = box;\n          Inspector.show(box,\n            () => Canvas.mark_dirty(),\n            () => { /* parent's delete_box machinery isn't reachable\n                     * from the picker context; the user can delete\n                     * via the inspector's delete button which calls\n                     * this closure — left as a no-op here, the\n                     * inspector hides on delete. */ }\n          );\n          Canvas.mark_dirty();\n          status_msg('encapsulated ' + sub_name + ' (' + inputs.length +\n                     ' input' + (inputs.length === 1 ? '' : 's') + ', ' +\n                     outputs.length + ' output' + (outputs.length === 1 ? '' : 's') +\n                     ')', 'info');\n        } catch (e) {\n          status_msg('encapsulate: put failed: ' + e.message, 'error');\n        }\n      }",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/005-app.js"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01XD2kvCsRQZmkoYKWwKpbQQ",

      }],

    "oldString":"      // -- helper: clickable map row\n      function mk_map_row(name, subtitle, onclick) {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className   = 'fb-file-row';\n        row.textContent = name;\n        if (subtitle) {\n          const s = document.createElement('span');\n          s.style.cssText = 'font-size:9px;color:#3a3f55;margin-left:6px;font-family:monospace;';\n          s.textContent   = subtitle;\n          row.appendChild(s);\n        }\n        row.onclick = onclick;\n        return row;\n      }",
    "newString":"      // -- helper: clickable map row, plus an inline \"encap\" button\n      // (issue 248) that drops the row's map onto the currently-edited\n      // parent map as a single BOX_MAP. The row's click still\n      // switches the active map (the familiar behaviour); the encap\n      // button is suppressed when `same_server` is false because the\n      // sub-map fetch and the file-path reference assume the picker\n      // and the editor are talking to the same server.\n      function mk_map_row(name, subtitle, onclick, same_server) {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className   = 'fb-file-row';\n        row.style.cssText = 'display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;';\n\n        const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n        lbl.style.cssText = 'flex:1;cursor:pointer;';\n        lbl.textContent = name;\n        if (subtitle) {\n          const s = document.createElement('span');\n          s.style.cssText = 'font-size:9px;color:#3a3f55;margin-left:6px;font-family:monospace;';\n          s.textContent   = subtitle;\n          lbl.appendChild(s);\n        }\n        lbl.onclick = onclick;\n        row.appendChild(lbl);\n\n        // The encap button is intentionally suppressed when the row\n        // refers to a map on a DIFFERENT server. Encapsulation needs\n        // to fetch the sub-map's box list to derive port shapes, and\n        // the convention of `../<name>` as a ref string only holds\n        // when both maps live as siblings under one filesystem root.\n        if (same_server && API.list_boxes_for) {\n          const encap_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          encap_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n          encap_btn.textContent = 'encap';\n          encap_btn.style.cssText = 'padding:2px 6px;font-size:10px;';\n          encap_btn.title       = 'drop ' + name + ' onto the current map as a sub-map box';\n          encap_btn.onclick = (e) => {\n            e.stopPropagation();\n            encapsulate_map(name);\n          };\n          row.appendChild(encap_btn);\n        }\n\n        return row;\n      }\n\n      // -- encapsulate_map: implements the file-browser \"Encapsulate\"\n      // action from issue 248. Fetches the target sub-map's boxes,\n      // derives the encap box's `inputs` / `outputs` arrays from\n      // every externally-supplied read box and every\n      // externally-consumed write box, and PUTs the new box at the\n      // current viewport's center.\n      async function encapsulate_map(sub_name) {\n        let sub_boxes;\n        try {\n          sub_boxes = await API.list_boxes_for(sub_name);\n        } catch (e) {\n          status_msg('encapsulate: cannot fetch ' + sub_name + ': ' + e.message, 'error');\n          return;\n        }\n\n        // Derive inputs from externally-supplied reads, outputs from\n        // externally-consumed writes. The `external.name` (named\n        // binding) becomes the encap port's name; positional /\n        // numbered bindings synthesize a default name from the kind\n        // and index so the canvas has something readable.\n        const inputs  = [];\n        const outputs = [];\n        const port_name = (b) => {\n          if (b.external && b.external.kind === 'named' && b.external.name) {\n            return b.external.name;\n          }\n          const i = (b.external && b.external.index) || 0;\n          return (b.kind === 'read' ? 'in_' : 'out_') + i;\n        };\n        for (const b of (sub_boxes || [])) {\n          if (!b.external || !b.external.kind) continue;\n          if (b.kind === 'read')  inputs.push({ name: port_name(b), type: 'string' });\n          if (b.kind === 'write') outputs.push({ name: port_name(b), type: 'string' });\n        }\n\n        // Drop the new box at the visible viewport center so the\n        // user sees it immediately rather than having to pan to find\n        // a fixed (0,0) origin.\n        const cw = Canvas.el.clientWidth, ch = Canvas.el.clientHeight;\n        const center = Canvas.screen_to_world(cw / 2, ch / 2);\n\n        const id = 'encap-' + Date.now().toString(36);\n        const box = {\n          id,\n          label: sub_name,\n          kind:  'map',\n          ref:   '../' + sub_name,\n          inputs,\n          outputs,\n          connections: [],\n          ui: { x: Math.round(center.x - 90), y: Math.round(center.y - 40) },\n        };\n        try {\n          await API.put_box(id, box);\n          Boxes.boxes[id] = box;\n          Inspector.show(box,\n            () => Canvas.mark_dirty(),\n            () => { /* parent's delete_box machinery isn't reachable\n                     * from the picker context; the user can delete\n                     * via the inspector's delete button which calls\n                     * this closure — left as a no-op here, the\n                     * inspector hides on delete. */ }\n          );\n          Canvas.mark_dirty();\n          status_msg('encapsulated ' + sub_name + ' (' + inputs.length +\n                     ' input' + (inputs.length === 1 ? '' : 's') + ', ' +\n                     outputs.length + ' output' + (outputs.length === 1 ? '' : 's') +\n                     ')', 'info');\n        } catch (e) {\n          status_msg('encapsulate: put failed: ' + e.message, 'error');\n        }\n      }",
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/005-app.js"
  },

}

    "content":[{
        "name":"Edit",
        "input":{
          "old_string":"Multi-output (more than one externally-consumed write box per\nencap) is supported by the schema — `outputs` is an array — but\nisn't covered by a fixture yet.\n\nThe editor toggles and file-browser Encapsulate action remain\nahead.",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"Multi-output (more than one externally-consumed write box per\nencap) is supported by the schema — `outputs` is an array — but\nisn't covered by a fixture yet.\n\n**Editor side** also lands in this slice:\n\n- The **inspector kind dropdown** grows a fourth option, `map`.\n  Selecting it switches the inspector to a specialised view\n  (`render_map_box`) that shows the sub-map's `ref` path plus an\n  editable list of input + output ports. The single-output rule\n  on every other kind doesn't apply here; the user can add or\n  remove output entries directly.\n- The inspector for `read` and `write` boxes grows an\n  **externally-supplied / externally-consumed toggle**\n  (`render_external_binding`). Off by default; when on, a\n  binding-kind dropdown (named / positional / numbered) appears,\n  followed by either a name input or an integer index input.\n  The block written to the box record is the same shape the C\n  loader's `parse_external_binding` reads.\n- The **map picker rows** grow an inline `encap` button. Clicking\n  it fetches the target sub-map's boxes via the new\n  `API.list_boxes_for(name)` helper, derives the encap box's\n  `inputs` and `outputs` arrays from the sub-map's\n  externally-marked read and write boxes, and drops a fresh\n  `kind: \"map\"` box at the current viewport's center. The\n  user can then wire it in like any other box. The button is\n  suppressed for rows whose server URL doesn't match the\n  picker's, because cross-server encapsulation has no clean\n  ref-string convention.\n- The **canvas** colours encap boxes violet (distinct from the\n  blue/green/cheddar triad of call/read/write) and lays out\n  output ports per the declared `outputs` array. The kind badge\n  in the box header reads \"MAP\" so encaps are recognisable at a\n  glance.\n- The **Lua schema** (`src/001-schema.lua`) gains\n  `kind: \"map\"`, the `external` block on read/write boxes, and a\n  loosened `from_branch` rule that accepts any non-empty string\n  (encap output ports use the slot to carry a port name). The\n  schema accepts every existing fixture shape and rejects the\n  bad ones with precise diagnostics.",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/248-encapsulated-map-as-box.md"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01JU5TpUxKNEgvJY8oEFXNHb",
        "type":"tool_use"
      }],

        "text":"All four 248 sub-tasks landed plus 315; only 319 left on the original todo. Five files touched for the editor slice:\n\n- **`src/001-schema.lua`** — added `map` kind, the `external` block on read/write, and loosened `from_branch` to accept any non-empty string (encap output ports use it for port names). Spot-tested: every fixture shape passes, three deliberately-broken shapes get rejected with precise messages.\n- **`assets/js/003-api.js`** — added `list_boxes_for(other_map_name)` for fetching sub-map shapes at encap time.\n- **`assets/js/002-boxes.js`** — `map` gets a violet color, a `sub-map` default header that falls back to the ref basename, a multi-output port-positions branch driven by the declared `outputs` array, and a height calculation that respects the documented exception to single-output-per-box.\n- **`assets/js/004-inspector.js`** — kind dropdown grows the `map` option; two new helpers wired into `show()`: `render_external_binding` (toggle + binding-kind dropdown + name/index field on read/write boxes) and `render_map_box` (ref input + editable inputs/outputs lists with +/− buttons).\n- **`assets/js/005-app.js`** — `mk_map_row` grows an inline `encap` button; new `encapsulate_map(sub_name)` fetches the sub-map, derives ports from its externally-marked boxes, and drops a `kind:\"map\"` box at viewport center.\n\nSuite stable at 23 / 4 (same 319 failures, unchanged).\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\n- The encap button on the map-picker row is the **single editor surface that closes the loop on issue 248**: without it, the only way to create an encap box was to hand-edit JSON. Hand-edited boxes work but bypass every UI safety net. With this button, the user can click a map, get an encap box pre-populated with the right port shape derived from the sub-map's own external markings, and just wire it up. The \"derive ports from the sub-map's own marked boxes\" step is what makes the affordance trustworthy — no double-entry, no risk of the parent's encap declaring ports the sub-map doesn't have.\n- Loosening `from_branch` to accept any non-empty string was the schema change with the most reach. Before: the field was restricted to lt/eq/gt/`out_<n>` because every routing kind that used it had a fixed vocabulary. After: encapsulated maps can use it freely for named output ports. The lexical schema gives up some precision, but the precision moves to the graph-load step where it actually belongs — the loader knows the producer's kind and can verify the port name exists. The schema's job is shape, not semantics; this change honours that boundary.\n- I deliberately didn't auto-clear `ref` / `fn` / `routing` when a box flips from `call` to `map` (or vice versa). The user can edit them manually afterward, and stale fields get ignored by the kind-appropriate loader path. The alternative — implicit field clearing on kind-change — risks discarding work the user wanted to preserve when they were just exploring. The \"fields ignored when the kind doesn't read them\" rule is a quieter and more forgiving contract than \"fields wiped on transition,\" and it composes naturally with issue 320's reconfigure path where every field can change at runtime anyway.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\n**Verification needs your browser.** The schema and JS parse cleanly, the suite is green, but the actual UI rendering needs you to run the dev server, open the editor, and try the four new affordances:\n\n1. Click a map in the picker → the new `encap` button should appear next to its name.\n2. Clicking `encap` should drop a violet box on the canvas, labelled with the sub-map's name, with the right number of input + output ports.\n3. Selecting a `read` or `write` box in the inspector should show the new \"externally-supplied / externally-consumed\" toggle + binding controls.\n4. Selecting a `map` box should show the specialized inspector with ref + inputs + outputs lists.\n\n**Todo recap.** Four of five done. Last is 319 — still \"open — planning stub\" with several design questions you'd need to weigh in on before code lands. Want me to write up the design questions in chat so we can settle them, hold for the editor verification first, or pause for a commit checkpoint? The diff across 248 / 315 / 320 / the strategem is sizeable."
      }],

        "content":"1\t# 319 — Built-in library for map self-construction\n2\t\n3\t## Status\n4\topen — planning stub. Several design questions need user resolution\n5\tbefore implementation can begin. See **Open design questions**\n6\tbelow.\n7\t\n8\t## Concept\n9\t\n10\tA map should be able to build more of itself while running.\n11\tTwo built-in primitives, exposed by the runtime to every language\n12\tspec, are enough to bootstrap that capability:\n13\t\n14\t- **`create_box(filepath, function_name) -> box_handle`**\n15\t  Spawn a new box on the currently-running map. The first argument\n16\t  is the file holding the function the box will run; the second is\n17\t  the name of that function inside the file. The runtime does any\n18\t  build-pipeline work that's needed (compile the source, register\n19\t  the spec, allocate the box's input port slots) before returning\n20\t  a handle the caller can use to wire the box up.\n21\t\n22\t- **`connect(from_box, to_box_a, to_box_b, ...) -> bool`**\n23\t  Attach a wire from the single output of `from_box` to each of\n24\t  the destination boxes. Variadic on the destinations, since fan-out\n25\t  from a single producer is the common pattern. Returns true if\n26\t  every connection succeeded, false otherwise.\n27\t\n28\tTogether these let a running map grow new sub-graphs in response\n29\tto runtime conditions: a planner box decides what sub-pipeline to\n30\tbuild, calls `create_box` for each node, calls `connect` to wire\n31\tthem, and the dispatch layer picks up the new region on the next\n32\tpush.\n33\t\n34\t## Why this shape works (and the parts that need to be checked)\n35\t\n36\t**Single-output-per-box is already the law.** Issue 218 collapsed\n37\tboxes to one output. Variadic destinations on `connect` is just\n38\tfan-out across that single output — no new concept on the wire\n39\tside. The variadic part of the API matches the data model.\n40\t\n41\t**`filepath + function_name` matches box JSON.** That's already how\n42\tlanguage specs locate the code a box runs. The API takes the same\n43\ttwo strings the box JSON would hold.\n44\t\n45\t**Handle-as-return mirrors `data` boxes' encapsulation contract\n46\t(issue 248).** Encapsulated maps already expose typed handles\n47\tto externally-supplied inputs. A `create_box` handle is the same\n48\tkind of thing — a reference the caller uses to identify the box\n49\tin follow-up calls.\n50\t\n51\t## Open design questions\n52\t\n53\tThese are real forks in the design. Each one changes what the\n54\timplementation looks like; none have a default answer that's\n55\tobviously right.\n56\t\n57\t### Q1 — When does the new box exist? — **RESOLVED: runtime growth, unified store**\n58\t\n59\t**Resolution.** The slot store grows at runtime. There is no\n60\t\"static region\" versus \"dynamic region\" distinction — every box\n61\tis a dynamic box, allocated through the same mechanism, whether\n62\tit was declared in `boxes/<id>.json` at graph load or created\n63\tby a `create_box` built-in call mid-run. Graph load becomes the\n64\tfirst user of the growth primitive rather than a separate code\n65\tpath.\n66\t\n67\t**Why this is the right shape (not a compromise).**\n68\t\n69\tThe slot store *already* needs dynamic memory at runtime for an\n70\tunrelated reason: a user may push 200 values into an input slot\n71\tbefore the consuming box has run even once. Ring buffer cells\n72\thave to be growable on the push path regardless of whether the\n73\tgraph itself is growing. Once dynamic allocation is in the slot\n74\tstore's hot path, gating new *box* allocation behind a separate\n75\t\"static-only\" pathway is artificial — we'd be solving the same\n76\tproblem in two places.\n77\t\n78\tThe encapsulated-map feature (248) and the same-language-merge\n79\tresearch (313) both want to *unzip* a `.map` file into the\n80\truntime graph at the same level as ordinary boxes — the entire\n81\tpoint is that the runtime doesn't spawn a nested thread pool for\n82\tthe inner graph. Unzipping requires growing the box population\n83\tat runtime. A unified growable store covers all three callers\n84\t(graph load, `create_box`, map unzipping) with one mechanism.\n85\t\n86\t**The structure: two-level chunked-append index table, no\n87\tstatic ceilings.**\n88\t\n89\tThe slot store keeps a top-level array of \"chunk pointers.\" Each\n90\tchunk is a fixed-size block of slot pointers. Slot bodies\n91\tthemselves are allocated separately and pointed to from chunk\n92\tentries. Three layers of growth, each cheaper than the layer\n93\tabove:\n94\t\n95\t- **Layer 1 — appending a slot inside a chunk** (most common).\n96\t  Atomic-increment the chunk's in-use counter; publish the slot\n97\t  pointer at that index. Lock-free, single-instruction-ish.\n98\t- **Layer 2 — adding a new chunk** (uncommon). Write a new chunk\n99\t  pointer into the top-level array at the next free top-level\n100\t  index; bump the atomic \"chunks in use\" counter. Lock-free.\n101\t- **Layer 3 — growing the top-level array** (rare; logarithmic in\n102\t  total slots across the run). When the top-level array itself\n103\t  fills, use the double-buffer-with-swap pattern: allocate a new\n104\t  top-level array of 2× size, copy existing chunk pointers\n105\t  (pointers only; chunks themselves stay put), atomically swap\n106\t  the top-level array pointer, defer-free the old array via\n107\t  refcount or epoch-based reclamation. Workers caching the old\n108\t  top-level pointer can finish their lookups against it — every\n109\t  chunk and every slot the old array references is still alive.\n110\t\n111\t**No static ceilings anywhere.** Layer 1's chunk capacity is a\n112\ttuning constant (cache-friendly size, e.g. 64), not a limit on\n113\ttotal slots. Layer 2's top-level capacity grows via layer 3.\n114\tLayer 3 has no upper bound. The user pays one extra indirection\n115\ton every slot access (top-level → chunk → slot), and a rare\n116\tdouble-buffer swap whose cost amortizes to zero across the run.\n117\t\n118\t**Same machinery serves three callers:** graph load (the first\n119\tbatch of slots), `create_box` (one slot at a time during dispatch),\n120\tand `.map` unzipping for encapsulated maps (a burst of slots when\n121\ta sub-map is expanded into the runtime). All three look identical\n122\tto the slot store — append, append, append.\n123\t\n124\tThe allocator-wide-lock-free property is preserved. Only the\n125\tin-use counters and the top-level swap use atomics; everything\n126\ton the hot read/write path stays per-slot.\n127\t\n128\t**Removal — refcount, not tombstone.** Issue 315 (compiled\n129\tartifact reference counting) is the safety mechanism. A box's\n130\trefcount goes to zero only when no other box references it as\n131\tproducer or consumer; any worker about to use the box must hold\n132\ta reference that keeps the count positive. Therefore \"refcount\n133\treached zero\" is a proof that no worker holds a stale pointer.\n134\tSlot indices freed at that moment are safe to reuse.\n135\t\n136\tNo tombstoning required, no generation counters on handles, no\n137\tABA hazard — 315's refcount discipline subsumes all three.\n138\t\n139\t**What this resolution does NOT decide:** the precise API of the\n140\tgrowth primitive on the slot store, the cache-line-aware chunk\n141\tsize choice, and whether ring buffer *cell* growth uses\n142\tdouble-buffer-with-swap under the per-slot lock (the suggested\n143\tshape, since each slot already holds a lock during growth).\n144\tThose are implementation details for the slot store work itself,\n145\tnot the `create_box` / `connect` design.\n146\t\n147\t### Prerequisite — remove the dispatch input cap before `create_box` ships\n148\t\n149\tToday `src/012-dispatch.c` allocates five parallel stack arrays\n150\tof size 16 (`bufs`, `buf_chunks`, `datas`, `sizes`,\n151\t`input_native`) inside the per-call invocation path. A box with\n152\tmore than 16 inputs hits a hard error from the dispatcher. This\n153\tcontradicts the \"no static ceilings\" principle resolved in Q1.\n154\t\n155\t**Fix:** convert the five arrays to VLAs (`char *bufs[n];` etc.,\n156\tC99). Cost is zero — VLAs adjust the stack pointer by\n157\t`n * 5 * sizeof(void*)` with no allocator call. Keep a sanity\n158\tguard at a generous ceiling (e.g. 4096 inputs) so a runaway\n159\tloader can't blow the stack; the existing error-return path\n160\tstays in place above that.\n161\t\n162\t**Related but lower priority:** the `branch[24]` stack buffers\n163\tat dispatch.c:629/647/678 hold a `snprintf(\"out_%u\", ...)`\n164\tresult. Worst-case formatted length is 15 bytes; 24 is\n165\tarbitrary-but-safe and `snprintf` truncates without overflowing.\n166\tChange to a named constant (`MAX_BRANCH_NAME = 16`) for hygiene\n167\twhen the VLA work lands. Not a real bug.\n168\t\n169\t### Q1.5 — The shape of the `create_box` argument: box JSON schema as the contract\n170\t\n171\t`create_box`'s argument is **one structured value whose shape is\n172\texactly the box JSON schema**. In Lua, a table; in C, either a\n173\tstruct or a JSON string built by the caller; in Bash, a JSON\n174\tstring. The runtime converts to JSON internally (same path as the\n175\tuniversal wire format), validates against the box schema, and\n176\tinstantiates the box record. Anything you can write into\n177\t`boxes/<id>.json` on disk, you can pass to `create_box` at\n178\truntime.\n179\t\n180\t**Why this shape (not a fat positional signature, not key/value\n181\tvarargs, not a builder pattern):**\n182\t\n183\t- The box JSON schema **is** the source of truth on disk. Having\n184\t  `create_box` mirror that schema means there is no parallel\n185\t  \"create_box parameter list\" to maintain — adding a new schema\n186\t  field works in `create_box` automatically.\n187\t- New customization toggles (priority, debug-instrumentation\n188\t  flags, custom translation specs per port, emoji labels for tap\n189\t  mode, etc.) land in the schema and become available to\n190\t  `create_box` callers in the same change.\n191\t- Languages without rich native structured types (Bash) can use\n192\t  JSON strings; languages with rich types (Lua tables, C structs)\n193\t  can use native shapes that the spec converts.\n194\t\n195\t**Structural metadata vs runtime values — the split this design\n196\tenforces.** The argument carries **structural metadata** (id,\n197\tkind, lang, ref, fn, routing, inputs/outputs schema, position).\n198\tPer-invocation **runtime values** (the data flowing through\n199\twires) keep flowing through input slots as before. They do not\n200\tmix. Asking \"should priority arrive on an input slot?\" is the\n201\twrong question — priority is metadata, not a value flowing\n202\tthrough the dataflow. Mixing the two would make a box's *shape*\n203\tdepend on runtime state, which the slot store and the dispatcher\n204\tboth assume is fixed once the box exists.\n205\t\n206\t### Box customization surface — what `create_box` accepts (audit, 2026-05-23)\n207\t\n208\tMaintained list of every per-box customization that currently\n209\texists or is on a known open issue. When a new toggle is added\n210\tanywhere in SoraMech, **append to this list** in the same change.\n211\tThe list is a contract reminder: `create_box`'s structured\n212\targument must cover all of these because they are all valid\n213\tfields in the box JSON schema.\n214\t\n215\t**Working today (in shipped box JSON):**\n216\t\n217\t- `id` — required, unique within the map.\n218\t- `kind` — call / read / data / write / comparator / iterator /\n219\t  randomizer / weighted / distributor / map (the encapsulated\n220\t  kind from 248).\n221\t- `lang` — lua / c / bash / map (issue 303 spec registry).\n222\t- `ref` — file path to the source containing the box's function.\n223\t- `fn` — function name within `ref`.\n224\t- `inputs[]` — per-port: `name`, `type`, `value` (default),\n225\t  `optional`.\n226\t- `value` (read-box literal source).\n227\t- `path` (data and write boxes — disk file).\n228\t- `comparand` (comparator boxes).\n229\t- `routing.kind` — plain / comparator / randomizer / weighted /\n230\t  iterator / distributor.\n231\t- `routing.weights` (weighted), `routing.n_outputs` (iterator,\n232\t  randomizer).\n233\t- `iterator_outputs[]` (iterator branch names).\n234\t- `output_capacity` (ring buffer cell size hint).\n235\t- `connections[]` — outgoing wires: `from_branch`, `to_box`,\n236\t  `to_input`. (May be omitted in `create_box` calls if the caller\n237\t  will follow up with `connect()`.)\n238\t- `ui.x`, `ui.y` (canvas position).\n239\t\n240\t**Coming from open issues (must be supported by `create_box`\n241\twhen they land):**\n242\t\n243\t- `external` block on `data` boxes — issue 248 (externally-supplied).\n244\t- `external` block on `write` boxes — issue 248 amended (externally-consumed).\n245\t- `outputs[]` array — issue 248, encapsulated boxes only, exception\n246\t  to issue 218's single-output-per-box rule.\n247\t- `custom_translation_spec` per input port — issue 246.\n248\t- `encap_mode` (`inline` | `runtime`) — issue 248, on `kind: \"map\"` boxes.\n249\t- Four-emoji label for tap mode — issue 249.\n250\t- Debug instrumentation flags per box — issue 247.\n251\t- `priority` — not yet specced; would feed the pool's\n252\t  task-scheduling priority. Worth its own issue when introduced;\n253\t  goes into the schema and into this list.\n254\t\n255\t**Derived (NOT settable via `create_box`):**\n256\t\n257\t- Wire color — derived from producer/consumer language pairing\n258\t  (issue 245). The compiler colors wires; the user doesn't.\n259\t- Per-edge native flag — derived by the graph loader at compile\n260\t  time from input/output language pairs (issue 312). Not a\n261\t  user-set field.\n262\t\n263\t### Q2 — Which input port does `connect` target? — **RESOLVED: connection-entry shape from box JSON schema**\n264\t\n265\t**Resolution.** `connect`'s argument is **one (or many)\n266\tstructured value(s) whose shape is exactly a connection entry\n267\tfrom the box JSON schema's `connections[]` array**:\n268\t\n269\t```\n270\tconnect({from_box=A, from_branch=null, to_box=B, to_input=\"x\"})\n271\t```\n272\t\n273\tVariadic for multiple connections at once:\n274\t\n275\t```\n276\tconnect({from_box=A, from_branch=null, to_box=B, to_input=\"x\"},\n277\t        {from_box=A, from_branch=\"gt\",  to_box=C, to_input=\"value\"},\n278\t        {from_box=A, from_branch=\"lt\",  to_box=D, to_input=\"value\"})\n279\t```\n280\t\n281\tThe \"which port\" question is answered by **`to_input` being\n282\texplicit in every connection entry**. No implicit-first-free\n283\tmagic, no pair-syntax that has to be remembered separately from\n284\tthe JSON shape, no per-port sub-handles on the box handle. The\n285\tshape on disk and the shape in the API call are identical.\n286\t\n287\t**Why this shape (consistent with Q1.5).** The schema is the\n288\tAPI. Every place SoraMech needs a \"way to describe a box\" or a\n289\t\"way to describe a wire,\" the same JSON shape we already have on\n290\tdisk is what the API accepts. Two artifacts (the schema, the\n291\tAPI) collapse to one artifact, and every future schema change\n292\tupdates the API for free.\n293\t\n294\t**Construction in each language — `native_to_json` is the answer.**\n295\t\n296\tEach language spec already implements `native_to_json` for the\n297\tdual-ring wire format (issue 312) — that's how a Lua box's\n298\treturn value crosses into a C consumer. The *same callback*\n299\tconverts the user's spec-side value into the JSON shape the\n300\truntime ingests. No new spec contract; no new callback; adding\n301\ta new language gives self-construction for free.\n302\t\n303\t- **Lua:** table literal. Idiomatic, terse.\n304\t  ```lua\n305\t  soramech.connect({from_box = \"a\", from_branch = nil,\n306\t                    to_box = \"b\", to_input = \"x\"})\n307\t  ```\n308\t- **C:** designated-initializer struct (`connection_t c = {.from_box=\"a\", ...};`)\n309\t  for the common case; varargs JSON-string helper for dynamic\n310\t  fields. The struct definition lives alongside the C spec's\n311\t  header.\n312\t- **Bash:** JSON string. Bash has no native dict; JSON strings\n313\t  are how it talks to everything anyway.\n314\t\n315\t**Benefits that stack from machinery reuse:**\n316\t\n317\t- No new callback on the language spec — `native_to_json` is\n318\t  already required for wire crossings.\n319\t- One validator in the runtime — the box JSON schema validator\n320\t  used for `boxes/<id>.json` files at graph load handles\n321\t  runtime-constructed connections as-is.\n322\t- Persistence is trivial — if `create_box` ever grows an \"also\n323\t  write to disk\" option, the JSON is already in hand.\n324\t- The connections inside a `create_box` call's structured value\n325\t  (the box's own `connections[]` field) and standalone `connect()`\n326\t  calls produce the same internal records.\n327\t\n328\t**What this resolution does NOT decide:** the precise validation\n329\terror policy when a `to_input` names a non-existent port (likely\n330\thard-crash per Q3 territory), and whether `connect()` accepts\n331\tthe `from_box` as a handle from `create_box`, as the box's\n332\tstring id, or both (likely both, since both can be resolved to\n333\tthe same internal record). These fall under Q3 and Q4\n334\trespectively.\n335\t\n336\t### Q3 — Bool return versus hard-crash — **RESOLVED: hard-crash with reason**\n337\t\n338\t**Resolution.** `connect` returns nothing (`void`). On any\n339\tfailure it aborts the program with a plain-English message\n340\tnaming the boxes, the attempted wire, and what went wrong:\n341\t\n342\t```\n343\tsoramech: cannot connect 'a' → 'b'.in_x\n344\t  reason: 'b' has no input port named 'in_x'\n345\t  available ports: 'count', 'label'\n346\t```\n347\t\n348\tMatches the project-wide error policy in CLAUDE.md (\"prefer\n349\terror messages and breaking functionality over fallbacks\";\n350\t\"nil checks are just asking for errors\"). A bool return invites\n351\tsilent ignoring — if the user is calling `connect` they\n352\tintend the wire to exist; any reason it doesn't is a bug worth\n353\tsurfacing immediately, not a normal-flow result to branch on.\n354\t\n355\tThe corresponding `create_box` rule: failure to instantiate a\n356\tbox (missing file, malformed schema, unknown spec language,\n357\tduplicate id) is also a hard crash with reason. No box handle\n358\tis returned for a failed creation — the program aborts before\n359\tany caller has the chance to mis-use a null handle.\n360\t\n361\t### Q4 — What is the \"box handle\" actually? — **RESOLVED: auto-generated box_id string**\n362\t\n363\t**Resolution.** The handle returned by `create_box` is **a\n364\tstring — the box's `id` field from the box JSON schema**. If\n365\tthe caller's spec value supplied an explicit `id`, that string\n366\tis returned. If `id` was omitted, the runtime mints an\n367\tauto-generated UUID-style string (e.g.\n368\t`auto_8f3c2a1e9b4d`) and uses it as the box's id.\n369\t\n370\tThe handle is therefore identical to the box_id used everywhere\n371\telse in the system: in `boxes/<id>.json` filenames, in the\n372\t`from_box` / `to_box` fields of connection entries, in dispatch\n373\tlog lines, in the run-output JSONL. There is no separate handle\n374\ttype, no fast in-process pointer that has to be unwrapped at\n375\twire crossings, no struct carrying both an id and a pointer.\n376\t\n377\t**Why a string id (not an in-process pointer, not the function\n378\tname).**\n379\t\n380\t- *Not an in-process pointer*: the handle has to survive being\n381\t  passed to `connect()` from any worker, being persisted to\n382\t  `tmp/last-run.jsonl`, and potentially being carried as a value\n383\t  on a wire to another box. The cross-language wire format\n384\t  explicitly forbids handles that back-route to a specific spec\n385\t  (see `feedback_cross_language_pitfalls`). A string id has\n386\t  none of those problems.\n387\t- *Not the function name*: multiple boxes can run the same\n388\t  function with different wiring, different input slot widths,\n389\t  different external bindings. The id distinguishes them.\n390\t- *Why UUID-style auto-generation*: when a runtime caller\n391\t  constructs a box dynamically, they often don't have a\n392\t  meaningful name in mind. Auto-generation removes the need to\n393\t  invent one and removes the risk of collision with an\n394\t  existing id. Callers who *do* want a meaningful name (for\n395\t  log readability) can pass `id = \"my_planner_step_3\"`\n396\t  themselves.\n397\t\n398\t**Internal lookup cost.** The dispatcher resolves\n399\tbox_id → box record via a hash table (already needed for the\n400\texisting static graph load path). One hash lookup per `connect`\n401\tcall, amortized to ~zero for the steady-state wire-push hot\n402\tpath (which holds a direct pointer cached at graph-build time).\n403\tBox destruction (315) removes the hash entry as part of the\n404\trefcount-zero teardown.\n405\t\n406\t### Q5 — Does `create_box` trigger the build pipeline? — **RESOLVED: both, via a compile cache in tmp/**\n407\t\n408\t**Resolution.** Both runtime and compile-time paths exist, and\n409\tthe runner stays ignorant of the compiler's internals by treating\n410\tthe compiler as an external shell-out tool (which it already is:\n411\t`scripts/soramech-compile.sh`).\n412\t\n413\t**The compile cache.** A directory under `tmp/` holds compiled\n414\tartifacts keyed by a content hash of (source file + spec\n415\tlanguage + relevant compile flags). When `create_box` resolves\n416\ta `ref` + `fn`:\n417\t\n418\t1. Compute the cache key from the source's contents and the\n419\t   language spec.\n420\t2. Look up the key in the cache.\n421\t3. **Hit:** `dlopen` (or equivalent for the language) the cached\n422\t   artifact and proceed.\n423\t4. **Miss:** shell out to `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` with the\n424\t   source path and target artifact path; wait for completion;\n425\t   verify exit status; dlopen the freshly built artifact.\n426\t\n427\tThe runner never links the compiler, never imports\n428\tcompiler-internal modules, never duplicates compiler logic. It\n429\tonly knows \"if artifact X exists in the cache, use it; otherwise\n430\trun this script.\" The three-program separation in\n431\t`project_soramech` (server / runner / editor) extends cleanly to\n432\t\"runner treats compiler as external tool, same as it treats\n433\tlanguage-spec subprocess binaries.\"\n434\t\n435\t**Compile-time precompilation as optimization.** When the\n436\tcompile pipeline can statically determine that some\n437\t`create_box(spec)` calls have constant `ref` + `fn` (e.g. the\n438\tspec is a literal table in the caller's source), it can\n439\tpre-populate the cache during the compile step. Runtime calls\n440\tto `create_box` with those refs hit the cache immediately, no\n441\tshell-out latency. This is purely an optimization — correctness\n442\tdoesn't depend on it. Defer the analysis pass until profiling\n443\tshows the runtime compile-on-demand path is a bottleneck.\n444\t\n445\t**Cache invalidation.** Cache key includes source content hash,\n446\tso changing a source file naturally produces a new key (and the\n447\told entry becomes garbage to be collected during run teardown).\n448\tNo invalidation logic needed; content hashing is the\n449\tinvalidation.\n450\t\n451\t**Why not pure runtime / pure compile-time:**\n452\t\n453\t- *Pure runtime*: every `create_box` call would pay shell-out\n454\t  latency even for code that hasn't changed since the previous\n455\t  run. Wasteful in tight loops or hot planner boxes.\n456\t- *Pure compile-time*: dynamic `create_box` calls (where `ref`\n457\t  comes from a runtime value, e.g. a planner box choosing what\n458\t  pipeline to construct based on LLM output) can't be analyzed\n459\t  ahead of time. Forbidding them gives up the use case that\n460\t  motivates self-construction in the first place.\n461\t\n462\tThe cache makes both paths cheap when they apply and removes the\n463\tneed to pick one.\n464\t\n465\t## Suggested implementation steps (after Q1–Q5 are resolved)\n466\t\n467\t1. Resolve the open design questions; update this issue with the\n468\t   chosen shape before any code is written.\n469\t2. Add the two built-ins to the language-spec contract\n470\t   (`lang_spec_t` — the runtime exposes them via the spec's\n471\t   built-in table; each language spec wraps them in its native\n472\t   calling convention).\n473\t3. Extend the slot store with the growth primitive Q1 selects\n474\t   (if Q1 picks (a) or (c)).\n475\t4. Add dispatch-layer logic for newly-created boxes — they need to\n476\t   participate in the same push-on-arrival mechanism as static\n477\t   boxes.\n478\t5. Tests under `tests/`: a small map whose first box uses\n479\t   `create_box` + `connect` to build a downstream pipeline, then\n480\t   runs end-to-end and validates outputs.\n481\t6. Update `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` to describe the\n482\t   self-construction contract and the slot-store growth shape.\n483\t7. Update phase-3-progress.md.\n484\t\n485\t## Related issues and documents\n486\t\n487\t- 248 — encapsulated map as box (the function-like abstraction\n488\t  these primitives could be used to construct ad-hoc).\n489\t- 302 — wire value slot store (the structure that needs the growth\n490\t  primitive in Q1).\n491\t- 218 — single output per box (justifies the variadic-on-destinations\n492\t  shape).\n493\t- 217–222 — compile pipeline (relevant to Q5).\n494\t- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — current threading model these\n495\t  primitives must fit inside.\n496\t",
