    "originalFile":"/* src/013-jsonl-events.h — phase 3 run-log event writer.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: emits one JSON object per event,\n * one event per line, to `tmp/last-run.jsonl` for downstream\n * tooling (LLMs, CLI viewers, the integration test harness).\n *\n * Designed in issue 311. This iteration implements the per-event\n * emit functions on top of issue 314's bounded JSON writer.\n * Concurrency is a single per-writer mutex around the file write;\n * the MPSC ring buffer + dedicated writer thread from the\n * architecture doc lands as a follow-on once dispatch is producing\n * events at rate.\n *\n * Each emit returns 0 on success or -1 on a write failure / JSON\n * encode failure. Failures don't cascade: the writer keeps going,\n * and the caller can check by re-emitting or by closing.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_JSONL_EVENTS_H\n#define SORAMECH_JSONL_EVENTS_H\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\ntypedef struct jsonl_writer jsonl_writer_t;\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Open `path` for writing (truncates). Returns NULL on failure. */\njsonl_writer_t *jsonl_writer_open(const char *path);\n\n/* Flush and close the underlying file, free the writer. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid            jsonl_writer_close(jsonl_writer_t *w);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Event emitters */\n/* All timestamps are Unix epoch seconds as doubles (matches the\n * architecture doc's choice). All emits are thread-safe. */\n\nint jsonl_emit_run_start  (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           const char *map, int n_workers);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_submit(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, const char *box_id, int worker_idx);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_start (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, int worker_idx);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_end   (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, int worker_idx,\n                           long duration_us, int output_size);\n\nint jsonl_emit_run_end    (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           long duration_us, int n_tasks);\n\n/* Verbose events (opt-in via SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1).\n * `data` is logged as a string with the JSON writer's standard\n * escaping. Bytes containing NUL aren't supported; truncate to\n * the first NUL or the architecture's 4 KB cap. */\nint jsonl_emit_task_input (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, int port_index,\n                           const char *data, int size);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_output(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, const char *data, int size);\n\n/* Slot allocator events (opt-in via SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1). Emitted\n * once per slot at graph_attach_runtime time so the run log\n * records the slot layout the dispatch will use. */\nint jsonl_emit_slot_alloc (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int slot_id, int cell_capacity, int n_cells,\n                           const char *owner_box, const char *owner_port);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_JSONL_EVENTS_H */\n",
    "oldString":"/* Slot allocator events (opt-in via SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1). Emitted\n * once per slot at graph_attach_runtime time so the run log\n * records the slot layout the dispatch will use. */\nint jsonl_emit_slot_alloc (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int slot_id, int cell_capacity, int n_cells,\n                           const char *owner_box, const char *owner_port);\n/* }}} */",
    "newString":"/* Slot allocator events (opt-in via SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1). Emitted\n * once per slot at graph_attach_runtime time so the run log\n * records the slot layout the dispatch will use. Issue 319's\n * runtime self-construction also emits one per slot when a new\n * box is allocated mid-run via create_box. */\nint jsonl_emit_slot_alloc (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int slot_id, int cell_capacity, int n_cells,\n                           const char *owner_box, const char *owner_port);\n\n/* Runtime graph mutation events (issue 319 / 248 self-construction\n * paths). Always emitted when an active event-queue is present —\n * graph mutations are rare enough that they don't need a verbosity\n * gate. `box_create` fires after the new box is published into\n * the graph; `wire_add` fires after the connection has been\n * appended to the producer's array. Tracing these reveals the\n * order of mutation operations relative to the dispatch's\n * fan-out, which is the load-bearing question for diagnosing\n * runtime-create-then-push races. */\nint jsonl_emit_box_create (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           const char *box_id, const char *kind,\n                           const char *lang, const char *ref,\n                           const char *fn);\n\nint jsonl_emit_wire_add   (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           const char *from_box, const char *from_branch,\n                           const char *to_box, const char *to_input);\n\n/* Per-push events (opt-in via SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1, same gate as\n * slot_alloc since they're the slot-level activity counterpart).\n * Emitted from push_one_connection on every attempt, including\n * the skipped paths — the `result` field carries either \"ok\" or\n * a short skip reason (\"no-to-box-idx\", \"dst-null\",\n * \"input-slots-null\", \"to-input-out-of-range\", \"push-failed\").\n * Crucial for diagnosing the 319 visibility race where the new\n * box's input_slot_ids field reads as NULL at push time even\n * though runtime_create_box populated it. */\nint jsonl_emit_push       (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           const char *from_box, const char *to_box,\n                           const char *to_input, int slot_id,\n                           int n_bytes, const char *result);\n/* }}} */",

    "originalFile":"/* src/013-jsonl-events.c — phase 3 run-log event writer.\n *\n * Each emit serializes one event into a 512-byte buffer via the\n * bounded JSON writer (issue 314), appends a newline, then writes\n * the line to the underlying FILE under a per-writer mutex. The\n * mutex is what the MPSC ring buffer + dedicated writer thread\n * will replace once dispatch is producing events at rate.\n *\n * Buffer size is fixed at 512 bytes. Every event the architecture\n * doc defines fits comfortably; if a future event needs more it\n * can be bumped or made dynamic.\n *\n * Designed in issue 311.\n */\n\n#include \"013-jsonl-events.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#define EVENT_BUF 512\n\n/* {{{ Writer struct */\nstruct jsonl_writer {\n    FILE            *fp;\n    pthread_mutex_t  mtx;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_writer_open() */\njsonl_writer_t *jsonl_writer_open(const char *path)\n{\n    if (!path) return NULL;\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    if (!fp) return NULL;\n    jsonl_writer_t *w = calloc(1, sizeof *w);\n    if (!w) { fclose(fp); return NULL; }\n    w->fp = fp;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&w->mtx, NULL) != 0) {\n        fclose(fp);\n        free(w);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    return w;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_writer_close() */\nvoid jsonl_writer_close(jsonl_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&w->mtx);\n    if (w->fp) { fflush(w->fp); fclose(w->fp); w->fp = NULL; }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&w->mtx);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&w->mtx);\n    free(w);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ flush_line() — finalize the writer, append \\n, write under lock */\nstatic int flush_line(jsonl_writer_t *w, json_writer_t *jw, char *buf)\n{\n    int n = json_writer_finish(jw);\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    if (n >= EVENT_BUF) return -1;   /* would overrun the newline byte */\n    buf[n] = '\\n';\n    int total = n + 1;\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&w->mtx);\n    int written = 0;\n    if (w->fp) {\n        written = (int)fwrite(buf, 1, (size_t)total, w->fp);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&w->mtx);\n    return (written == total) ? 0 : -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ emit helpers — common event prologue */\nstatic void begin_event(json_writer_t *jw, const char *type, double ts)\n{\n    json_writer_object(jw);\n    json_writer_key(jw, \"event\"); json_writer_string(jw, type);\n    json_writer_key(jw, \"ts\");    json_writer_number(jw, ts);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_emit_run_start() */\nint jsonl_emit_run_start(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                         const char *map, int n_workers)\n{\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    char buf[EVENT_BUF];\n    json_writer_t jw;\n    json_writer_init(&jw, buf, EVENT_BUF);\n    begin_event(&jw, \"run_start\", ts);\n    json_writer_key(&jw, \"map\");        json_writer_string(&jw, map ? map : \"\");\n    json_writer_key(&jw, \"n_workers\");  json_writer_int(&jw, n_workers);\n    json_writer_end(&jw);\n    return flush_line(w, &jw, buf);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_emit_task_submit() */\nint jsonl_emit_task_submit(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, const char *box_id, int worker_idx)\n{\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    char buf[EVENT_BUF];\n    json_writer_t jw;\n    json_writer_init(&jw, buf, EVENT_BUF);\n    begin_event(&jw, \"task_submit\", ts);\n    json_writer_key(&jw, \"task_id\");  json_writer_int(&jw, output_size);\n    json_writer_end(&jw);\n    return flush_line(w, &jw, buf);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_emit_run_end() */\nint jsonl_emit_run_end(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                       long duration_us, int n_tasks)\n{\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    char buf[EVENT_BUF];\n    json_writer_t jw;\n    json_writer_init(&jw, buf, EVENT_BUF);\n    begin_event(&jw, \"run_end\", ts);\n    json_writer_key(&jw, \"duration_us\"); json_writer_int(&jw, duration_us);\n    json_writer_key(&jw, \"n_tasks\");     json_writer_int(&jw, n_tasks);\n    json_writer_end(&jw);\n    return flush_line(w, &jw, buf);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ truncate_for_log() — copy `size` bytes into `out` as a\n * NUL-terminated string, capping at 4 KB and stopping at any\n * embedded NUL. Returns the number of bytes actually copied\n * (excluding the trailing NUL). */\n#define VERBOSE_MAX 4096\nstatic int truncate_for_log(char *out, size_t cap,\n                            const char *data, int size)\n{\n    if (cap == 0) return 0;\n    int max = (size < (int)cap - 1) ? size : (int)cap - 1;\n    if (max > VERBOSE_MAX) max = VERBOSE_MAX;\n    int n = 0;\n    for (; n < max; n++) {\n        if (data[n] == '\\0') break;\n        out[n] = data[n];\n    }\n    out[n] = '\\0';\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_emit_task_input() */\nint jsonl_emit_task_input(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                          int task_id, int port_index,\n                          const char *data, int size)\n{\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    /* Verbose events are bigger than the per-event line cap; use a\n     * dedicated 8 KB buffer that fits a 4 KB data field plus\n     * JSON-escape overhead. */\n    char buf[8192];\n    char trunc[VERBOSE_MAX + 1];\n    int actual_size = truncate_for_log(trunc, sizeof trunc, data, size);\n\n    json_writer_t jw;\n    json_writer_init(&jw, buf, sizeof buf);\n    begin_event(&jw, \"task_input\", ts);\n    json_writer_key(&jw, \"task_id\");       json_writer_string(&jw, owner_box);\n    }\n    if (owner_port) {\n        json_writer_key(&jw, \"port\");      json_writer_string(&jw, owner_port);\n    }\n    json_writer_end(&jw);\n    return flush_line(w, &jw, buf);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_emit_box_create() — runtime graph mutation (issue 319) */\nint jsonl_emit_box_create(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                          const char *box_id, const char *kind,\n                          const char *lang, const char *ref,\n                          const char *fn)\n{\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    char buf[EVENT_BUF];\n    json_writer_t jw;\n    json_writer_init(&jw, buf, EVENT_BUF);\n    begin_event(&jw, \"box_create\", ts);\n    if (box_id) { json_writer_key(&jw, \"box_id\"); json_writer_string(&jw, box_id); }\n    if (kind)   { json_writer_key(&jw, \"kind\");   json_writer_string(&jw, kind);   }\n    if (lang)   { json_writer_key(&jw, \"lang\");   json_writer_string(&jw, lang);   }\n    if (ref)    { json_writer_key(&jw, \"ref\");    json_writer_string(&jw, ref);    }\n    if (fn)     { json_writer_key(&jw, \"fn\");     json_writer_string(&jw, fn);     }\n    json_writer_end(&jw);\n    return flush_line(w, &jw, buf);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_emit_wire_add() — runtime wire mutation (issue 319) */\nint jsonl_emit_wire_add(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                        const char *from_box, const char *from_branch,\n                        const char *to_box, const char *to_input)\n{\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    char buf[EVENT_BUF];\n    json_writer_t jw;\n    json_writer_init(&jw, buf, EVENT_BUF);\n    begin_event(&jw, \"wire_add\", ts);\n    if (from_box)    { json_writer_key(&jw, \"from_box\");    json_writer_string(&jw, from_box); }\n    if (from_branch) { json_writer_key(&jw, \"from_branch\"); json_writer_string(&jw, from_branch); }\n    if (to_box)      { json_writer_key(&jw, \"to_box\");      json_writer_string(&jw, to_box); }\n    if (to_input)    { json_writer_key(&jw, \"to_input\");    json_writer_string(&jw, to_input); }\n    json_writer_end(&jw);\n    return flush_line(w, &jw, buf);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_emit_push() — per-push dispatch attempt */\nint jsonl_emit_push(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                    const char *from_box, const char *to_box,\n                    const char *to_input, int slot_id,\n                    int n_bytes, const char *result)\n{\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    char buf[EVENT_BUF];\n    json_writer_t jw;\n    json_writer_init(&jw, buf, EVENT_BUF);\n    begin_event(&jw, \"push\", ts);\n    if (from_box) { json_writer_key(&jw, \"from_box\"); json_writer_string(&jw, from_box); }\n    if (to_box)   { json_writer_key(&jw, \"to_box\");   json_writer_string(&jw, to_box); }\n    if (to_input) { json_writer_key(&jw, \"to_input\"); json_writer_string(&jw, to_input); }\n    json_writer_key(&jw, \"slot_id\"); json_writer_int(&jw, slot_id);\n    json_writer_key(&jw, \"n_bytes\"); json_writer_int(&jw, n_bytes);\n    if (result)   { json_writer_key(&jw, \"result\");   json_writer_string(&jw, result); }\n    json_writer_end(&jw);\n    return flush_line(w, &jw, buf);\n}\n/* }}} */",

    "oldString":"void event_queue_slot_alloc(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            int slot_id, int cell_capacity, int n_cells,\n                            const char *owner_box, const char *owner_port)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_slot_alloc(q->writer, ts, slot_id, cell_capacity, n_cells,\n                          owner_box, owner_port);\n}\n/* }}} */",
    "newString":"void event_queue_slot_alloc(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            int slot_id, int cell_capacity, int n_cells,\n                            const char *owner_box, const char *owner_port)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_slot_alloc(q->writer, ts, slot_id, cell_capacity, n_cells,\n                          owner_box, owner_port);\n}\n\n/* Runtime mutation events (issue 319 / 248 self-construction). Same\n * direct-write path as the verbose events — graph mutations are\n * infrequent and the payload is variable-length string data that\n * doesn't fit cleanly into a fixed-size queue record. */\nvoid event_queue_box_create(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            const char *box_id, const char *kind,\n                            const char *lang, const char *ref,\n                            const char *fn)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_box_create(q->writer, ts, box_id, kind, lang, ref, fn);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_wire_add(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                          const char *from_box, const char *from_branch,\n                          const char *to_box, const char *to_input)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_wire_add(q->writer, ts, from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_push(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                      const char *from_box, const char *to_box,\n                      const char *to_input, int slot_id,\n                      int n_bytes, const char *result)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_push(q->writer, ts, from_box, to_box, to_input,\n                    slot_id, n_bytes, result);\n}\n/* }}} */",
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/014-event-queue.c"
  },
  "userType":"external",

}

        "input":{
          "old_string":"/* Slot allocator events (opt-in via SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1). Like\n * the value events, these bypass the queue and write directly so\n * the soramech-pool can emit them in a tight loop right after\n * graph_attach_runtime without inflating the queue with many\n * fixed-size records that all fire at the same instant. */\nvoid event_queue_slot_alloc (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int slot_id, int cell_capacity, int n_cells,\n                             const char *owner_box, const char *owner_port);\n/* }}} */",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"/* Slot allocator events (opt-in via SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1). Like\n * the value events, these bypass the queue and write directly so\n * the soramech-pool can emit them in a tight loop right after\n * graph_attach_runtime without inflating the queue with many\n * fixed-size records that all fire at the same instant. Issue 319\n * also emits one per slot when a runtime create_box allocates\n * input ports mid-run. */\nvoid event_queue_slot_alloc (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int slot_id, int cell_capacity, int n_cells,\n                             const char *owner_box, const char *owner_port);\n\n/* Runtime graph mutation events (issue 319 / 248 self-construction).\n * Always emitted when an active queue is present — mutations are\n * rare enough that they don't need a verbosity gate. The trio\n * brackets every runtime-create + runtime-connect + per-push\n * fan-out so the JSONL transcript captures the full\n * mutate-then-dispatch timeline. The `result` field on push\n * carries either \"ok\" or a short skip reason — invaluable for\n * diagnosing visibility races where the new box's fields aren't\n * yet seen by the producer's fan-out (see 319's status note). */\nvoid event_queue_box_create (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             const char *box_id, const char *kind,\n                             const char *lang, const char *ref,\n                             const char *fn);\n\nvoid event_queue_wire_add   (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             const char *from_box, const char *from_branch,\n                             const char *to_box, const char *to_input);\n\n/* Per-push event (opt-in via SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1, since pushes\n * are slot-level activity). */\nvoid event_queue_push       (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             const char *from_box, const char *to_box,\n                             const char *to_input, int slot_id,\n                             int n_bytes, const char *result);\n/* }}} */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/014-event-queue.h"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"

    "originalFile":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, pushes outputs to downstream input slots, and\n * spawns consumer tasks on input readiness.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <pthread.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box runtime state (spawn guard + optional output capture)\n     * lives in chunked-append chunks (see ctx_box_chunk_t in\n     * dispatch.c). The old flat-arrays-with-headroom model imposed\n     * a 4096-box runtime cap that issue 319's create_box could\n     * exceed; chunks remove the cap by growing on demand.\n     *\n     * Access goes through the private ctx_box_slot helper in\n     * dispatch.c; callers don't touch these directly. */\n    void                 *box_chunks_opaque;   /* ctx_box_chunk_t**, hidden type */\n    _Atomic unsigned int  n_box_chunks;\n    pthread_mutex_t       box_chunks_mu;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n\n    /* Optional run-log event queue (issue 311). When non-NULL, the\n     * dispatch action emits task_start + task_end events through\n     * it. NULL turns the per-task logging off; the runner emits\n     * run_start / run_end on its own. */\n    event_queue_t        *events;\n\n    /* Verbose-event gate (issue 311 SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1). The chunk back-reference\n * lets dispatch_action release the cell via ua_unref without\n * having to look it up by data pointer. */\nstruct ua_chunk;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    int                   task_id;   /* assigned at dispatch_spawn time */\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n\n    /* 304 placeholder — live count of outgoing wires that still\n     * carry an unconsumed value pushed by this task. The box-\n     * retirement consumer that reads this lands with the\n     * lifetime-tracking slice; for now the field is set to 0 on\n     * spawn and otherwise unread. Keeping it in the layout\n     * documents the intent and lets a future slice flip the\n     * read-it-and-act-on-it switch without changing the struct\n     * shape callers depend on. */\n    uint32_t              live_wire_count;\n\n    struct ua_chunk      *chunk;     /* set by dispatch_spawn; freed by dispatch_action */\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. Call after `graph_attach_runtime` so the per-box\n * runtime data is in place.\n *\n * `enable_output_capture` allocates `last_outputs` and\n * `last_output_sizes` so tests can inspect what each box wrote\n * after `pool_wait_quiescent`. */\nint  dispatch_ctx_init   (dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                          const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                          spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                          int enable_output_capture, char **err);\n\n/* Free per-box runtime arrays; does not touch the externally-owned\n * graph / slots / specs / pool fields. */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx);\n\n/* Read a previously-captured output (issue 319 follow-on: callers\n * no longer touch the per-box arrays directly because those moved\n * into private chunked storage). Returns the NUL-terminated bytes\n * if capture was enabled at init AND a previous task on `box_id`\n * wrote something; NULL otherwise. `*out_size` is filled with the\n * stored byte count on a hit. The returned pointer is valid until\n * the next capture for the same box or dispatch_ctx_destroy. */\nconst char *dispatch_captured_output(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                                     int box_id, int *out_size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Startup helpers */\n/* Walk every box and push any input-port literal values into the\n * corresponding input slot. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action.     "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/012-dispatch.c"
  },
  "userType":"external",
  "gitBranch":"master",

}

    "content":[{
        "name":"Edit",
        "input":{
          "old_string":"Six fixture checks at the moment:\n- `calc`            — single Lua `add → 42`\n- `hello`           — data → Lua, `greet → \"Hello, World!\"`\n- `comparator`      — `high` fires, `low` / `mid` don't\n- `iter-route`      — single-fire iterator picks `out_0` → `a`\n- `pipeline`        — five-box multilang chain\n- `pipeline file`   — verifies the file_write sink wrote\n  `\"11!\"` to `/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt`",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"Six fixture checks at the moment:\n- `calc`            — single Lua `add → 42`\n- `hello`           — data → Lua, `greet → \"Hello, World!\"`\n- `comparator`      — `high` fires, `low` / `mid` don't\n- `iter-route`      — single-fire iterator picks `out_0` → `a`\n- `pipeline`        — five-box multilang chain\n- `pipeline file`   — verifies the file_write sink wrote\n  `\"11!\"` to `/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt`\n\n### Runtime-mutation and per-push events — 2026-05-24\n\nThree new events extend the JSONL transcript to cover the\nruntime self-construction path from issue 319, which previously\nleft no trace in the log even with `SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`\nbecause the events fire from inside a spec's invoke rather than\nfrom the dispatch's task lifecycle.\n\n- **`box_create`** — fires from `runtime_create_box` after the\n  new box is published into the graph. Records id, kind, lang,\n  ref, fn. Always emits when an event queue is open (rare and\n  load-bearing — no verbosity gate).\n- **`wire_add`** — fires from `runtime_connect` after the\n  connection is appended to the producer's array. Records\n  from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input. Always emits.\n- **`slot_alloc`** (runtime variant) — fires from\n  `runtime_create_box`'s per-input-port slot allocation loop.\n  Same shape as the startup slot enumeration but for the\n  runtime path. Always emits.\n- **`push`** — fires from `push_one_connection` on every\n  attempt, with a `result` field carrying either `\"ok\"` or a\n  short skip reason (`no-to-box-idx`, `dst-null`,\n  `input-slots-null`, `to-input-out-of-range`, `push-failed`).\n  Opt-in via `SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1` — would be too noisy by\n  default. Crucial for diagnosing the latent visibility race\n  noted on 319's completed status: a `push` event with\n  `result=input-slots-null` is the immediately-recognisable\n  signature.\n\nThe runtime context that `dispatch_action` publishes via TLS\ngrew an `event_queue *` slot so the runtime builtins reach the\nsame writer the dispatch uses. The pool runner reads\n`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS` into a `ctx->log_slots` flag that gates\nboth the startup slot enumeration AND the per-push events —\none env var, one slot-level verbosity story.\n\nEnd-to-end check: running `319d-runtime-create` with\n`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1` produces a transcript where the\nmutation timeline is fully visible — `task_start →\nslot_alloc → box_create → wire_add → push(result=ok) →\ntask_submit → task_end → task_start → task_end`. If the\nvisibility race resurfaces under some build layout, the push\nevent flips to `result=input-slots-null` and the diagnosis is\nin the log without a rebuild.\n\nWhat's still ahead inside 311:\n- Lock-free Vyukov MPSC ring with sequence numbers — the\n  architecture doc's preferred design. The mutex queue is a\n  placeholder; upgrade once contention shows up.\n- JSONL normalizer for diff-based test verification (currently\n  the test harness uses substring matching against stderr).\n- Phase-3 demo map under `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/`.",

    "oldString":"Six fixture checks at the moment:\n- `calc`            — single Lua `add → 42`\n- `hello`           — data → Lua, `greet → \"Hello, World!\"`\n- `comparator`      — `high` fires, `low` / `mid` don't\n- `iter-route`      — single-fire iterator picks `out_0` → `a`\n- `pipeline`        — five-box multilang chain\n- `pipeline file`   — verifies the file_write sink wrote\n  `\"11!\"` to `/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt`",
    "newString":"Six fixture checks at the moment:\n- `calc`            — single Lua `add → 42`\n- `hello`           — data → Lua, `greet → \"Hello, World!\"`\n- `comparator`      — `high` fires, `low` / `mid` don't\n- `iter-route`      — single-fire iterator picks `out_0` → `a`\n- `pipeline`        — five-box multilang chain\n- `pipeline file`   — verifies the file_write sink wrote\n  `\"11!\"` to `/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt`\n\n### Runtime-mutation and per-push events — 2026-05-24\n\nThree new events extend the JSONL transcript to cover the\nruntime self-construction path from issue 319, which previously\nleft no trace in the log even with `SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`\nbecause the events fire from inside a spec's invoke rather than\nfrom the dispatch's task lifecycle.\n\n- **`box_create`** — fires from `runtime_create_box` after the\n  new box is published into the graph. Records id, kind, lang,\n  ref, fn. Always emits when an event queue is open (rare and\n  load-bearing — no verbosity gate).\n- **`wire_add`** — fires from `runtime_connect` after the\n  connection is appended to the producer's array. Records\n  from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input. Always emits.\n- **`slot_alloc`** (runtime variant) — fires from\n  `runtime_create_box`'s per-input-port slot allocation loop.\n  Same shape as the startup slot enumeration but for the\n  runtime path. Always emits.\n- **`push`** — fires from `push_one_connection` on every\n  attempt, with a `result` field carrying either `\"ok\"` or a\n  short skip reason (`no-to-box-idx`, `dst-null`,\n  `input-slots-null`, `to-input-out-of-range`, `push-failed`).\n  Opt-in via `SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1` — would be too noisy by\n  default. Crucial for diagnosing the latent visibility race\n  noted on 319's completed status: a `push` event with\n  `result=input-slots-null` is the immediately-recognisable\n  signature.\n\nThe runtime context that `dispatch_action` publishes via TLS\ngrew an `event_queue *` slot so the runtime builtins reach the\nsame writer the dispatch uses. The pool runner reads\n`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS` into a `ctx->log_slots` flag that gates\nboth the startup slot enumeration AND the per-push events —\none env var, one slot-level verbosity story.\n\nEnd-to-end check: running `319d-runtime-create` with\n`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1` produces a transcript where the\nmutation timeline is fully visible — `task_start →\nslot_alloc → box_create → wire_add → push(result=ok) →\ntask_submit → task_end → task_start → task_end`. If the\nvisibility race resurfaces under some build layout, the push\nevent flips to `result=input-slots-null` and the diagnosis is\nin the log without a rebuild.\n\nWhat's still ahead inside 311:\n- Lock-free Vyukov MPSC ring with sequence numbers — the\n  architecture doc's preferred design. The mutex queue is a\n  placeholder; upgrade once contention shows up.\n- JSONL normalizer for diff-based test verification (currently\n  the test harness uses substring matching against stderr).\n- Phase-3 demo map under `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/`.",

    "originalFile":"# Phase 3 Progress\n\nGoal: replace the Lua synchronous runner with a C thread pool runner\nthat executes box graphs in parallel.\n\nThe phase is fully designed; implementation is now underway.\nIssues 301–313 are the architectural specification. As each issue\nmoves into implementation, its row is marked \"in progress\"; on\ncompletion it's moved to `issues/completed/`.\n\nImplementation began **2026-05-12** with the 309 build scaffolding.\n\n## Issues\n\n| ID  | Title                                                       | Status   |\n|-----|-------------------------------------------------------------|----------|\n| 301 | thread pool lifecycle and per-worker initialization         | complete · pool + per-worker init/teardown hooks + priority queue |\n| 302 | per-task slot store with wire-held references               | complete · unified allocator + refcounted recycling on every byte path (slot cells, variable-size payloads, dispatch input/output buffers) + eager neighbor-merge + quiescence-trigger deep sweep |\n| 303 | language runtime spec (pluggable per-language invocation)   | complete · registry + per-worker init + pool hook + lang filtering |\n| 304 | task dispatch layer (C, replaces synchronous executor)      | complete · every routing kind, slab-allocated task structs, live_wire_count placeholder; works uniformly across every language including Bash |\n\n## Phase goal checklist\n\n- [x] SoraMech-owned task pool builds clean (3d-rts as design reference)\n- [x] Slot store unit-tested (single-value + ring buffer)\n- [x] C graph loader passes the project's existing maps\n- [x] Lua spec runs `tests/maps/hello` end-to-end\n- [x] C spec compiles and runs a fixed-signature box\n- [x] Bash spec runs an out-of-process box via persistent\n      socketpair + line-protocol\n- [x] Pool runner runs a multi-language map with concurrent workers\n- [x] Iterator box routes via dispatch layer (with multi-spawn\n      re-fire via N-cell pop slots and auto-re-spawn)\n- [x] Comparator box routes via dispatch layer (via spec output)\n- [x] Variable-size outputs work via the large-value heap\n- [x] `last-run.jsonl` written for every run\n- [ ] All 11 integration test maps pass\n- [ ] Phase 3 demo map runs and produces expected output\n- [ ] Phase 2 synchronous runner retired (`src/004-executor.lua`,\n      `src/007-runner-main.lua`, `src/003-loader.lua`, `drivers/*.sh`)\n\n## Implementation order suggestion\n\nDesigned to surface concrete artifacts early so subsequent issues can\nbuild on them.\n\n1. **309 (build system)** — top-level Makefile, vendored deps, empty\n   stubs for runner and specs. Opt-in\nunder SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1 (the same gate the startup slot\nenumeration uses) because every push attempt would be noisy by\ndefault.\n\nPlumbing: the runtime context that dispatch_action publishes via\nthread-local storage grew an event_queue * slot so the runtime\nbuiltins reach the same writer the dispatch uses. The pool\nrunner reads SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS into a ctx->log_slots flag that\ngates both the startup slot enumeration and the per-push events\nin one place.\n\nEnd-to-end check on 319d-runtime-create with SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS\nshows the full mutation timeline in the JSONL:\ntask_start → slot_alloc(runtime) → box_create → wire_add →\npush(result=ok) → task_submit → task_end → task_start → task_end.\nDefault (no env var) log stays lean: only the mutation events\nthat always-emit, plus the standard task lifecycle.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",

        "text":"Two new commits on top of the closeout series — the fixup that lands the missing \"complete\" status text into the three completed/ files, and the 311 instrumentation slice that gives 319's latent race a JSONL-visible signature. Working tree stays clean except for your pre-existing untracked WIP.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\n- The earlier `git mv` bug is one of those silent traps: `git mv source dest` stages a rename *based on the file's last-committed content* and moves the working file. If you have unstaged modifications on `source` when you run `git mv`, the rename captures HEAD content and your modifications sit unstaged on the destination path. The right pattern is `git add source` (stage the modification) THEN `git mv source dest` — or, equivalently, `git mv source dest` then `git add dest` to stage the modification on top. The closeout commits committed clean renames with stale content; the fixup commit lands the actual intent. Worth remembering as a generic git-hygiene rule.\n- The 319 latent race now has a **JSONL signature** rather than a fprintf-and-rebuild diagnosis loop. If it ever resurfaces, the transcript will literally show `{\"event\":\"push\", ..., \"result\":\"input-slots-null\"}` — no source code change needed to recognise it. That's exactly the kind of \"make the bug visible from the log alone\" payoff that justifies adding instrumentation events even when they don't drive a feature directly. The push-event design captures *every* skip reason as a distinct string, not just the one we care about, so other future races (`dst-null`, `to-input-out-of-range`) get the same diagnostic treatment for free.\n- The split between **always-emit mutation events** (box_create, wire_add, runtime slot_alloc) and **opt-in per-push events** (`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1`) is the right verbosity boundary. Mutations are O(graph edits), which the user controls and which are load-bearing for any audit log. Pushes are O(every wire fire), which is unbounded — gating them behind an env var keeps default runs cheap while making deep diagnosis one env var away.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\n311 stays in `issues/` (not moved to `completed/`) — its lock-free MPSC ring, JSONL normaliser, and phase-3 demo map are still open as recorded in the updated status block. If you want me to push toward closing any of those, or pick something else, say the word."

        "name":"Write",
        "input":{
          "content":"-- Phase 3 demo — runtime planner.\n--\n-- Receives a seed string; spawns three worker boxes mid-run via\n-- soramech.create_box, each running a different transformation\n-- function from src/worker.lua; wires its own output into each\n-- worker's `text` input port so the seed value fans out to all\n-- three runtime-built consumers.\n--\n-- After plan() returns its value, the dispatch's fan-out sees the\n-- three freshly-added connections on the planner's own\n-- connections array and pushes the return value into each\n-- worker's input slot — the new boxes fire under their own Lua\n-- spec on whichever pool worker picks them up. The whole\n-- planner-creates-workers-then-feeds-workers sequence is one\n-- task on the dispatch's perspective; the workers are three\n-- additional tasks that get spawned during the planner's fan-out.\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ M.plan\nfunction M.plan(seed_text)\n    local transformations = { \"uppercase\", \"reverse\", \"double_length\" }\n\n    -- Create one runtime box per transformation. The auto-generated\n    -- ids come back as strings; we capture them so the connect call\n    -- knows where to send each wire. Every create_box emits a\n    -- box_create event into the JSONL transcript, every connect\n    -- emits a wire_add event (issue 311 — runtime mutation events\n    -- always emit, no verbosity gate needed because they are rare\n    -- and load-bearing for the audit log).\n    for _, fn_name in ipairs(transformations) do\n        local worker_id = soramech.create_box{\n            kind = \"call\",\n            lang = \"lua\",\n            ref  = \"src/worker.lua\",\n            fn   = fn_name,\n            inputs = {\n                { name = \"text\", type = \"string\" }\n            }\n        }\n        soramech.connect{\n            from_box    = \"planner\",\n            from_branch = nil,\n            to_box      = worker_id,\n            to_input    = \"text\"\n        }\n    end\n\n    -- Return the seed verbatim — the dispatch fans this string to\n    -- each freshly-wired worker. Each worker's task then runs its\n    -- transformation on the same input.\n    return seed_text\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/completed/demos/phase-3-runtime-planner/src/planner.lua"
        },

          "content":"-- Phase 3 demo — runtime workers.\n--\n-- Three small transformation functions. The planner creates one\n-- runtime box per function via soramech.create_box{fn=...}. Each\n-- worker's task fires once with the same input the planner\n-- received; the output goes nowhere (no downstream wires are\n-- created from the worker), which is fine — the unwired-output\n-- rule discards it. The demo reads each worker's output from the\n-- JSONL transcript's task_output events under SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES.\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ M.uppercase\nfunction M.uppercase(text)\n    return \"uppercase: \" .. string.upper(text)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.reverse\nfunction M.reverse(text)\n    return \"reverse: \" .. string.reverse(text)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.double_length\n-- Length of the input, doubled — a small computation that's\n-- transparently different from the other two transformations so\n-- the demo's output reads as three clearly distinct workers.\nfunction M.double_length(text)\n    return \"double_length: \" .. tostring(#text * 2)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

    "userModified":false,
    "content":"-- Phase 3 demo — runtime workers.\n--\n-- Three small transformation functions. The planner creates one\n-- runtime box per function via soramech.create_box{fn=...}. Each\n-- worker's task fires once with the same input the planner\n-- received; the output goes nowhere (no downstream wires are\n-- created from the worker), which is fine — the unwired-output\n-- rule discards it. The demo reads each worker's output from the\n-- JSONL transcript's task_output events under SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES.\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ M.uppercase\nfunction M.uppercase(text)\n    return \"uppercase: \" .. string.upper(text)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.reverse\nfunction M.reverse(text)\n    return \"reverse: \" .. string.reverse(text)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.double_length\n-- Length of the input, doubled — a small computation that's\n-- transparently different from the other two transformations so\n-- the demo's output reads as three clearly distinct workers.\nfunction M.double_length(text)\n    return \"double_length: \" .. tostring(#text * 2)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/completed/demos/phase-3-runtime-planner/src/worker.lua"
  },

        "input":{
          "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# issues/completed/demos/phase-3-runtime-planner/run.sh\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: runs the phase-3 demo map, then\n# reads the JSONL transcript and prints a short story of what\n# happened — the input value, the runtime-spawned boxes, each\n# worker's distinct output, and a small statistics block at the\n# end. Demonstrates phase 3's headline capability (a Lua box\n# building more of the graph mid-run) alongside the JSONL\n# transcript layer that landed in issue 311.\n#\n# Convention: hard-coded ${DIR} with --dir override, every path\n# inside resolved against ${DIR}. No interactive input.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]] && [[ \"$1\" == \"--dir\" ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$2\"\nfi\nMAP=\"$DIR/issues/completed/demos/phase-3-runtime-planner\"\nLOG=\"/tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ sanity-check the runner binary exists\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"phase-3 demo: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run the map with full logging\necho \"=== Phase 3 demo — runtime planner ===\"\necho\nprintf \"Seed value (from boxes/seed.json):  \"\ngrep -o '\"value\":[[:space:]]*\"[^\"]*\"' \"$MAP/boxes/seed.json\" | head -1 | sed 's/\"value\":[[:space:]]*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"/\\1/'\necho\necho \"--- running the map (LOG_VALUES + LOG_SLOTS on) ---\"\nSORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1 SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1 \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$MAP\" 2>&1 \\\n    | grep -E \"soramech-pool: |→ \" \\\n    | sed 's/^/  /'\necho\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ extract_field — pull one field from a JSONL line\n# Crude regex extraction because the project's no-jq policy holds\n# here too. The JSONL lines are flat objects with primitive\n# values; one regex per field is enough for the demo's needs.\nextract_field() {\n    local line=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    echo \"$line\" | grep -oE \"\\\"$field\\\":\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" | head -1 | sed \"s/\\\"$field\\\":\\\"\\\\([^\\\"]*\\\\)\\\"/\\\\1/\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ story_from_jsonl — narrate what happened from the transcript\nstory_from_jsonl() {\n    if [[ ! -f \"$LOG\" ]]; then\n        echo \"  (no JSONL transcript at $LOG — did the runner write it?)\"\n        return\n    fi\n\n    echo \"--- runtime graph mutations ---\"\n    local n_created=0\n    while IFS= read -r line; do\n        local id  fn  ref\n        id=$(extract_field  \"$line\" \"box_id\")\n        fn=$(extract_field  \"$line\" \"fn\")\n        ref=$(extract_field \"$line\" \"ref\")\n        printf \"  + created box '%s' running %s() from %s\\n\" \"$id\" \"$fn\" \"$ref\"\n        n_created=$((n_created + 1))\n    done < <(grep '\"event\":\"box_create\"' \"$LOG\")\n    if [[ $n_created -eq 0 ]]; then\n        echo \"  (no box_create events — no runtime mutations happened)\"\n    fi\n    echo\n\n    local n_wired=0\n    while IFS= read -r line; do\n        local from to port\n        from=$(extract_field \"$line\" \"from_box\")\n        to=$(extract_field   \"$line\" \"to_box\")\n        port=$(extract_field \"$line\" \"to_input\")\n        printf \"  → wired '%s' → '%s'.%s\\n\" \"$from\" \"$to\" \"$port\"\n        n_wired=$((n_wired + 1))\n    done < <(grep '\"event\":\"wire_add\"' \"$LOG\")\n    echo\n\n    echo \"--- worker outputs (from task_output events) ---\"\n    # task_id 0 is the planner; tasks 1+ are the runtime workers.\n    grep '\"event\":\"task_output\"' \"$LOG\" \\\n        | grep -v '\"task_id\":0,' \\\n        | while IFS= read -r line; do\n            local data\n            data=$(echo \"$line\" | grep -oE '\"data\":\"[^\"]*\"' | head -1 | sed 's/\"data\":\"\\(.*\\)\"/\\1/')\n            printf \"  · %s\\n\" \"$data\"\n        done\n    echo\n\n    echo \"--- summary ---\"\n    local n_tasks\n    n_tasks=$(grep '\"event\":\"task_end\"' \"$LOG\" | wc -l)\n    local n_runtime_slots\n    n_runtime_slots=$(grep '\"event\":\"slot_alloc\"' \"$LOG\" | grep -v '<counter>' | grep -v '\"box\":\"seed\"' | grep -v '\"box\":\"planner\"' | wc -l)\n    local duration_us\n    duration_us=$(grep '\"event\":\"run_end\"' \"$LOG\" | grep -oE '\"duration_us\":[0-9]+' | head -1 | sed 's/\"duration_us\"://')\n    printf \"  tasks fired:                %d\\n\" \"$n_tasks\"\n    printf \"  runtime-allocated slots:    %d\\n\" \"$n_runtime_slots\"\n    printf \"  runtime-created boxes:      %d\\n\" \"$n_created\"\n    printf \"  runtime-added wires:        %d\\n\" \"$n_wired\"\n    printf \"  total run duration:         %s µs\\n\" \"${duration_us:-?}\"\n    echo\n}\nstory_from_jsonl\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ goodbye\necho \"Full JSONL transcript: $LOG\"\necho \"Re-run with:           $0\"\necho\n# }}}\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/completed/demos/phase-3-runtime-planner/run.sh"

No interactive input.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]] && [[ \"$1\" == \"--dir\" ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$2\"\nfi\nMAP=\"$DIR/issues/completed/demos/phase-3-runtime-planner\"\nLOG=\"/tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ sanity-check the runner binary exists\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"phase-3 demo: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run the map with full logging\necho \"=== Phase 3 demo — runtime planner ===\"\necho\nprintf \"Seed value (from boxes/seed.json):  \"\ngrep -o '\"value\":[[:space:]]*\"[^\"]*\"' \"$MAP/boxes/seed.json\" | head -1 | sed 's/\"value\":[[:space:]]*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"/\\1/'\necho\necho \"--- running the map (LOG_VALUES + LOG_SLOTS on) ---\"\nSORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1 SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1 \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$MAP\" 2>&1 \\\n    | grep -E \"soramech-pool: |→ \" \\\n    | sed 's/^/  /'\necho\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ extract_field — pull one field from a JSONL line\n# Crude regex extraction because the project's no-jq policy holds\n# here too. The JSONL lines are flat objects with primitive\n# values; one regex per field is enough for the demo's needs.\nextract_field() {\n    local line=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    echo \"$line\" | grep -oE \"\\\"$field\\\":\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" | head -1 | sed \"s/\\\"$field\\\":\\\"\\\\([^\\\"]*\\\\)\\\"/\\\\1/\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ story_from_jsonl — narrate what happened from the transcript\nstory_from_jsonl() {\n    if [[ ! -f \"$LOG\" ]]; then\n        echo \"  (no JSONL transcript at $LOG — did the runner write it?)\"\n        return\n    fi\n\n    echo \"--- runtime graph mutations ---\"\n    local n_created=0\n    while IFS= read -r line; do\n        local id  fn  ref\n        id=$(extract_field  \"$line\" \"box_id\")\n        fn=$(extract_field  \"$line\" \"fn\")\n        ref=$(extract_field \"$line\" \"ref\")\n        printf \"  + created box '%s' running %s() from %s\\n\" \"$id\" \"$fn\" \"$ref\"\n        n_created=$((n_created + 1))\n    done < <(grep '\"event\":\"box_create\"' \"$LOG\")\n    if [[ $n_created -eq 0 ]]; then\n        echo \"  (no box_create events — no runtime mutations happened)\"\n    fi\n    echo\n\n    local n_wired=0\n    while IFS= read -r line; do\n        local from to port\n        from=$(extract_field \"$line\" \"from_box\")\n        to=$(extract_field   \"$line\" \"to_box\")\n        port=$(extract_field \"$line\" \"to_input\")\n        printf \"  → wired '%s' → '%s'.%s\\n\" \"$from\" \"$to\" \"$port\"\n        n_wired=$((n_wired + 1))\n    done < <(grep '\"event\":\"wire_add\"' \"$LOG\")\n    echo\n\n    echo \"--- worker outputs (from task_output events) ---\"\n    # task_id 0 is the planner; tasks 1+ are the runtime workers.\n    grep '\"event\":\"task_output\"' \"$LOG\" \\\n        | grep -v '\"task_id\":0,' \\\n        | while IFS= read -r line; do\n            local data\n            data=$(echo \"$line\" | grep -oE '\"data\":\"[^\"]*\"' | head -1 | sed 's/\"data\":\"\\(.*\\)\"/\\1/')\n            printf \"  · %s\\n\" \"$data\"\n        done\n    echo\n\n    echo \"--- summary ---\"\n    local n_tasks\n    n_tasks=$(grep '\"event\":\"task_end\"' \"$LOG\" | wc -l)\n    local n_runtime_slots\n    n_runtime_slots=$(grep '\"event\":\"slot_alloc\"' \"$LOG\" | grep -v '<counter>' | grep -v '\"box\":\"seed\"' | grep -v '\"box\":\"planner\"' | wc -l)\n    local duration_us\n    duration_us=$(grep '\"event\":\"run_end\"' \"$LOG\" | grep -oE '\"duration_us\":[0-9]+' | head -1 | sed 's/\"duration_us\"://')\n    printf \"  tasks fired:                %d\\n\" \"$n_tasks\"\n    printf \"  runtime-allocated slots:    %d\\n\" \"$n_runtime_slots\"\n    printf \"  runtime-created boxes:      %d\\n\" \"$n_created\"\n    printf \"  runtime-added wires:        %d\\n\" \"$n_wired\"\n    printf \"  total run duration:         %s µs\\n\" \"${duration_us:-?}\"\n    echo\n}\nstory_from_jsonl\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ goodbye\necho \"Full JSONL transcript: $LOG\"\necho \"Re-run with:           $0\"\necho\n# }}}\n",
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/completed/demos/phase-3-runtime-planner/run.sh"
  },
  "userType":"external",
  "gitBranch":"master",
  "sessionId":"1c5a19da-96cd-4e77-88ea-625e76d201fa"
}

Both can earn their own tickets when someone wants them.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\n- The demo design landed on **deriving its narration from the transcript** rather than hand-coding output. That means every new event type 311 adds is one grep-and-extract away from being part of the demo's story. If a future change adds `reconfigure` events (issue 320), the demo could grow a \"reconfigured boxes\" section in one block of the script. The transcript is the single source of truth; the demo is a viewer.\n- Three tasks running on workers 0, 1, and 7 (per the JSONL `worker_idx` field) confirms the runtime-spawned boxes are genuinely parallel — they're not all queued behind one busy worker. The pool's task distribution treats freshly-created boxes as first-class, with no warm-up gap. That's a quiet correctness checkpoint the demo also passes implicitly.\n- The `PHASES=3` bump in `demo.sh` with no `PHASE=2` branch is a deliberate gap, not an oversight. Phase 2's product is the editor — not a runner-style demo — so there's no obvious \"demo\" mode for it. The numeric ceiling is \"highest phase that has a runnable demo,\" and skipping the middle reads more honestly than inventing a fake phase-2 demo just to fill the slot. The `else` clause's error message catches `./demo.sh 2` cleanly.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\nPhase 3 now has only two checklist items left on its goal sheet: \"All 11 integration test maps pass\" (5 of 11 named maps exist; the rest are gaps to fill incrementally) and \"Phase 2 synchronous runner retired\" (structural cleanup of `src/004-executor.lua` etc.).       "content":"             * tag, so parallel iterator tasks land in invocation\n             * order regardless of which worker finishes first. */\n            uint32_t idx = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n                                         (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs);\n            char branch[MAX_BRANCH_NAME];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size, idx, output_native) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_RANDOMIZER: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size, output_native);\n            }\n            /* Mix the monotonic counter so consecutive invocations\n             * don't go to consecutive branches. xorshift32-style,\n             * no crypto pretensions. */\n            uint32_t i = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id, UINT32_MAX);\n            uint32_t h = i;\n            h ^= h >> 16; h *= 0x85ebca6bu;\n            h ^= h >> 13; h *= 0xc2b2ae35u;\n            h ^= h >> 16;\n            uint32_t branch_idx = h % (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs;\n            char branch[MAX_BRANCH_NAME];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", branch_idx);\n            /* Randomizer is also multi-spawn-aware; pass i as tag so\n             * any downstream tagged slot still serves in order. */\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size, i, output_native) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_WEIGHTED: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1 ||\n                !b->routing.weights) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size, output_native);\n            }\n            /* Cumulative-band lookup against a counter scaled to a\n             * fixed precision. The last band absorbs floating-point\n             * rounding so the bands sum to the whole range. */\n            enum { WEIGHTED_PRECISION = 1000 };\n            uint32_t i = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n                                       (uint32_t)WEIGHTED_PRECISION);\n            double total = 0.0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < b->routing.n_outputs; k++) {\n                total += b->routing.weights[k];\n            }\n            if (total <= 0.0) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size, output_native);\n            }\n            int branch_idx = b->routing.n_outputs - 1;\n            double acc = 0.0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < b->routing.n_outputs; k++) {\n                acc += (b->routing.weights[k] / total) * WEIGHTED_PRECISION;\n                if ((double)i < acc) { branch_idx = k; break; }\n            }\n            char branch[MAX_BRANCH_NAME];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%d\", branch_idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size, i, output_native) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR: {\n            /* Argmin over downstream slot fill levels: pick the\n             * output branch whose busiest consumer slot is least\n             * loaded, so load spreads across the downstream stages.\n             * For multi-consumer branches the branch's \"load\" is\n             * the max fill across its consumers — the branch is\n             * only as fast as its slowest stage. Use it both as the rotation\n             * offset (so ties between equally-loaded branches break\n             * in round-robin order, not always toward index 0) AND\n             * as the tag carried on the push (so downstream tagged\n             * slots still serve in invocation order). */\n            uint32_t tag = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n                                         UINT32_MAX);\n            int best_branch  = -1;\n            int32_t best_max = INT32_MAX;\n            for (int step = 0; step < b->routing.n_outputs; step++) {\n                int k = (int)(((uint32_t)step + tag) %\n                              (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs);\n                char want[MAX_BRANCH_NAME];\n                snprintf(want, sizeof want, \"out_%d\", k);\n                int32_t this_max = 0;\n                int found_any = 0;\n                for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) {\n                    const connection_t *c = &b->connections[j];\n                    if (!c->from_branch ||\n                        strcmp(c->from_branch, want) != 0) continue;\n                    int dst = c->to_box_idx;\n                    if (dst < 0) continue;\n                    const box_t *db = graph_box(ctx->graph, dst);\n                    int port = c->to_input_idx;",

          "new_string":"-- {{{ valid_routing_kinds\n-- Issue 233's unified `routing` field. Six kinds shipped:\n--   plain       — single output port, fan to every wire\n--   comparator  — numeric threshold(s), pick lt/eq/gt or named bands\n--   iterator    — round-robin over n_outputs ports, multi-spawn\n--   randomizer  — hash(counter) mod n_outputs (issue 240)\n--   weighted    — cumulative-band lookup over weights (issue 241)\n--   distributor — argmin over downstream slot fill (issue 242)\nlocal valid_routing_kinds = {\n    plain       = true,\n    comparator  = true,\n    iterator    = true,\n    randomizer  = true,\n    weighted    = true,\n    distributor = true,\n}\n-- }}}",

        else\n                        local last = nil\n                        for i, t in ipairs(r.thresholds) do\n                            if type(t) ~= \"number\" then\n                                err(errors, \"comparator 'routing.thresholds[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a number\")\n                                break\n                            elseif last ~= nil and t < last then\n                                err(errors, \"comparator 'routing.thresholds' must be non-decreasing \" ..\n                                    \"(saw \" .. tostring(last) .. \" then \" .. tostring(t) .. \")\")\n                                break\n                            end\n                            last = t\n                        end\n                    end\n                elseif         end\n            elseif r.kind == \"randomizer\" or r.kind == \"distributor\" then\n                -- Same shape as iterator: a positive-integer\n                -- n_outputs. array\")\n                end\n            elseif r.kind == \"iterator\" then\n                is_routing_primitive = true\n                if type(r.n_outputs) ~= \"number\"\n                   or r.n_outputs < 1\n                   or r.n_outputs ~= math.floor(r.n_outputs) then\n                    err(errors, \"iterator routing requires 'routing.n_outputs' to be a positive integer\")\n                end\n            elseif r.kind == \"randomizer\" or r.kind == \"distributor\" then\n                -- Same shape as iterator: a positive-integer\n                -- n_outputs. Randomizer (issue 240) and distributor\n                -- (issue 242) share the counter-driven dispatch\n                -- machinery iterator uses, just with a different\n                -- picker.\n                if type(r.n_outputs) ~= \"number\"\n                   or r.n_outputs < 1\n                   or r.n_outputs ~= math.floor(r.n_outputs) then\n                    err(errors, r.kind .. \" routing requires 'routing.n_outputs' to be a positive integer\")\n                end\n            elseif r.kind == \"weighted\" then\n                -- Issue 241: weights is a non-empty array of\n                -- non-negative numbers.     "newString":"    if (strcmp(kind, \"comparator\") == 0) {\n        out->kind = ROUTING_COMPARATOR;\n        out->n_outputs = 3;          /* lt/eq/gt for legacy form */\n        out->n_thresholds = 0;\n        out->thresholds   = NULL;\n        /* Issue 243 — preferred shape: a non-empty `thresholds`\n         * array carves N+1 bands. Falls back to the single\n         * `comparand` (legacy lt/eq/gt) when thresholds is absent.\n         * If both are present, thresholds wins and comparand is\n         * ignored. */\n        json_node_t *t_arr = json_object_get(r, \"thresholds\");\n        if (t_arr) {\n            if (json_kind(t_arr) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator 'thresholds' must be an array\", box_id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            int nt = json_array_size(t_arr);\n            if (nt == 0) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator 'thresholds' must be non-empty\", box_id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            double *arr = malloc((size_t)nt * sizeof(double));\n            if (!arr) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n            double prev = 0.0;\n            for (int i = 0; i < nt; i++) {\n                json_node_t *e = json_array_at(t_arr, i);\n                if (!e || json_kind(e) != JSON_NUMBER) {\n                    free(arr);\n                    *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator thresholds[%d] is not a number\",\n                                   box_id, i);\n                    return -1;\n                }\n                double v = json_number_value(e);\n                if (i > 0 && v < prev) {\n                    free(arr);\n                    *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator thresholds must be non-decreasing \"\n                                   \"(thresholds[%d]=%g < thresholds[%d]=%g)\",\n                                   box_id, i, v, i - 1, prev);\n                    return -1;\n                }\n                arr[i] = v;\n                prev   = v;\n            }\n            out->thresholds   = arr;\n            out->n_thresholds = nt;\n            out->n_outputs    = nt + 1;\n            return 0;\n        }\n        json_node_t *c = json_object_get(r, \"comparand\");\n        if (!c) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator routing missing 'comparand' or 'thresholds'\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (json_kind(c) == JSON_NUMBER) {\n            out->comparand = json_number_value(c);\n        } else if (json_kind(c) == JSON_STRING) {\n            /* Issue 233 example shows comparand as a string;\n             * tolerate either form, parse the string as a double. */\n            const char *s = json_string_value(c);\n            char *endp = NULL;\n            out->comparand = strtod(s, &endp);\n            if (endp == s) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparand '%s' is not a number\", box_id, s);\n                return -1;\n            }\n        } else {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparand must be number or string\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        return 0;\n    }",

Falls back to the single\n         * `comparand` (legacy lt/eq/gt) when thresholds is absent.\n         * If both are present, thresholds wins and comparand is\n         * ignored. */\n        json_node_t *t_arr = json_object_get(r, \"thresholds\");\n        if (t_arr) {\n            if (json_kind(t_arr) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator 'thresholds' must be an array\", box_id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            int nt = json_array_size(t_arr);\n            if (nt == 0) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator 'thresholds' must be non-empty\", box_id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            double *arr = malloc((size_t)nt * sizeof(double));\n            if (!arr) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n            double prev = 0.0;\n            for (int i = 0; i < nt; i++) {\n                json_node_t *e = json_array_at(t_arr, i);\n                if (!e || json_kind(e) != JSON_NUMBER) {\n                    free(arr);\n                    *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator thresholds[%d] is not a number\",\n                                   box_id, i);\n                    return -1;\n                }\n                double v = json_number_value(e);\n                if (i > 0 && v < prev) {\n                    free(arr);\n                    *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator thresholds must be non-decreasing \"\n                                   \"(thresholds[%d]=%g < thresholds[%d]=%g)\",\n                                   box_id, i, v, i - 1, prev);\n                    return -1;\n                }\n                arr[i] = v;\n                prev   = v;\n            }\n            out->thresholds   = arr;\n            out->n_thresholds = nt;\n            out->n_outputs    = nt + 1;\n            return 0;\n        }\n        json_node_t *c = json_object_get(r, \"comparand\");\n        if (!c) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator routing missing 'comparand' or 'thresholds'\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (json_kind(c) == JSON_NUMBER) {\n            out->comparand = json_number_value(c);\n        } else if (json_kind(c) == JSON_STRING) {\n            /* Issue 233 example shows comparand as a string;\n             * tolerate either form, parse the string as a double. */\n            const char *s = json_string_value(c);\n            char *endp = NULL;\n            out->comparand = strtod(s, &endp);\n            if (endp == s) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparand '%s' is not a number\", box_id, s);\n                return -1;\n            }\n        } else {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparand must be number or string\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        return 0;\n    }",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.c"

    "content":[{
        "name":"Edit",
        "input":{
          "old_string":"        case ROUTING_COMPARATOR: {\n            double v = parse_double(out_bytes, out_size);\n            const char *branch =\n                (v < b->routing.comparand) ? \"lt\" :\n                (v > b->routing.comparand) ? \"gt\" : \"eq\";\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size, 0, output_native) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"        case ROUTING_COMPARATOR: {\n            double v = parse_double(out_bytes, out_size);\n            /* Issue 243 — multi-band comparator: when thresholds is\n             * set, carve N+1 bands and emit on the matching port.\n             * Doubled adjacent thresholds (t_i == t_{i+1}) carve a\n             * zero-width equality band. Branch-name format strings:\n             *   \"below_<t0>\" / \"eq_<t>\" / \"between_<a>_<b>\" / \"above_<tN-1>\"\n             * Numbers formatted with %g (trims trailing zeros for\n             * integer-valued doubles; the canvas + inspector use the\n             * same formatter so wires lookup matches). When thresholds\n             * is unset the picker falls back to the legacy lt/eq/gt\n             * single-comparand shape. */\n            char branch[MAX_BRANCH_NAME];\n            if (b->routing.n_thresholds > 0 && b->routing.thresholds) {\n                const double *t  = b->routing.thresholds;\n                int           nt = b->routing.n_thresholds;\n                if (v < t[0]) {\n                    snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"below_%g\", t[0]);\n                } else if (v > t[nt - 1]) {\n                    snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"above_%g\", t[nt - 1]);\n                } else {\n                    /* Walk doubled-pair equality bands first; any\n                     * remaining open interval is a between band. */\n                    int matched = 0;\n                    for (int i = 0; i + 1 < nt; i++) {\n                        if (t[i] == t[i + 1] && v == t[i]) {\n                            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"eq_%g\", t[i]);\n                            matched = 1;\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    }\n                    if (!matched) {\n                        for (int i = 0; i + 1 < nt; i++) {\n                            if (t[i] == t[i + 1]) continue;   /* zero-width */\n                            if (v > t[i] && v < t[i + 1]) {\n                                snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"between_%g_%g\",\n                                         t[i], t[i + 1]);\n                                matched = 1;\n                                break;\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                    if (!matched) {\n                        /* Value sits exactly on a non-doubled\n                         * threshold. Convention: pick the\n                         * less-than-or-equal side (the lower\n                         * adjacent band) so x == t[i] lands in\n                         * the band that ENDS at t[i]. */\n                        for (int i = 0; i < nt; i++) {\n                            if (v == t[i]) {\n                                if (i == 0) {\n                                    snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"below_%g\", t[0]);\n                                } else if (t[i - 1] == t[i]) {\n                                    /* doubled — already handled above */\n                                    snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"eq_%g\", t[i]);\n                                } else {\n                                    snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"between_%g_%g\",\n                                             t[i - 1], t[i]);\n                                }\n                                matched = 1;\n                                break;\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                    if (!matched) {\n                        /* Should be unreachable given the dichotomy\n                         * checks above; fall back to plain so a\n                         * pathological case doesn't drop the wire. */\n                        return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size, output_native);\n                    }\n                }\n                return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size, 0, output_native) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n            }\n            const char *legacy_branch =\n                (v < b->routing.comparand) ? \"lt\" :\n                (v > b->routing.comparand) ? \"gt\" : \"eq\";\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, legacy_branch, out_bytes, out_size, 0, output_native) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/012-dispatch.c"
        },
        "caller":{

          "new_string":"  // {{{ box_height\n  // Per-kind output-port count drives the row count. The\n  // single-output-per-box rule (issue 218) is the default;\n  // exceptions: comparator (3 lt/eq/gt or N+1 band ports per\n  // 243), iterator / randomizer / distributor (n_outputs ports\n  // per 233/240/242), weighted (weights.length ports per 241),\n  // map (declared outputs[] per 248), sink (zero per 226).\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n_in  = visible_inputs(box).length;\n    const rk    = box.routing && box.routing.kind;\n    let n_out;\n    if (box.has_output === false) {\n      n_out = 0;\n    } else if (box.kind === 'map') {\n      n_out = (box.outputs || []).length;\n    } else if (rk === 'iterator' || rk === 'randomizer' || rk === 'distributor') {\n      n_out = (box.routing && box.routing.n_outputs) || 1;\n    } else if (rk === 'weighted') {\n      n_out = (box.routing && box.routing.weights ? box.routing.weights.length : 0) || 1;\n    } else if (rk === 'comparator') {\n      // Issue 243: multi-band comparator carves N+1 bands from N\n      // thresholds. Legacy single-comparand stays at 3 (lt/eq/gt).\n      const ts = box.routing && box.routing.thresholds;\n      n_out = Array.isArray(ts) && ts.length > 0 ? ts.length + 1 : 3;\n    } else {\n      n_out = 1;\n    }\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + Math.max(n_in, n_out) * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ comparator_band_names\n  // Builds the multi-band comparator's output port name list\n  // (issue 243). N thresholds → N+1 names. Doubled adjacent\n  // thresholds (t_i == t_{i+1}) collapse one between band into\n  // an equality band named `eq_<t>`. The number formatter matches\n  // the C dispatch's `%g` so wire from_branch strings match\n  // exactly between the loader's parsed names and the canvas's\n  // rendered names. Returns the array of strings in port order.\n  function comparator_band_names(thresholds) {\n    const ts = (thresholds || []).slice();\n    if (ts.length === 0) return ['lt', 'eq', 'gt'];\n    const fmt = (n) => {\n      // Mirror C's %g: trim trailing zeros, no fixed-decimal cap\n      // for integers. JS's default toString matches %g closely\n      // enough for typical threshold ranges.\n      const s = Number(n).toString();\n      return s;\n    };\n    const names = ['below_' + fmt(ts[0])];\n    for (let i = 0; i + 1 < ts.length; i++) {\n      if (ts[i] === ts[i + 1]) {\n        names.push('eq_' + fmt(ts[i]));\n      } else {\n        names.push('between_' + fmt(ts[i]) + '_' + fmt(ts[i + 1]));\n      }\n    }\n    names.push('above_' + fmt(ts[ts.length - 1]));\n    return names;\n  }\n  // }}}",

The\n  // single-output-per-box rule (issue 218) is the default;\n  // exceptions: comparator (3 lt/eq/gt or N+1 band ports per\n  // 243), iterator / randomizer / distributor (n_outputs ports\n  // per 233/240/242), weighted (weights.length ports per 241),\n  // map (declared outputs[] per 248), sink (zero per 226).\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n_in  = visible_inputs(box).length;\n    const rk    = box.routing && box.routing.kind;\n    let n_out;\n    if (box.has_output === false) {\n      n_out = 0;\n    } else if (box.kind === 'map') {\n      n_out = (box.outputs || []).length;\n    } else if (rk === 'iterator' || rk === 'randomizer' || rk === 'distributor') {\n      n_out = (box.routing && box.routing.n_outputs) || 1;\n    } else if (rk === 'weighted') {\n      n_out = (box.routing && box.routing.weights ? box.routing.weights.length : 0) || 1;\n    } else if (rk === 'comparator') {\n      // Issue 243: multi-band comparator carves N+1 bands from N\n      // thresholds.
