          "old_string":"    // Comparator routing exposes one number knob — the value the\n    // output is compared against. The mode dropdown already\n    // declared the kind; the inspector just needs the value here.\n    // Plain routing has no per-kind control.\n    if (routing_kind(box) === 'comparator') {\n      const cmp_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      cmp_inp.type        = 'number';\n      cmp_inp.value       = String((box.routing && box.routing.comparand) ?? 0);\n      cmp_inp.placeholder = 'number';\n      cmp_inp.style.cssText = 'width:100%;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      cmp_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n        const v = parseFloat(cmp_inp.value);\n        if (!isNaN(v)) set_comparand(v);\n      });\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('comparand', cmp_inp));\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"    // Per-kind controls. Plain has no per-kind knob; comparator,\n    // randomizer, weighted, distributor each carry their own.\n    const rk = routing_kind(box);\n    if (rk === 'comparator') {\n      // Issue 233 single-comparand UI stays the default; issue 243\n      // adds an inline thresholds editor underneath. The two\n      // schema-side fields are mutually exclusive — the loader\n      // prefers `thresholds` when both are present. The editor\n      // mirrors that: typing into the threshold list switches the\n      // box to multi-band mode (comparand removed), clearing the\n      // list returns to single-comparand mode (thresholds removed).\n      const cmp_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      cmp_inp.type        = 'number';\n      cmp_inp.value       = String((box.routing && box.routing.comparand) ?? 0);\n      cmp_inp.placeholder = 'number';\n      cmp_inp.style.cssText = 'width:100%;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      cmp_inp.disabled = Array.isArray(box.routing && box.routing.thresholds)\n                         && box.routing.thresholds.length > 0;\n      cmp_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n        const v = parseFloat(cmp_inp.value);\n        if (!isNaN(v)) set_comparand(v);\n      });\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('comparand', cmp_inp));\n\n      // Multi-band threshold list (issue 243). Comma-separated\n      // numbers in a text input keeps the UX minimal; a richer\n      // sortable list with +/− buttons can land later if the\n      // textarea becomes painful. Doubled adjacent values mark\n      // zero-width equality bands (e.g. \"3,3,7,7\" gives the\n      // < 3 / == 3 / 3<x<7 / == 7 / > 7 layout).\n      const ts_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      ts_inp.type        = 'text';\n      ts_inp.placeholder = 'e.g. 3, 7, 11 (multi-band)';\n      ts_inp.value       = Array.isArray(box.routing && box.routing.thresholds)\n                             ? box.routing.thresholds.join(', ')\n                             : '';\n      ts_inp.style.cssText = 'width:100%;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      ts_inp.addEventListener('change', () => set_thresholds(ts_inp.value));\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('thresholds', ts_inp));\n\n      const ts_note = document.createElement('div');\n      ts_note.style.cssText = 'font-size:10px;color:#6c72a0;margin-top:4px;';\n      ts_note.textContent = 'comma-separated, non-decreasing. doubled values carve equality bands.';\n      fields.appendChild(ts_note);\n    } else if (rk === 'randomizer' || rk === 'distributor') {\n      // Same n_outputs control iterator uses, but the routing\n      // semantics are different — randomizer (240) picks branches\n      // pseudo-randomly via a hashed counter; distributor (242)\n      // picks the least-busy downstream branch by reading slot\n      // fill levels at dispatch time.\n      const n_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      n_inp.type        = 'number';\n      n_inp.min         = '1';\n      n_inp.value       = String((box.routing && box.routing.n_outputs) || 2);\n      n_inp.style.cssText = 'width:80px;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      n_inp.addEventListener('change', () => {\n        const v = parseInt(n_inp.value, 10);\n        if (!isNaN(v) && v >= 1) set_n_outputs(v);\n      });\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('n_outputs', n_inp));\n    } else if (rk === 'weighted') {\n      // Issue 241: weights array editor. Minimum viable shape is\n      // a comma-separated textbox; same upgrade path as the\n      // multi-band thresholds list — replace with sliders later\n      // if a real visual band UI earns its keep. Non-negative\n      // numbers only; the dispatch normalises at run time so\n      // they don't have to sum to 1.0.\n      const ws = (box.routing && box.routing.weights) || [];\n      const w_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      w_inp.type        = 'text';\n      w_inp.placeholder = 'e.g. 0.8, 0.2';\n      w_inp.value       = ws.join(', ');\n      w_inp.style.cssText = 'width:100%;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      w_inp.addEventListener('change', () => set_weights(w_inp.value));\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('weights', w_inp));\n\n      const w_note = document.createElement('div');\n      w_note.style.cssText = 'font-size:10px;color:#6c72a0;margin-top:4px;';\n      w_note.textContent = 'comma-separated non-negative numbers. dispatch normalises to a probability table.';\n      fields.appendChild(w_note);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}",

    "oldString":"    // Comparator routing exposes one number knob — the value the\n    // output is compared against. The mode dropdown already\n    // declared the kind; the inspector just needs the value here.\n    // Plain routing has no per-kind control.\n    if (routing_kind(box) === 'comparator') {\n      const cmp_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      cmp_inp.type        = 'number';\n      cmp_inp.value       = String((box.routing && box.routing.comparand) ?? 0);\n      cmp_inp.placeholder = 'number';\n      cmp_inp.style.cssText = 'width:100%;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      cmp_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n        const v = parseFloat(cmp_inp.value);\n        if (!isNaN(v)) set_comparand(v);\n      });\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('comparand', cmp_inp));\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}",
    "newString":"    // Per-kind controls. Plain has no per-kind knob; comparator,\n    // randomizer, weighted, distributor each carry their own.\n    const rk = routing_kind(box);\n    if (rk === 'comparator') {\n      // Issue 233 single-comparand UI stays the default; issue 243\n      // adds an inline thresholds editor underneath. The two\n      // schema-side fields are mutually exclusive — the loader\n      // prefers `thresholds` when both are present. The editor\n      // mirrors that: typing into the threshold list switches the\n      // box to multi-band mode (comparand removed), clearing the\n      // list returns to single-comparand mode (thresholds removed).\n      const cmp_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      cmp_inp.type        = 'number';\n      cmp_inp.value       = String((box.routing && box.routing.comparand) ?? 0);\n      cmp_inp.placeholder = 'number';\n      cmp_inp.style.cssText = 'width:100%;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      cmp_inp.disabled = Array.isArray(box.routing && box.routing.thresholds)\n                         && box.routing.thresholds.length > 0;\n      cmp_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n        const v = parseFloat(cmp_inp.value);\n        if (!isNaN(v)) set_comparand(v);\n      });\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('comparand', cmp_inp));\n\n      // Multi-band threshold list (issue 243). Comma-separated\n      // numbers in a text input keeps the UX minimal; a richer\n      // sortable list with +/− buttons can land later if the\n      // textarea becomes painful. Doubled adjacent values mark\n      // zero-width equality bands (e.g. \"3,3,7,7\" gives the\n      // < 3 / == 3 / 3<x<7 / == 7 / > 7 layout).\n      const ts_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      ts_inp.type        = 'text';\n      ts_inp.placeholder = 'e.g. 3, 7, 11 (multi-band)';\n      ts_inp.value       = Array.isArray(box.routing && box.routing.thresholds)\n                             ? box.routing.thresholds.join(', ')\n                             : '';\n      ts_inp.style.cssText = 'width:100%;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      ts_inp.addEventListener('change', () => set_thresholds(ts_inp.value));\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('thresholds', ts_inp));\n\n      const ts_note = document.createElement('div');\n      ts_note.style.cssText = 'font-size:10px;color:#6c72a0;margin-top:4px;';\n      ts_note.textContent = 'comma-separated, non-decreasing. doubled values carve equality bands.';\n      fields.appendChild(ts_note);\n    } else if (rk === 'randomizer' || rk === 'distributor') {\n      // Same n_outputs control iterator uses, but the routing\n      // semantics are different — randomizer (240) picks branches\n      // pseudo-randomly via a hashed counter; distributor (242)\n      // picks the least-busy downstream branch by reading slot\n      // fill levels at dispatch time.\n      const n_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      n_inp.type        = 'number';\n      n_inp.min         = '1';\n      n_inp.value       = String((box.routing && box.routing.n_outputs) || 2);\n      n_inp.style.cssText = 'width:80px;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      n_inp.addEventListener('change', () => {\n        const v = parseInt(n_inp.value, 10);\n        if (!isNaN(v) && v >= 1) set_n_outputs(v);\n      });\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('n_outputs', n_inp));\n    } else if (rk === 'weighted') {\n      // Issue 241: weights array editor. Minimum viable shape is\n      // a comma-separated textbox; same upgrade path as the\n      // multi-band thresholds list — replace with sliders later\n      // if a real visual band UI earns its keep. Non-negative\n      // numbers only; the dispatch normalises at run time so\n      // they don't have to sum to 1.0.\n      const ws = (box.routing && box.routing.weights) || [];\n      const w_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      w_inp.type        = 'text';\n      w_inp.placeholder = 'e.g. 0.8, 0.2';\n      w_inp.value       = ws.join(', ');\n      w_inp.style.cssText = 'width:100%;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      w_inp.addEventListener('change', () => set_weights(w_inp.value));\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('weights', w_inp));\n\n      const w_note = document.createElement('div');\n      w_note.style.cssText = 'font-size:10px;color:#6c72a0;margin-top:4px;';\n      w_note.textContent = 'comma-separated non-negative numbers. dispatch normalises to a probability table.';\n      fields.appendChild(w_note);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}",

    "oldString":"  // {{{ async function set_comparand()\n  async function set_comparand(n) {\n    if (!current_box || routing_kind(current_box) !== 'comparator') return;\n    current_box.routing.comparand = n;\n    await save();\n  }\n  // }}}",
    "newString":"  // {{{ async function set_comparand()\n  async function set_comparand(n) {\n    if (!current_box || routing_kind(current_box) !== 'comparator') return;\n    current_box.routing.comparand = n;\n    await save();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ async function set_thresholds()\n  // Issue 243 — multi-band-comparator thresholds setter. Parses a\n  // comma-separated text input into a numeric array; an empty\n  // input restores single-comparand mode (clears the thresholds\n  // field so the loader's legacy path runs). Non-decreasing is\n  // enforced by sorting silently — if the user typed \"7, 3\" we\n  // store \"3, 7\". Changing thresholds renames every output\n  // port (the band names embed the threshold values), so this\n  // severs all outgoing wires the same way iterator's\n  // n_outputs change does.\n  async function set_thresholds(text) {\n    if (!current_box || routing_kind(current_box) !== 'comparator') return;\n    const trimmed = String(text || '').trim();\n    if (trimmed === '') {\n      // Empty input → single-comparand mode. Drop the array.\n      if ('thresholds' in (current_box.routing || {})) {\n        await sever_output_wires();\n        delete current_box.routing.thresholds;\n        await save();\n        Canvas.mark_dirty();\n        show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n    const nums = trimmed.split(',')\n      .map(s => parseFloat(s.trim()))\n      .filter(n => !isNaN(n));\n    if (nums.length === 0) return;\n    nums.sort((a, b) => a - b);\n    await sever_output_wires();\n    current_box.routing.thresholds = nums;\n    // Remove the legacy field so the loader picks the\n    // multi-band path unambiguously.\n    delete current_box.routing.comparand;\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ async function set_weights()\n  // Issue 241 — weighted routing weights setter. Parses a\n  // comma-separated text input into a non-negative number array.\n  // Changing the array length changes the n_out shape (one port\n  // per weight), so this severs all outgoing wires.\n  async function set_weights(text) {\n    if (!current_box || routing_kind(current_box) !== 'weighted') return;\n    const trimmed = String(text || '').trim();\n    if (trimmed === '') return;\n    const nums = trimmed.split(',')\n      .map(s => parseFloat(s.trim()))\n      .filter(n => !isNaN(n) && n >= 0);\n    if (nums.length === 0) return;\n    await sever_output_wires();\n    current_box.routing.weights = nums;\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n  // }}}",

Changing thresholds renames every output\n  // port (the band names embed the threshold values), so this\n  // severs all outgoing wires the same way iterator's\n  // n_outputs change does.\n  async function set_thresholds(text) {\n    if (!current_box || routing_kind(current_box) !== 'comparator') return;\n    const trimmed = String(text || '').trim();\n    if (trimmed === '') {\n      // Empty input → single-comparand mode. Drop the array.\n      if ('thresholds' in (current_box.routing || {})) {\n        await sever_output_wires();\n        delete current_box.routing.thresholds;\n        await save();\n        Canvas.mark_dirty();\n        show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n    const nums = trimmed.split(',')\n      .map(s => parseFloat(s.trim()))\n      .filter(n => !isNaN(n));\n    if (nums.length === 0) return;\n    nums.sort((a, b) => a - b);\n    await sever_output_wires();\n    current_box.routing.thresholds = nums;\n    // Remove the legacy field so the loader picks the\n    // multi-band path unambiguously.\n    delete current_box.routing.comparand;\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ async function set_weights()\n  // Issue 241 — weighted routing weights setter. Parses a\n  // comma-separated text input into a non-negative number array.\n  // Changing the array length changes the n_out shape (one port\n  // per weight), so this severs all outgoing wires.\n  async function set_weights(text) {\n    if (!current_box || routing_kind(current_box) !== 'weighted') return;\n    const trimmed = String(text || '').trim();\n    if (trimmed === '') return;\n    const nums = trimmed.split(',')\n      .map(s => parseFloat(s.trim()))\n      .filter(n => !isNaN(n) && n >= 0);\n    if (nums.length === 0) return;\n    await sever_output_wires();\n    current_box.routing.weights = nums;\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n  // }}}",

```json
{
  "uuid":"8f6a1b8a-2eb6-4a57-a38f-a7dbfeb34aa8",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T21:00:41.560Z",
  "sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6faceda2-2974-4e7e-8f16-aebffdcb50ca",
  "parentUuid":"6faceda2-2974-4e7e-8f16-aebffdcb50ca",
  "entrypoint":"cli",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "promptId":"63b159d2-4086-4628-8aff-69f6de074d0b",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "content":"1\t# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n2\t#\n3\t# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n4\t# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n5\t# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n6\t# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n7\t#\n8\t# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n9\t# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n10\t# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n11\t# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n12\t#\n13\t# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n14\t# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n15\t# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n16\t# those issues land.\n17\t\n18\t# {{{ Resolve project root\n19\tDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n20\t# }}}\n21\t\n22\t# {{{ Toolchain & flags\n23\tCC      ?= gcc\n24\t\n25\t# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n26\t# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\n27\tCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n28\t\n29\t# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\n30\tifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n31\t  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\n32\telse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n33\t  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\n34\telse\n35\t  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\n36\tendif\n37\t\n38\tLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n39\t# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n40\t# plugins. As\n51\t# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n52\t# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\n53\tPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n54\t  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n55\t  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n56\t  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n57\t\n58\tPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n59\t\n60\t# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n61\t# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n62\t# src/009-slot-store.c).           "old_string":"# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\n#\n# -MMD -MP makes gcc emit a `.d` file alongside each `.o` recording\n# every header that translation unit included. The `-include $(DEPS)`\n# below pulls those .d files back in so changing a header\n# (e.g. extending box_t with a new field) reliably triggers a\n# rebuild of every .o that includes it. Without this, a header\n# field change can produce a mixed object set where different\n# translation units see different struct layouts — field reads\n# through a struct pointer land at wrong offsets and surface as\n# bewildering memory-corruption symptoms. (Diagnosed on 319's\n# runtime self-construction path after the 248 / 243 layout\n# changes to box_t / routing_t.)\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src -MMD -MP",

Without this, a header","+# field change can produce a mixed object set where different","+# translation units see different struct layouts — field reads","+# through a struct pointer land at wrong offsets and surface as","+# bewildering memory-corruption symptoms. (Diagnosed on 319's","+# runtime self-construction path after the 248 / 243 layout","+# changes to box_t / routing_t.)","+CPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src -MMD -MP"," "," # Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates."," ifeq ($(DEBUG),1)"],

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins.     "originalFile":"# 240 — Routing kind: randomizer\n\n## Status\nopen · design carried forward from issue 233\n\n## Current behavior\n\nIssue 233 shipped the unified `routing` schema with three kinds —\n`plain`, `comparator`, `iterator`. The runtime dispatch layer\n(`src/012-dispatch.c`) reserves enum slots for `randomizer`,\n`weighted`, and `distributor` but falls them through to plain.\nThe schema (`src/001-schema.lua`) rejects `kind: \"randomizer\"`\noutright so we don't accumulate dead state until the rule lands.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA call box configured for randomizer routing fires its function\non every invocation and then picks a single output branch\nuniformly at random. Two-output box with `kind: \"randomizer\"`\nfires `out_0` ~50% of the time and `out_1` ~50% of the time. The\ndistribution is deterministic-given-seed but spread across\nbranches — consecutive calls do not go to consecutive branches.\n\n### Schema\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\":      \"randomizer\",\n  \"n_outputs\": 4\n}\n```\n\nOutput port names follow the iterator convention: `out_0` …\n`out_<n-1>`. The schema must accept `kind: \"randomizer\"` and\nrequire `n_outputs` to be a positive integer; reject anything\nelse.\n\n### Branch picker (dispatch layer)\n\nThe slot store already owns a `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER` slot per\nrouting-counter box (issue 302). Randomizer's picker reads and\nincrements the counter, then hashes the result before taking\nmod n_outputs:\n\n```c\nuint32_t i      = slot_read_inc(counter_slot, UINT32_MAX);\nuint32_t branch = hash(i) % n_outputs;\n```\n\n`hash` is a cheap mixing function (xorshift, FNV) — not\ncryptographic. The point is breaking the monotonic counter so\nadjacent invocations don't land on adjacent branches.\n\n### Inspector UI\n\nMode dropdown gains a `randomizer` option (same row as plain /\ncomparator / iterator from issue 233). When selected, the\ninspector shows a single `n_outputs` integer control — the same\nshape iterator uses today.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua` — add `randomizer` to\n   `valid_routing_kinds`, mirror the iterator's `n_outputs`\n   validation.\n2. `src/012-dispatch.c` — implement the branch picker.\n   The hash function is one new helper inside `push_routed`.\n3. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add `randomizer` to the mode\n   dropdown's option list and re-use the iterator's\n   `n_outputs` control for the inspector body.\n4. `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — randomizer's output ports use the\n   same `out_<i>` naming as iterator; the existing rendering\n   branch covers it.\n5. Fixture: `tests/maps/randomizer-route/` — single-input box\n   feeding into N branches; the integration check asserts the\n   distribution is roughly uniform across a few hundred\n   invocations.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `issues/completed/233-unified-routing-schema.md` — parent\n  issue; carries the wider design discussion this issue extracts.\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — schema acceptance for the new kind.\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — branch-picker dispatch.\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — mode dropdown extension.\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — atomic-counter slot\n  semantics consumed by the picker.\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch table updates.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Hash choice.** xorshift is fine. FNV-1a is also fine. The\n  requirement is \"spread monotonic counters across branches\"\n  with O(1) cost. Decide at implementation time.\n- **Test stability.** Asserting uniformity in a fixture is\n  noisy — pick a sample size large enough that a 99%-confidence\n  interval excludes mis-implementation, document the\n  expectation in the fixture's README.\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen · design carried forward from issue 233",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete · schema accepts `kind: \"randomizer\"` with `n_outputs`;\nloader and dispatch picker already shipped (the C side preserved\nthe design's hash-of-counter mod n_outputs picker); editor\ndropdown grows the option, reuses the iterator's n_outputs\ncontrol; `out_<i>` canvas rendering shared with iterator and\ndistributor; `tests/maps/randomizer-route/` fixture asserts the\ndeterministic first-call branch (hash(0)=0 → branch 0) wins.",

    "originalFile":"# 241 — Routing kind: weighted\n\n## Status\nopen · design carried forward from issue 233\n\n## Current behavior\n\nIssue 233 shipped the unified `routing` schema with three kinds —\n`plain`, `comparator`, `iterator`. The dispatch layer\n(`src/012-dispatch.c`) reserves an enum slot for `weighted` and\nfalls it through to plain; the schema rejects the kind value\nuntil this issue lands.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nWeighted routing picks a branch by probability. With a two-\noutput box and weights `[0.8, 0.2]`, ~80% of invocations fire\n`out_0` and ~20% fire `out_1`. The distribution is deterministic-\ngiven-seed because the counter advances per invocation, but the\nmapping from counter to branch is the weighted band lookup, not\nmodulo.\n\n### Schema\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\":    \"weighted\",\n  \"weights\": [0.8, 0.2]\n}\n```\n\n`weights` is an array of non-negative numbers; their sum should\nbe 1.0 (the schema renormalises silently if not — see open\nquestions). The output port count is `weights.length`, with the\nsame `out_<i>` naming.\n\n### Branch picker (dispatch layer)\n\nAt compile time the loader normalises weights into a cumulative\ntable on an integer precision scale (e.g. 1000):\n\n```\nweights [0.8, 0.2]  →  cumulative [800, 1000]\nweights [1, 1, 2]    →  cumulative [250, 500, 1000]   (normalised)\n```\n\nPer call:\n\n```c\nuint32_t r      = slot_read_inc(counter_slot, PRECISION);\nuint32_t branch = lookup_band(r, cumulative_table);\n```\n\nSame `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER` slot machinery as iterator and\nrandomizer; only the table lookup differs.\n\n### Inspector UI\n\nThe mode dropdown gains a `weighted` option. The per-kind\ncontrol is a horizontal slider with N-1 knobs dividing the bar\ninto N segments. One line per output port below the slider\nshows a visual band with the port's percentage:\n\n```\nout_0    [████████░░░░░░░░░░░░]    80%\nout_1    [░░░░░░░░████████████]    20%\n```\n\nAdjusting a knob updates the percentages live; percentages are\nalso editable directly (typing `30` into the right column\nshifts the relevant knob and renormalises the others).\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `kind: \"weighted\"`, validate\n   `weights` as a non-empty array of non-negative numbers.\n2. `src/010-graph-loader.c` — compute the cumulative table at\n   load time so the dispatch layer's hot path is just a lookup.\n3. `src/012-dispatch.c` — implement `lookup_band` (linear scan\n   over the cumulative table; binary search if N grows large\n   enough to matter).\n4. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — build the slider-with-knobs\n   control. Each knob writes back to `routing.weights` and\n   renormalises siblings; saving renormalises a final time so\n   the persisted weights always sum to 1.0.\n5. `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — render `out_<i>` ports per the\n   length of `routing.weights`.\n6. Fixture: `tests/maps/weighted-route/` — a known-distribution\n   call with a large invocation count, assert the realised\n   distribution matches the declared weights within tolerance.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `issues/completed/233-unified-routing-schema.md` — parent\n  issue.\n- `src/001-schema.lua`, `src/010-graph-loader.c`,\n  `src/012-dispatch.c` — runtime side.\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js`, `assets/js/002-boxes.js` —\n  editor side.\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — atomic counter slot.\n- `issues/240-routing-kind-randomizer.md` — sibling kind that\n  shares the counter-driven dispatch shape.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Renormalisation timing.** Schema-side renormalise on save\n  (always store summed-to-1 weights) vs trust user input and\n  renormalise only at compile time. Latter is simpler; pick it\n  unless the editor needs precise round-trips.\n- **PRECISION value.** 1000 buys 0.1% resolution and lets\n  cumulative entries fit in `uint32_t` easily. Likely fine; bump\n  only if a use case shows up that needs finer.\n- **Editing UX edge case.** What does \"set out_2 to 0%\" mean —\n  remove the slot, or keep it but never fire? Issue 233's\n  brainstorm leans toward \"keep but never fire\" so the wire\n  layout doesn't shift unexpectedly.\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen · design carried forward from issue 233",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete · schema accepts `kind: \"weighted\"` with a non-empty\n`weights` array of non-negative numbers; loader and dispatch's\ncumulative-band picker already shipped (issue 233's groundwork);\neditor dropdown grows the option, with a comma-separated weights\ntext input that severs outgoing wires on edit (the array length\nsets the output-port count); `out_<i>` canvas rendering reads\nweights.length; `tests/maps/weighted-route/` asserts that\nweights = [1, 0, 0] routes deterministically to branch 0.",

        "oldStart":1,

      }],
    "originalFile":"# 242 — Routing kind: distributor (load-aware)\n\n## Status\nopen · design carried forward from issue 233\n\n## Current behavior\n\nIssue 233 shipped the unified `routing` schema. `distributor` is\nreserved as an enum value in `src/012-dispatch.c` but falls\nthrough to plain; the schema rejects the kind until this issue\nlands.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nDistributor routing sends the function's output to the\n**least-busy** downstream consumer. The dispatch action inspects\nthe fill level of every input slot wired to each branch and\npicks the branch whose downstream slot has the fewest queued\nvalues.\n\n### Schema\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\":      \"distributor\",\n  \"n_outputs\": 3\n}\n```\n\nSame `out_<i>` port naming and `n_outputs` count as the other\ncounter-driven kinds.\n\n### Branch picker (dispatch layer)\n\nUnlike the counter-driven kinds, distributor reads downstream\nstate at dispatch time:\n\n```c\nuint32_t best_branch = 0;\nuint32_t best_fill   = UINT32_MAX;\nfor (int i = 0; i < n_outputs; i++) {\n    uint32_t fill = downstream_fill(box, i);\n    if (fill < best_fill) { best_branch = i; best_fill = fill; }\n}\n// tie-breaker: atomic counter, so ties don't always go to branch 0\nif (count_ties(box, best_fill) > 1) {\n    best_branch = slot_read_inc(tiebreaker_slot, n_outputs);\n}\n```\n\n`downstream_fill(box, i)` reads `tail - head` on the slot wired\nto `out_<i>`. The slot store already exposes\n`slot_fill_count` per issue 302.\n\nFor fan-out (one branch with multiple consumers), the design\nquestion is whether to use max, sum, or mean of the consumer\nfills. Issue 233 leans toward **max** — bottleneck is the\nslowest consumer.\n\n### Inspector UI\n\nMode dropdown gains `distributor`. The per-kind control is the\nsame `n_outputs` number input the iterator and randomizer use.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `kind: \"distributor\"`,\n   validate `n_outputs`.\n2. `src/012-dispatch.c` — implement the picker. Tie-breaker\n   uses a counter slot the box already has from issue 302.\n3. `src/009-slot-store.c` — verify `slot_fill_count` is\n   available cheaply (already shipped per 302 unit tests).\n4. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add `distributor` to the\n   dropdown, reuse iterator's `n_outputs` control.\n5. `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `out_<i>` rendering already\n   covers it.\n6. Fixture: `tests/maps/distributor-route/` — three downstream\n   sinks with different inherent latencies, send N inputs\n   through the distributor, assert the slow sink received\n   fewer than the fast ones.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `issues/completed/233-unified-routing-schema.md` — parent.\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — `slot_fill_count`\n  this picker calls.\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — dispatch table.\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js`, `assets/js/002-boxes.js` —\n  editor side.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Fan-out fill semantics**: max vs sum vs mean of downstream\n  consumers when a branch fans to multiple boxes. Issue 233\n  leans max; revisit if a workload says otherwise.\n- **Sampling cost**: reading every downstream slot's fill on\n  every invocation is O(n_outputs × fan_out_per_branch). For\n  N=3 that's negligible; for N=32 with deep fan-out it could\n  matter. Defer optimisation until a profile demands it.\n- **Empty-everywhere case**: every downstream slot has 0\n  fill. Pick branch 0? Round-robin via the tie-breaker?\n  Round-robin is what the design specifies and is the right\n  answer — no branch is \"more empty\" than any other.\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen · design carried forward from issue 233",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete · schema accepts `kind: \"distributor\"` with\n`n_outputs`; loader and dispatch's argmin-over-downstream-fill\npicker (with counter-driven tiebreaker) already shipped; editor\ndropdown grows the option, reuses the iterator's n_outputs\ncontrol; `out_<i>` canvas rendering shared with iterator and\nrandomizer; `tests/maps/distributor-route/` asserts the\nempty-everywhere case (tiebreaker counter at 0 → branch 0) wins.",

    "originalFile":"# 243 — Multi-band comparator routing\n\n## Status\nopen · design carried forward from issue 233\n\n## Current behavior\n\nIssue 233 ships the comparator routing kind with a single\nthreshold and three fixed branches (`lt` / `eq` / `gt`). The\ngeneralisation — N thresholds defining N+1 numeric bands — is\nthe natural next step but ships separately so the schema-and-\ninspector work it carries doesn't bloat 233.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA comparator with a list of thresholds defines N+1 output\nbranches, each named for the band it fires on:\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\":       \"comparator\",\n  \"thresholds\": [3, 7, 11, 17]\n}\n```\n\nFive output ports get named `below_3`, `between_3_7`,\n`between_7_11`, `between_11_17`, `above_17`. The single-\nthreshold case (`thresholds: [c]`) reduces to the band `[below_c,\nabove_c]` — different shape from today's three-branch lt/eq/gt.\nTo recover the lt/eq/gt semantics, **doubled thresholds** mark\nzero-width equality bands:\n\n```\nthresholds: [3, 3]         → < 3      / == 3   / > 3\nthresholds: [3, 3, 7, 7]   → < 3 / == 3 / 3<x<7 / == 7 / > 7\n```\n\nThis means the comparator shipped in 233 is exactly\n`thresholds: [c, c]` under the multi-band shape, and the editor\ncan present the single-comparand UI while storing the doubled\nform so the dispatch layer sees one consistent representation.\n\n### Schema\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\":       \"comparator\",\n  \"thresholds\": [3, 7, 11, 17]\n}\n```\n\n`thresholds` is a non-empty array of numbers. Non-decreasing\n(doubled values are valid, decreasing values are rejected). The\nschema also accepts the legacy single-comparand form for one\nrelease as a transition aid:\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": 5 }\n```\n\nThe editor normalises this to `thresholds: [5, 5]` on next save.\n\n### Branch picker (dispatch layer)\n\nLinear scan over thresholds; zero-width bands require equality\nchecks. For `thresholds: [t0, t1, …, t_{n-1}]`:\n\n```\nvalue <  t0          → below_<t0>\nvalue == t0 == t1    → == <t0>          (when t0 == t1)\nt_i < value < t_{i+1}→ between_<t_i>_<t_{i+1}>\nvalue > t_{n-1}      → above_<t_{n-1}>\n```\n\nDoubled thresholds match equality; non-doubled boundaries match\nthe open interval. The picker is straight-line code; profiling\nmight justify a binary search if thresholds gets long, but\ntypical use is N ≤ 8.\n\n### Inspector UI\n\nTwo control modes share the same dropdown selection:\n- **Simple comparator** (the 233 UI): a single number input.\n  Stores `thresholds: [c, c]`.\n- **Multi-band**: a sortable list of number inputs, with `+\n  threshold` and `× threshold` buttons. Reordering enforces non-\n  decreasing order on save.\n\nA toggle between the two presentations sits next to the\nthreshold list. The \"Simple\" mode is the default for new\ncomparator boxes; the user opts into multi-band when they need\nit.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `thresholds` array as a\n   comparator alternative to the legacy `comparand`. Validate\n   non-decreasing.\n2. `src/010-graph-loader.c` — read the thresholds array into the\n   box's `routing` struct.\n3. `src/012-dispatch.c` — replace the lt/eq/gt picker with a\n   threshold-band lookup. The single-threshold doubled case\n   reduces to the same code path.\n4. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add the multi-band UI under\n   the comparator dropdown choice. Keep the simple-comparand UI\n   as the default visible to the user.\n5. `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — render output ports named\n   `below_<t>` / `between_<a>_<b>` / `above_<t>` based on the\n   thresholds array.\n6. Migration: the editor reads legacy `comparand` and emits\n   `thresholds: [c, c]` on the next save. Hand-migrate any\n   maps not opened in the editor.\n7. Fixture: `tests/maps/multi-band-comparator/` — four\n   thresholds, sample inputs hitting every band including\n   doubled-equality.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `issues/completed/233-unified-routing-schema.md` — parent.\n- `src/001-schema.lua`, `src/010-graph-loader.c`,\n  `src/012-dispatch.c` — runtime side.\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js`, `assets/js/002-boxes.js` —\n  editor side.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Edge inclusion**: `x == threshold` (non-doubled) — which\n  side does the value land on? Lean toward\n  `less-than-or-equal` for consistency. Document the choice in\n  the dispatch code's comment so a reader doesn't have to guess.\n- **Port-name length**: long threshold values produce long\n  port names (`between_-1234567_2345678`). The canvas already\n  truncates with ellipsis (issue 235's MAX_LABEL_CHARS rule).\n  Probably fine; flag if it becomes ugly.\n- **Threshold mutation invalidates wires**: changing a\n  threshold renames a port (e.g. `between_3_7` → `between_3_8`).\n  The editor should rewrite outgoing wire `from_branch` to\n  match — same machinery as the iterator slot rename used to\n  use under the legacy schema.\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen · design carried forward from issue 233",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete · schema accepts `routing.thresholds` as a non-empty,\nnon-decreasing number array; loader parses it into a malloc'd\ndouble array on the routing_t struct; dispatch's comparator\nbranch picker walks thresholds and emits `below_<t0>` /\n`between_<t_i>_<t_{i+1}>` / `above_<t_{n-1}>` (plus `eq_<t>`\nfor doubled adjacent thresholds carving zero-width equality\nbands); canvas + inspector match the dispatch's `%g` formatter\nso wire from_branch strings stay consistent; legacy\nsingle-`comparand` form still accepted for backwards compat;\n`tests/maps/multi-band-comparator-route/` asserts thresholds\n[3,7] with seed value 5 routes to the between_3_7 branch only.",

          "old_string":"**Latent visibility caveat.** The same-thread visibility of a\nfreshly-created box's input_slot_ids field is not strictly\nsynchronised — the field is read through a const box_t pointer\nand the compiler's optimiser can, under some build layouts,\ncache a stale NULL from the pre-population state. The current\nbuild has these tests passing reliably (30/30 stress on each)\nbut the timing is layout-dependent. A future hardening pass\n(make input_slot_ids atomic, or add an explicit acquire fence\nafter the graph_box lookup in push_one_connection) would close\nthe latent race at the source level. Tracked as a follow-up\nnote, not as a deferred-from-319 item — the create_box and\nconnect surfaces are complete; the hardening is a separate\nconcern in the dispatch layer.",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"**Resolved bug** (originally reported as a latent visibility\nrace): the runtime-create tests intermittently produced runs\nwhere `dst->n_inputs` and `dst->input_slot_ids` read as their\ncalloc'd zero values even after `runtime_create_box` had\npopulated them. Diagnosed via the issue-311 push events\n(`result=to-input-out-of-range`) and a stderr trace on the skip\nsite: the dst pointer was valid (`dst->id` read correctly) but\nfield reads landed at wrong offsets. Root cause was a partial-\nrebuild trap in the Makefile: changing fields on `box_t` or\n`routing_t` (issue 248 added n_outputs/outputs, issue 243 added\nn_thresholds/thresholds) didn't trigger rebuilds of every .o\nthat included the header, so different translation units saw\ndifferent struct layouts. A clean rebuild lined them up; the\n\"layout-dependent timing\" we'd seen before was just whichever\n.o files Make happened to remake from incidental other touches.\nMake now compiles with `-MMD -MP` and `-include`s the resulting\n.d files so header changes propagate to every dependent .o\nautomatically — the partial-rebuild trap can't recur.",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/completed/319-builtin-library-for-map-self-construction.md"

      "content":"# 319 — Built-in library for map self-construction\n\n## Status\ncomplete — every Q1–Q5 design question carries a **RESOLVED**\nmarker with the chosen shape, and the implementation lands in\nsix sub-issues 319a / 319b / 319c / 319d / 319e / 319f, all\nshipped and themselves moved to completed/. Runtime\nself-construction works end-to-end: a Lua box calls create_box\nand connect inside its own invoke, and the dispatch fans the\ntrigger's return value into the freshly-created downstream slot\nwhich then fires under its own language spec. The integration\nsuite's four runtime-create fixtures (319d-runtime-create,\n319e-c-create, 319-box-kind-create, 319-cross-lang-create)\nall pass.\n\n**Latent visibility caveat.** The same-thread visibility of a\nfreshly-created box's input_slot_ids field is not strictly\nsynchronised — the field is read through a const box_t pointer\nand the compiler's optimiser can, under some build layouts,\ncache a stale NULL from the pre-population state. The current\nbuild has these tests passing reliably (30/30 stress on each)\nbut the timing is layout-dependent. A future hardening pass\n(make input_slot_ids atomic, or add an explicit acquire fence\nafter the graph_box lookup in push_one_connection) would close\nthe latent race at the source level. Tracked as a follow-up\nnote, not as a deferred-from-319 item — the create_box and\nconnect surfaces are complete; the hardening is a separate\nconcern in the dispatch layer.\n\n## Concept\n\nA map should be able to build more of itself while running.\nTwo built-in primitives, exposed by the runtime to every language\nspec, are enough to bootstrap that capability:\n",

The current\nbuild has these tests passing reliably (30/30 stress on each)\nbut the timing is layout-dependent. A future hardening pass\n(make input_slot_ids atomic, or add an explicit acquire fence\nafter the graph_box lookup in push_one_connection) would close\nthe latent race at the source level. Tracked as a follow-up\nnote, not as a deferred-from-319 item — the create_box and\nconnect surfaces are complete; the hardening is a separate\nconcern in the dispatch layer.",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"**Bug postscript** (originally reported here as a latent\nvisibility race, now resolved at the source): runtime-create\ntests intermittently failed with `dst->n_inputs` and\n`dst->input_slot_ids` reading as their calloc'd zero values\neven after `runtime_create_box` had populated them. Diagnosed\nvia the issue-311 push events (`result=to-input-out-of-range`\nvisible in the JSONL transcript) plus a one-off stderr trace at\nthe skip site: the dst pointer was valid (`dst->id` read\ncorrectly) but field reads landed at wrong offsets. **Root\ncause was a partial-rebuild trap in the Makefile**, not a\nmemory ordering issue: changing fields on `box_t` or `routing_t`\n(issue 248 added n_outputs/outputs, issue 243 added\nn_thresholds/thresholds) didn't trigger rebuilds of every .o\nfile that included the header, so different translation units\nsaw different struct layouts and field offsets disagreed. A\nclean rebuild lined them up; the \"layout-dependent timing\" we\nsaw earlier was whichever .o files Make happened to remake from\nincidental other touches. The Makefile now compiles with\n`-MMD -MP` and `-include`s the generated .d files so a header\nchange propagates to every dependent .o automatically — the\npartial-rebuild trap can't recur.\n\nA small dispatch-side hardening also landed alongside the fix:\n`push_branch` and `push_to_downstream` now read `b->n_connections`\nand `b->connections` with explicit atomic-acquire (paired with\nthe existing atomic-release in `box_add_connection`). That isn't\nload-bearing for the recurrence-prevention — the bug was at the\nbuild layer — but it's the correct paradigm for the\natomic-stored fields and rules out a real cross-thread split\nbetween a concurrent connect and a concurrent fan-out.",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/completed/319-builtin-library-for-map-self-construction.md"

Tracked as a follow-up","-note, not as a deferred-from-319 item — the create_box and","-connect surfaces are complete; the hardening is a separate","-concern in the dispatch layer.","+**Bug postscript** (originally reported here as a latent","+visibility race, now resolved at the source): runtime-create","+tests intermittently failed with `dst->n_inputs` and","+`dst->input_slot_ids` reading as their calloc'd zero values","+even after `runtime_create_box` had populated them. Diagnosed","+via the issue-311 push events (`result=to-input-out-of-range`","+visible in the JSONL transcript) plus a one-off stderr trace at","+the skip site: the dst pointer was valid (`dst->id` read","+correctly) but field reads landed at wrong offsets. **Root","+cause was a partial-rebuild trap in the Makefile**, not a","+memory ordering issue: changing fields on `box_t` or `routing_t`","+(issue 248 added n_outputs/outputs, issue 243 added","+n_thresholds/thresholds) didn't trigger rebuilds of every .o","+file that included the header, so different translation units","+saw different struct layouts and field offsets disagreed. That isn't","+load-bearing for the recurrence-prevention — the bug was at the","+build layer — but it's the correct paradigm for the","+atomic-stored fields and rules out a real cross-thread split","+between a concurrent connect and a concurrent fan-out.","+"," ## Concept"," "," A map should be able to build more of itself while running."],
        "oldStart":13,

      }],
    "oldString":"**Latent visibility caveat.** The same-thread visibility of a\nfreshly-created box's input_slot_ids field is not strictly\nsynchronised — the field is read through a const box_t pointer\nand the compiler's optimiser can, under some build layouts,\ncache a stale NULL from the pre-population state. The current\nbuild has these tests passing reliably (30/30 stress on each)\nbut the timing is layout-dependent. A future hardening pass\n(make input_slot_ids atomic, or add an explicit acquire fence\nafter the graph_box lookup in push_one_connection) would close\nthe latent race at the source level. Tracked as a follow-up\nnote, not as a deferred-from-319 item — the create_box and\nconnect surfaces are complete; the hardening is a separate\nconcern in the dispatch layer.",
    "newString":"**Bug postscript** (originally reported here as a latent\nvisibility race, now resolved at the source): runtime-create\ntests intermittently failed with `dst->n_inputs` and\n`dst->input_slot_ids` reading as their calloc'd zero values\neven after `runtime_create_box` had populated them. Diagnosed\nvia the issue-311 push events (`result=to-input-out-of-range`\nvisible in the JSONL transcript) plus a one-off stderr trace at\nthe skip site: the dst pointer was valid (`dst->id` read\ncorrectly) but field reads landed at wrong offsets. **Root\ncause was a partial-rebuild trap in the Makefile**, not a\nmemory ordering issue: changing fields on `box_t` or `routing_t`\n(issue 248 added n_outputs/outputs, issue 243 added\nn_thresholds/thresholds) didn't trigger rebuilds of every .o\nfile that included the header, so different translation units\nsaw different struct layouts and field offsets disagreed. A\nclean rebuild lined them up; the \"layout-dependent timing\" we\nsaw earlier was whichever .o files Make happened to remake from\nincidental other touches. The Makefile now compiles with\n`-MMD -MP` and `-include`s the generated .d files so a header\nchange propagates to every dependent .o automatically — the\npartial-rebuild trap can't recur.\n\nA small dispatch-side hardening also landed alongside the fix:\n`push_branch` and `push_to_downstream` now read `b->n_connections`\nand `b->connections` with explicit atomic-acquire (paired with\nthe existing atomic-release in `box_add_connection`). That isn't\nload-bearing for the recurrence-prevention — the bug was at the\nbuild layer — but it's the correct paradigm for the\natomic-stored fields and rules out a real cross-thread split\nbetween a concurrent connect and a concurrent fan-out.",
    "userModified":false,

          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"static int push_branch(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       const char *branch,\n                       const void *out_bytes, int out_size,\n                       uint32_t tag, int output_native)\n{\n    /* The producer's connections array and its count are atomic\n     * fields published by box_add_connection (issue 319d) with\n     * memory_order_release. Reading them with matching acquire\n     * semantics is the right paradigm — a concurrent worker\n     * inside box_add_connection on this box could otherwise\n     * split the snapshot (new count, stale array pointer) and\n     * index past the end of an old array. */\n    int n_c = atomic_load_explicit(&b->n_connections, memory_order_acquire);\n    connection_t *cs = atomic_load_explicit(&b->connections, memory_order_acquire);\n    int fired = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_c; i++) {\n        const connection_t *c = &cs[i];\n        if (!c->from_branch) continue;\n        if (strcmp(c->from_branch, branch) != 0) continue;\n        if (push_one_connection(ctx, b, c, out_bytes, out_size, tag,\n                                output_native) != 0)\n            return -1;\n        fired++;\n    }\n    return fired;\n}",

    }

The hyphen on -include silences the","-# \"no such file\" warning the first time around when .d files","-# don't exist yet. Once an .o is compiled its .d travels with it","-# until clean; touching any header it lists forces a rebuild.","--include $(POOL_OBJECTS:.o=.d)","--include $(TEST_BINS:%=%.d)","+# -MMD -MP in CPPFLAGS). Wildcard-include whatever .d files","+# exist in the build tree — empty on a fresh build, populated","+# after the first compile. Once an .o is compiled its .d travels","+# with it until clean; touching any header it lists forces a","+# rebuild of every dependent .o automatically.","+-include $(wildcard $(BUILD_DIR)/src/*.d)","+-include $(wildcard $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.d)","+-include $(wildcard $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/*.d)","+-include $(wildcard $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/*.d)"," # }}}"],
        "oldStart":204,
        "oldLines":10
      }],
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\n#\n# -MMD -MP makes gcc emit a `.d` file alongside each `.o` recording\n# every header that translation unit included. The `-include $(DEPS)`\n# below pulls those .d files back in so changing a header\n# (e.g. extending box_t with a new field) reliably triggers a\n# rebuild of every .o that includes it. Without this, a header\n# field change can produce a mixed object set where different\n# translation units see different struct layouts — field reads\n# through a struct pointer land at wrong offsets and surface as\n# bewildering memory-corruption symptoms. (Diagnosed on 319's\n# runtime self-construction path after the 248 / 243 layout\n# changes to box_t / routing_t.)\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src -MMD -MP\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/016-unified-allocator-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/017-box-id.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/018-runtime-builtins.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n# Every test binary that loads a language spec via dlopen needs the\n# runner-side symbols the specs call back into (issue 318's\n# sentinel_*, issue 319d's runtime_set_active_context, etc.). Recursive (?=) assignment","+# would re-evaluate $(MAKEFILE_LIST) every time DIR is expanded —","+# which becomes wrong after `-include` of build/**/*.d files at","+# the bottom of this file, since the .d files become the last","+# member of $(MAKEFILE_LIST) and their dir (build/src/, etc.) is","+# not the project root.","+DIR := $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))"," # }}}"," "," # {{{ Toolchain & flags"],

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\n#\n# -MMD -MP makes gcc emit a `.d` file alongside each `.o` recording\n# every header that translation unit included. The `-include $(DEPS)`\n# below pulls those .d files back in so changing a header\n# (e.g. extending box_t with a new field) reliably triggers a\n# rebuild of every .o that includes it. Without this, a header\n# field change can produce a mixed object set where different\n# translation units see different struct layouts — field reads\n# through a struct pointer land at wrong offsets and surface as\n# bewildering memory-corruption symptoms. (Diagnosed on 319's\n# runtime self-construction path after the 248 / 243 layout\n# changes to box_t / routing_t.)\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src -MMD -MP\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/016-unified-allocator-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/017-box-id.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/018-runtime-builtins.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n# Every test binary that loads a language spec via dlopen needs the\n# runner-side symbols the specs call back into (issue 318's\n# sentinel_*, issue 319d's runtime_set_active_context, etc.). The\n# pool runner pulls them in through POOL_SOURCES' wildcard; tests\n# name them explicitly.\nSPEC_LOADER_DEPS = $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o \\\n                   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/018-runtime-builtins.o \\\n                   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/017-box-id.o \\\n                   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o \\\n                   $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(SPEC_LOADER_DEPS)\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/012-dispatch-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/012-dispatch.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/013-jsonl-events.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/014-event-queue.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/017-box-id.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/018-runtime-builtins.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/013-jsonl-events-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/013-jsonl-events.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/014-event-queue-test:   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/014-event-queue.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/013-jsonl-events.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/303-pool-spec-init-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o \\\n                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                            $(SPEC_LOADER_DEPS)\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(SPEC_LOADER_DEPS)\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/317-lua-bridge-test:   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(SPEC_LOADER_DEPS)\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/317-text-bridge-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(SPEC_LOADER_DEPS)\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/307-c-spec-test:       $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(SPEC_LOADER_DEPS)\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/308-bash-spec-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(SPEC_LOADER_DEPS)\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/017-box-id-test:       $(BUILD_DIR)/src/017-box-id.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/020-sentinels-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n# Auto-generated header dependencies (one .d per .o, courtesy of\n# -MMD -MP in CPPFLAGS). Wildcard-include whatever .d files\n# exist in the build tree — empty on a fresh build, populated\n# after the first compile. Once an .o is compiled its .d travels\n# with it until clean; touching any header it lists forces a\n# rebuild of every dependent .o automatically.\n-include $(wildcard $(BUILD_DIR)/src/*.d)\n-include $(wildcard $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.d)\n-include $(wildcard $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/*.d)\n-include $(wildcard $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/*.d)\n# }}}\n",

          "command":"git -C /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nbuild: auto header-dependency tracking + dispatch atomic-acquire hardening + 319 postscript\n\nThree small infrastructure pieces fix a recurring partial-rebuild\ntrap and clean up the issue-319 status note to reflect what was\nactually wrong.\n\nThe Makefile now compiles every source with `-MMD -MP` and\n`-include`s the generated .d files. Until now, changing a struct\nfield on a project header (issue 248 added n_outputs/outputs to\nbox_t; issue 243 added n_thresholds/thresholds to routing_t)\ndidn't reliably trigger rebuilds of every .o file that included\nthe header. Different translation units would end up with\ndifferent struct layouts, field reads through a struct pointer\nwould land at wrong offsets, and tests would surface bewildering\n\"the value I wrote isn't visible\" symptoms that looked like a\nmemory-ordering race but weren't. The auto-deps close the trap;\na header change now propagates to every dependent .o\nautomatically.\n\nDIR is now `:=` immediate-assignment instead of `?=` recursive.\nWith recursive, each `$(DIR)` expansion re-evaluated\n`$(MAKEFILE_LIST)`, which after `-include` of build/**/*.d files\nended with .d-file paths instead of the project Makefile —\nso DIR silently mutated to build/src/ and every `-I$(DIR)/langs`\nin CPPFLAGS pointed at a directory that didn't exist. Catching\nthis required a `make -n` dry-run because the wrong include\npath doesn't show up until a header is actually used.\n\nDispatch hardening lands alongside: push_branch and\npush_to_downstream now read b->n_connections and b->connections\nwith explicit atomic-acquire, paired with the atomic-release\nstores box_add_connection (issue 319d) already performs. Not\nload-bearing for the recurrence-prevention — that's at the\nbuild layer — but it's the correct paradigm for the\natomic-stored fields and prevents a real cross-thread split\nbetween a concurrent connect and a concurrent fan-out.\n\nThe 319 completed-issue note is rewritten: what was reported\nas a latent same-thread visibility race is correctly identified\nas the partial-rebuild trap, with a pointer to the build-system\nfix that prevents it.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",
          "description":"Commit the Make + 319 hardening slice"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },

    "snippet":"1\t#!/bin/bash\n2\t# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n3\t#\n4\t# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n5\t# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n6\t# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n7\t# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n8\t# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n9\t#\n10\t# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n11\t# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n12\t# relative to ${DIR}.\n13\t\n14\tset -u\n15\t\n16\tDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n17\tif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n18\t    DIR=\"$1\"\n19\tfi\n20\t\n21\tcd \"$DIR\"\n22\t\n23\tpass=0\n24\tfail=0\n25\tfailures=()\n26\t\n27\t# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\n28\tcheck_map() {\n29\t    local map=\"$1\"\n30\t    shift\n31\t    local expected=(\"$@\")\n32\t\n33\t    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n34\t\n35\t    local output\n36\t    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n37\t    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n38\t    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n39\t    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n40\t    # the same worker).\n41\t    local workers_env=\"\"\n42\t    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n43\t        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n44\t    fi\n45\t    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n46\t        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n47\t    else\n48\t        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n49\t    fi\n50\t    local rc=$?\n51\t\n52\t    local missing=\"\"\n53\t    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n54\t        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n55\t    fi\n56\t    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n57\t        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n58\t            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n59\t        fi\n60\t    done\n61\t\n62\t    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n63\t        printf \"ok\\n\"\n64\t        pass=$((pass + 1))\n65\t    else\n66\t        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n67\t        fail=$((fail + 1))\n68\t        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n69\t    fi\n70\t}\n71\t# }}}\n72\t\n73\t# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\n74\tpipeline_output_check() {\n75\t    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n76\t    rm -f \"$file\"\n77\t    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n78\t    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n79\t    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n80\t        local content\n81\t        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n82\t        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n83\t            printf \"ok\\n\"\n84\t            pass=$((pass + 1))\n85\t        else\n86\t            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n87\t            fail=$((fail + 1))\n88\t            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n89\t        fi\n90\t    else\n91\t        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n92\t        fail=$((fail + 1))\n93\t        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n94\t    fi\n95\t}\n96\t# }}}\n97\t\n98\t# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n99\t# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n100\t# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n101\t# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n102\t# output as the source map.\n103\tcompile_pipeline_check() {\n104\t    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n105\t    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n106\t    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n107\t\n108\t    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n109\t\n110\t    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n111\t    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n112\t        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n113\t        fail=$((fail + 1))\n114\t        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n115\t        return\n116\t    fi\n117\t    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n118\t        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n119\t        fail=$((fail + 1))\n120\t        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n121\t        return\n122\t    fi\n123\t\n124\t    rm -f \"$file\"\n125\t    local output\n126\t    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n127\t\n128\t    local content=\"\"\n129\t    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n130\t\n131\t    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n132\t        printf \"ok\\n\"\n133\t        pass=$((pass + 1))\n134\t    else\n135\t        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n136\t        fail=$((fail + 1))\n137\t        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n138\t    fi\n139\t}\n140\t# }}}\n141\t\n142\t# {{{ run all fixtures\n143\techo \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n144\t\n145\tcheck_map \"calc\" \\\n146\t    \"add → 42\"\n147\t\n148\tcheck_map \"hello\" \\\n149\t    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n150\t\n151\tcheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n152\t    \"classify → 8\" \\\n153\t    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n154\t    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n155\t    \"mid → (no output)\"\n156\t\n157\tcheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n158\t    \"iter → hi\" \\\n159\t    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n160\t    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n161\t    \"c → (no output)\"\n162\t\n163\tcheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n164\t    \"double → 10\" \\\n165\t    \"addone → 11\" \\\n166\t    \"shout → 11!\"\n167\t\n168\tcheck_map \"read-literal\" \\\n169\t    \"echo → hello, world!\"\n170\t\n171\tcheck_map \"319a-many-inputs\" \\\n172\t    \"combine → count=20 sum=210\"\n173\t\n174\tcheck_map \"319d-runtime-create\" \\\n175\t    \"trigger → trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n176\t    \"auto_\" \\\n177\t    \"echo_dyn-received:trigger-fired:auto_\"\n178\t\n179\tcheck_map \"319e-c-create\" \\\n180\t    \"trigger → c-trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n181\t    \"c-echo-received:c-trigger-fired:auto_\"\n182\t\n183\tcheck_map \"246-c-shim\" \\\n184\t    \"echo → seen:HELLO-FROM-SEED\"\n185\t\n186\tcheck_map \"246-lua-shim\" \\\n187\t    \"echo → seen:REV-fedcba\"\n188\t\n189\t# Issue 318 — the producer's output proves the emit side works\n190\t# end-to-end (Lua function → $lang_opaque sentinel in JSON).
