    "content":"/* src/014-event-queue.c — multi-producer event queue with a\n * dedicated writer thread.\n *\n * Design: Vyukov-style bounded MPSC ring. Producers do one\n * fetch-add / CAS on the enqueue position, write their payload\n * into the claimed slot, and bump the slot's sequence number to\n * publish it. The single consumer thread drains the ring by\n * reading the slot at the dequeue position and observing the\n * sequence number to know when the producer has finished writing.\n * A pthread mutex + condition variable provide the wakeup\n * mechanism — the mutex is NOT on the producer hot path; it's\n * only taken briefly to signal the consumer that data is\n * available (or, on rare full-ring contention, to block a\n * producer waiting for space).\n *\n * Why this shape: the mutex-linked-list predecessor serialised\n * every producer through one append-mutex; under bursty dispatch\n * (many small task_start / task_end events firing in close\n * succession from every worker) that mutex was the contention\n * hotspot. The ring's per-slot atomic seq lets producers proceed\n * independently — they only see each other if they happen to\n * claim adjacent slots in the same instant.\n *\n * Designed in issue 311.\n */\n\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"013-jsonl-events.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Ring sizing */\n/* Power-of-two ring capacity. 4096 slots × ~160 B per slot ≈ 640\n * KB per event_queue. The dispatch can fire roughly 3 events per\n * task; a run of 1000 tasks queues ~3000 events, well under\n * capacity, but the ring sizes itself to absorb dispatch bursts\n * without backpressuring producers. */\n#define EQ_RING_SIZE 4096u\n#define EQ_RING_MASK (EQ_RING_SIZE - 1u)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Event record */\ntypedef enum {\n    EV_RUN_START,\n    EV_TASK_SUBMIT,\n    EV_TASK_START,\n    EV_TASK_END,\n    EV_RUN_END,\n} event_kind_t;\n\n#define MAP_BUF_SZ    128\n#define BOX_ID_BUF_SZ 64\n\ntypedef struct {\n    event_kind_t       kind;\n    double             ts;\n    union {\n        struct {\n            char map[MAP_BUF_SZ];\n            int  n_workers;\n        } run_start;\n\n        struct {\n            int  task_id;\n            char box_id[BOX_ID_BUF_SZ];\n            int  worker_idx;\n        } task_submit;\n\n        struct {\n            int task_id;\n            int worker_idx;\n        } task_start;\n\n        struct {\n            int  task_id;\n            int  worker_idx;\n            long duration_us;\n            int  output_size;\n        } task_end;\n\n        struct {\n            long duration_us;\n            int  n_tasks;\n        } run_end;\n    } u;\n} event_payload_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Ring slot — Vyukov sequence pattern.\n *\n * Each slot carries an atomic sequence number that tracks the\n * slot's lifecycle:\n *   - At init: seq[i] = i. The slot is \"free for enqueue at\n *     position i, position i + RING_SIZE, position i + 2*RING_SIZE...\"\n *   - Producer claims position p (where p % RING_SIZE == i). It\n *     spins until seq[i] == p, writes the payload, then stores\n *     seq[i] = p + 1 (release). The slot is now \"ready for the\n *     consumer at position p.\"\n *   - Consumer reads position d (where d % RING_SIZE == i). It\n *     checks seq[i] == d + 1 (acquire). If so, reads payload,\n *     then stores seq[i] = d + RING_SIZE — the slot is now free\n *     for the next producer at position d + RING_SIZE.\n *\n * The producer / consumer never share a writable field other\n * than the per-slot seq, so contention is per-slot, not global. */\ntypedef struct {\n    _Atomic uint64_t seq;\n    event_payload_t  payload;\n} eq_slot_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Queue struct */\nstruct event_queue {\n    /* The ring itself + the producer/consumer positions. */\n    eq_slot_t        ring[EQ_RING_SIZE];\n    _Atomic uint64_t enqueue_pos;       /* next slot a producer will claim */\n    _Atomic uint64_t dequeue_pos;       /* next slot the consumer will read */\n\n    /* Wakeup mechanism. The mutex is NOT held on the lock-free\n     * enqueue / dequeue paths — it's only taken briefly to\n     * signal a CV after producing (consumer wakes on has_data)\n     * or after consuming (any blocked producer wakes on\n     * has_space). */\n    pthread_mutex_t  mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   has_data;\n    pthread_cond_t   has_space;\n    _Atomic int      shutdown;\n\n    pthread_t        writer_thread;\n    jsonl_writer_t  *writer;\n\n    /* Best-effort count, exposed by event_queue_pending(). Not\n     * load-bearing for sync — the per-slot seq is. */\n    _Atomic int      pending;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ copy_str_bounded() — strncpy + always-NUL-terminate */\nstatic void copy_str_bounded(char *dst, const char *src, size_t cap)\n{\n    if (cap == 0) return;\n    if (!src) { dst[0] = '\\0'; return; }\n    size_t n = strlen(src);\n    if (n >= cap) n = cap - 1;\n    memcpy(dst, src, n);\n    dst[n] = '\\0';\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ enqueue_ring() — claim a slot, write payload, publish seq.\n *\n * Returns 0 on success. The caller never sees failure — on a full\n * ring the producer blocks on `has_space` until the consumer\n * frees a slot. Blocking is the right tradeoff because the\n * alternative — dropping events — destroys the audit trail the\n * JSONL transcript exists for. */\nstatic void enqueue_ring(event_queue_t *q, const event_payload_t *src)\n{\n    uint64_t pos = atomic_load_explicit(&q->enqueue_pos, memory_order_relaxed);\n    for (;;) {\n        eq_slot_t *slot = &q->ring[pos & EQ_RING_MASK];\n        uint64_t seq = atomic_load_explicit(&slot->seq, memory_order_acquire);\n        int64_t  diff = (int64_t)seq - (int64_t)pos;\n\n        if (diff == 0) {\n            /* Slot is ready for us at position pos. Try to claim\n             * by bumping enqueue_pos. CAS-weak because the\n             * producer is happy to retry on spurious failure. */\n            if (atomic_compare_exchange_weak_explicit(\n                    &q->enqueue_pos, &pos, pos + 1,\n                    memory_order_relaxed, memory_order_relaxed)) {\n                slot->payload = *src;\n                /* Publish: the seq bump's release pairs with the\n                 * consumer's acquire load on slot->seq. Anything\n                 * we wrote into payload above is now visible to\n                 * the consumer once it sees seq == pos + 1. */\n                atomic_store_explicit(&slot->seq, pos + 1,\n                                      memory_order_release);\n                atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&q->pending, 1,\n                                          memory_order_relaxed);\n                /* Wake the consumer if it's sleeping. The lock\n                 * is held just long enough to signal — never on\n                 * the hot path between producers. */\n                pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n                pthread_cond_signal(&q->has_data);\n                pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n                return;\n            }\n            /* CAS lost; another producer beat us. pos was\n             * refreshed in-place by the CAS. Retry. */\n        } else if (diff < 0) {\n            /* Ring is full at position pos. Block until the\n             * consumer signals has_space. Recheck under the\n             * lock to avoid lost wakeups. */\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n            seq = atomic_load_explicit(&slot->seq, memory_order_acquire);\n            if ((int64_t)seq - (int64_t)pos < 0\n                && !atomic_load_explicit(&q->shutdown,\n                                         memory_order_acquire)) {\n                pthread_cond_wait(&q->has_space, &q->mtx);\n            }\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n            pos = atomic_load_explicit(&q->enqueue_pos,\n                                       memory_order_relaxed);\n        } else {\n            /* diff > 0: another producer raced ahead and\n             * published past us. Refresh and retry. */\n            pos = atomic_load_explicit(&q->enqueue_pos,\n                                       memory_order_relaxed);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dequeue_ring() — consumer reads the next ready slot.\n *\n * Returns 1 + fills *out if a slot was ready, 0 if empty. The\n * consumer is the sole caller, so no CAS is needed on dequeue_pos\n * — a plain store is fine. */\nstatic int dequeue_ring(event_queue_t *q, event_payload_t *out)\n{\n    uint64_t pos = atomic_load_explicit(&q->dequeue_pos,\n                                        memory_order_relaxed);\n    eq_slot_t *slot = &q->ring[pos & EQ_RING_MASK];\n    uint64_t seq = atomic_load_explicit(&slot->seq, memory_order_acquire);\n    int64_t  diff = (int64_t)seq - (int64_t)(pos + 1);\n    if (diff != 0) return 0;       /* not yet published */\n\n    *out = slot->payload;\n    /* Mark the slot free for the producer that wraps around to\n     * position (pos + RING_SIZE). */\n    atomic_store_explicit(&slot->seq, pos + EQ_RING_SIZE,\n                          memory_order_release);\n    atomic_store_explicit(&q->dequeue_pos, pos + 1,\n                          memory_order_relaxed);\n    atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&q->pending, 1, memory_order_relaxed);\n    /* Wake any producer that was blocked waiting for space. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n    pthread_cond_signal(&q->has_space);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ write_one() — serialize one event through jsonl_emit_* */\nstatic void write_one(event_queue_t *q, const event_payload_t *n)\n{\n    switch (n->kind) {\n        case EV_RUN_START:\n            jsonl_emit_run_start(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                 n->u.run_start.map,\n                                 n->u.run_start.n_workers);\n            break;\n        case EV_TASK_SUBMIT:\n            jsonl_emit_task_submit(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                   n->u.task_submit.task_id,\n                                   n->u.task_submit.box_id,\n                                   n->u.task_submit.worker_idx);\n            break;\n        case EV_TASK_START:\n            jsonl_emit_task_start(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                  n->u.task_start.task_id,\n                                  n->u.task_start.worker_idx);\n            break;\n        case EV_TASK_END:\n            jsonl_emit_task_end(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                n->u.task_end.task_id,\n                                n->u.task_end.worker_idx,\n                                n->u.task_end.duration_us,\n                                n->u.task_end.output_size);\n            break;\n        case EV_RUN_END:\n            jsonl_emit_run_end(q->writer, n->ts,\n                               n->u.run_end.duration_us,\n                               n->u.run_end.n_tasks);\n            break;\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ writer_main() — drain loop.\n *\n * Two-state loop: drain everything you can see, then park on\n * has_data until a producer (or the destroy path) wakes you. The\n * recheck under the mutex avoids lost wakeups — the producer\n * publishes seq with release ordering BEFORE locking-and-signaling,\n * so a consumer that acquires the same lock after the producer\n * unlocks is guaranteed to observe the publish. */\nstatic void *writer_main(void *arg)\n{\n    event_queue_t *q = (event_queue_t *)arg;\n    event_payload_t payload;\n    for (;;) {\n        while (dequeue_ring(q, &payload)) {\n            write_one(q, &payload);\n        }\n        pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n        /* Recheck pending under the lock — if a producer\n         * published between the dequeue-empty and the lock, the\n         * recheck catches it. */\n        while (atomic_load_explicit(&q->pending,\n                                    memory_order_acquire) == 0\n               && !atomic_load_explicit(&q->shutdown,\n                                        memory_order_acquire)) {\n            pthread_cond_wait(&q->has_data, &q->mtx);\n        }\n        int shutting = atomic_load_explicit(&q->shutdown,\n                                            memory_order_acquire);\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n        if (shutting) {\n            /* Final drain — anything still on the ring lands in\n             * the file before the thread exits. */\n            while (dequeue_ring(q, &payload)) {\n                write_one(q, &payload);\n            }\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ event_queue_create() */\nevent_queue_t *event_queue_create(const char *path)\n{\n    if (!path) return NULL;\n    event_queue_t *q = calloc(1, sizeof *q);\n    if (!q) return NULL;\n\n    q->writer = jsonl_writer_open(path);\n    if (!q->writer) { free(q); return NULL; }\n\n    /* Seed each slot's seq to its own index — the slot is ready\n     * for the producer at position == index (and at position ==\n     * index + RING_SIZE, etc.). */\n    for (uint64_t i = 0; i < EQ_RING_SIZE; i++) {\n        atomic_init(&q->ring[i].seq, i);\n    }\n    atomic_init(&q->enqueue_pos, 0);\n    atomic_init(&q->dequeue_pos, 0);\n\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&q->mtx, NULL) != 0)         goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&q->has_data,  NULL) != 0)   goto fail_data;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&q->has_space, NULL) != 0)   goto fail_space;\n    atomic_init(&q->shutdown, 0);\n    atomic_init(&q->pending,  0);\n\n    if (pthread_create(&q->writer_thread, NULL, writer_main, q) != 0)\n        goto fail_thread;\n    return q;\n\nfail_thread:\n    pthread_cond_destroy(&q->has_space);\nfail_space:\n    pthread_cond_destroy(&q->has_data);\nfail_data:\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&q->mtx);\nfail:\n    jsonl_writer_close(q->writer);\n    free(q);\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ event_queue_destroy() */\nvoid event_queue_destroy(event_queue_t *q)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    /* Signal shutdown and wake the writer if it's parked on\n     * has_data. Also wake any producer blocked on has_space —\n     * once shutdown is set, producers that find the ring full\n     * will fall through their wait loop rather than blocking\n     * indefinitely. */\n    atomic_store_explicit(&q->shutdown, 1, memory_order_release);\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&q->has_data);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&q->has_space);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n\n    pthread_join(q->writer_thread, NULL);\n\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&q->mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&q->has_data);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&q->has_space);\n    jsonl_writer_close(q->writer);\n    free(q);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ event_queue_pending() */\nint event_queue_pending(const event_queue_t *q)\n{\n    return q ? atomic_load_explicit(&q->pending,\n                                    memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emit functions */\nvoid event_queue_run_start(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                           const char *map, int n_workers)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_payload_t p = {0};\n    p.kind = EV_RUN_START;\n    p.ts   = ts;\n    copy_str_bounded(p.u.run_start.map, map, MAP_BUF_SZ);\n    p.u.run_start.n_workers = n_workers;\n    enqueue_ring(q, &p);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_task_submit(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, const char *box_id, int worker_idx)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_payload_t p = {0};\n    p.kind = EV_TASK_SUBMIT;\n    p.ts   = ts;\n    p.u.task_submit.task_id    = task_id;\n    copy_str_bounded(p.u.task_submit.box_id, box_id, BOX_ID_BUF_SZ);\n    p.u.task_submit.worker_idx = worker_idx;\n    enqueue_ring(q, &p);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_task_start(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            int task_id, int worker_idx)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_payload_t p = {0};\n    p.kind = EV_TASK_START;\n    p.ts   = ts;\n    p.u.task_start.task_id    = task_id;\n    p.u.task_start.worker_idx = worker_idx;\n    enqueue_ring(q, &p);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_task_end(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                          int task_id, int worker_idx,\n                          long duration_us, int output_size)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_payload_t p = {0};\n    p.kind = EV_TASK_END;\n    p.ts   = ts;\n    p.u.task_end.task_id     = task_id;\n    p.u.task_end.worker_idx  = worker_idx;\n    p.u.task_end.duration_us = duration_us;\n    p.u.task_end.output_size = output_size;\n    enqueue_ring(q, &p);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_run_end(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                         long duration_us, int n_tasks)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_payload_t p = {0};\n    p.kind = EV_RUN_END;\n    p.ts   = ts;\n    p.u.run_end.duration_us = duration_us;\n    p.u.run_end.n_tasks     = n_tasks;\n    enqueue_ring(q, &p);\n}\n\n/* Verbose events go straight through the jsonl_writer's mutex\n * rather than the event queue. The data payload can be up to\n * 4 KB each, so embedding them in a ring slot is wasteful;\n * verbose mode is opt-in and infrequent enough that the writer's\n * own mutex is fine. */\nvoid event_queue_task_input(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            int task_id, int port_index,\n                            const char *data, int size)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_task_input(q->writer, ts, task_id, port_index, data, size);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_task_output(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, const char *data, int size)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_task_output(q->writer, ts, task_id, data, size);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_slot_alloc(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            int slot_id, int cell_capacity, int n_cells,\n                            const char *owner_box, const char *owner_port)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_slot_alloc(q->writer, ts, slot_id, cell_capacity, n_cells,\n                          owner_box, owner_port);\n}\n\n/* Runtime mutation events (issue 319 / 248 self-construction). Same\n * direct-write path as the verbose events — graph mutations are\n * infrequent and the payload is variable-length string data that\n * doesn't fit cleanly into a fixed-size queue record. */\nvoid event_queue_box_create(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            const char *box_id, const char *kind,\n                            const char *lang, const char *ref,\n                            const char *fn)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_box_create(q->writer, ts, box_id, kind, lang, ref, fn);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_wire_add(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                          const char *from_box, const char *from_branch,\n                          const char *to_box, const char *to_input)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_wire_add(q->writer, ts, from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_push(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                      const char *from_box, const char *to_box,\n                      const char *to_input, int slot_id,\n                      int n_bytes, const char *result)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_push(q->writer, ts, from_box, to_box, to_input,\n                    slot_id, n_bytes, result);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

        "input":{
          "content":"/* src/014-event-queue.c — multi-producer event queue with a\n * dedicated writer thread.\n *\n * Design: Vyukov-style bounded MPSC ring. Producers do one\n * fetch-add / CAS on the enqueue position, write their payload\n * into the claimed slot, and bump the slot's sequence number to\n * publish it. The single consumer thread drains the ring by\n * reading the slot at the dequeue position and observing the\n * sequence number to know when the producer has finished writing.\n * A pthread mutex + condition variable provide the wakeup\n * mechanism — the mutex is NOT on the producer hot path; it's\n * only taken briefly to signal the consumer that data is\n * available (or, on rare full-ring contention, to block a\n * producer waiting for space).\n *\n * Why this shape: the mutex-linked-list predecessor serialised\n * every producer through one append-mutex; under bursty dispatch\n * (many small task_start / task_end events firing in close\n * succession from every worker) that mutex was the contention\n * hotspot. The ring's per-slot atomic seq lets producers proceed\n * independently — they only see each other if they happen to\n * claim adjacent slots in the same instant.\n *\n * Designed in issue 311.\n */\n\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"013-jsonl-events.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Ring sizing */\n/* Power-of-two ring capacity. 4096 slots × ~160 B per slot ≈ 640\n * KB per event_queue. The dispatch can fire roughly 3 events per\n * task; a run of 1000 tasks queues ~3000 events, well under\n * capacity, but the ring sizes itself to absorb dispatch bursts\n * without backpressuring producers. */\n#define EQ_RING_SIZE 4096u\n#define EQ_RING_MASK (EQ_RING_SIZE - 1u)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Event record */\ntypedef enum {\n    EV_RUN_START,\n    EV_TASK_SUBMIT,\n    EV_TASK_START,\n    EV_TASK_END,\n    EV_RUN_END,\n} event_kind_t;\n\n#define MAP_BUF_SZ    128\n#define BOX_ID_BUF_SZ 64\n\ntypedef struct {\n    event_kind_t       kind;\n    double             ts;\n    union {\n        struct {\n            char map[MAP_BUF_SZ];\n            int  n_workers;\n        } run_start;\n\n        struct {\n            int  task_id;\n            char box_id[BOX_ID_BUF_SZ];\n            int  worker_idx;\n        } task_submit;\n\n        struct {\n            int task_id;\n            int worker_idx;\n        } task_start;\n\n        struct {\n            int  task_id;\n            int  worker_idx;\n            long duration_us;\n            int  output_size;\n        } task_end;\n\n        struct {\n            long duration_us;\n            int  n_tasks;\n        } run_end;\n    } u;\n} event_payload_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Ring slot — Vyukov sequence pattern.\n *\n * Each slot carries an atomic sequence number that tracks the\n * slot's lifecycle:\n *   - At init: seq[i] = i. The slot is \"free for enqueue at\n *     position i, position i + RING_SIZE, position i + 2*RING_SIZE...\"\n *   - Producer claims position p (where p % RING_SIZE == i). It\n *     spins until seq[i] == p, writes the payload, then stores\n *     seq[i] = p + 1 (release). The slot is now \"ready for the\n *     consumer at position p.\"\n *   - Consumer reads position d (where d % RING_SIZE == i). It\n *     checks seq[i] == d + 1 (acquire). If so, reads payload,\n *     then stores seq[i] = d + RING_SIZE — the slot is now free\n *     for the next producer at position d + RING_SIZE.\n *\n * The producer / consumer never share a writable field other\n * than the per-slot seq, so contention is per-slot, not global. */\ntypedef struct {\n    _Atomic uint64_t seq;\n    event_payload_t  payload;\n} eq_slot_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Queue struct */\nstruct event_queue {\n    /* The ring itself + the producer/consumer positions. */\n    eq_slot_t        ring[EQ_RING_SIZE];\n    _Atomic uint64_t enqueue_pos;       /* next slot a producer will claim */\n    _Atomic uint64_t dequeue_pos;       /* next slot the consumer will read */\n\n    /* Wakeup mechanism. The mutex is NOT held on the lock-free\n     * enqueue / dequeue paths — it's only taken briefly to\n     * signal a CV after producing (consumer wakes on has_data)\n     * or after consuming (any blocked producer wakes on\n     * has_space). */\n    pthread_mutex_t  mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   has_data;\n    pthread_cond_t   has_space;\n    _Atomic int      shutdown;\n\n    pthread_t        writer_thread;\n    jsonl_writer_t  *writer;\n\n    /* Best-effort count, exposed by event_queue_pending(). Not\n     * load-bearing for sync — the per-slot seq is. */\n    _Atomic int      pending;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ copy_str_bounded() — strncpy + always-NUL-terminate */\nstatic void copy_str_bounded(char *dst, const char *src, size_t cap)\n{\n    if (cap == 0) return;\n    if (!src) { dst[0] = '\\0'; return; }\n    size_t n = strlen(src);\n    if (n >= cap) n = cap - 1;\n    memcpy(dst, src, n);\n    dst[n] = '\\0';\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ enqueue_ring() — claim a slot, write payload, publish seq.\n *\n * Returns 0 on success. The caller never sees failure — on a full\n * ring the producer blocks on `has_space` until the consumer\n * frees a slot. Blocking is the right tradeoff because the\n * alternative — dropping events — destroys the audit trail the\n * JSONL transcript exists for. */\nstatic void enqueue_ring(event_queue_t *q, const event_payload_t *src)\n{\n    uint64_t pos = atomic_load_explicit(&q->enqueue_pos, memory_order_relaxed);\n    for (;;) {\n        eq_slot_t *slot = &q->ring[pos & EQ_RING_MASK];\n        uint64_t seq = atomic_load_explicit(&slot->seq, memory_order_acquire);\n        int64_t  diff = (int64_t)seq - (int64_t)pos;\n\n        if (diff == 0) {\n            /* Slot is ready for us at position pos. Try to claim\n             * by bumping enqueue_pos. CAS-weak because the\n             * producer is happy to retry on spurious failure. */\n            if (atomic_compare_exchange_weak_explicit(\n                    &q->enqueue_pos, &pos, pos + 1,\n                    memory_order_relaxed, memory_order_relaxed)) {\n                slot->payload = *src;\n                /* Publish: the seq bump's release pairs with the\n                 * consumer's acquire load on slot->seq. Anything\n                 * we wrote into payload above is now visible to\n                 * the consumer once it sees seq == pos + 1. */\n                atomic_store_explicit(&slot->seq, pos + 1,\n                                      memory_order_release);\n                atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&q->pending, 1,\n                                          memory_order_relaxed);\n                /* Wake the consumer if it's sleeping. The lock\n                 * is held just long enough to signal — never on\n                 * the hot path between producers. */\n                pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n                pthread_cond_signal(&q->has_data);\n                pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n                return;\n            }\n            /* CAS lost; another producer beat us. pos was\n             * refreshed in-place by the CAS. Retry. */\n        } else if (diff < 0) {\n            /* Ring is full at position pos. Block until the\n             * consumer signals has_space. Recheck under the\n             * lock to avoid lost wakeups. */\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n            seq = atomic_load_explicit(&slot->seq, memory_order_acquire);\n            if ((int64_t)seq - (int64_t)pos < 0\n                && !atomic_load_explicit(&q->shutdown,\n                                         memory_order_acquire)) {\n                pthread_cond_wait(&q->has_space, &q->mtx);\n            }\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n            pos = atomic_load_explicit(&q->enqueue_pos,\n                                       memory_order_relaxed);\n        } else {\n            /* diff > 0: another producer raced ahead and\n             * published past us. Refresh and retry. */\n            pos = atomic_load_explicit(&q->enqueue_pos,\n                                       memory_order_relaxed);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dequeue_ring() — consumer reads the next ready slot.\n *\n * Returns 1 + fills *out if a slot was ready, 0 if empty. The\n * consumer is the sole caller, so no CAS is needed on dequeue_pos\n * — a plain store is fine. */\nstatic int dequeue_ring(event_queue_t *q, event_payload_t *out)\n{\n    uint64_t pos = atomic_load_explicit(&q->dequeue_pos,\n                                        memory_order_relaxed);\n    eq_slot_t *slot = &q->ring[pos & EQ_RING_MASK];\n    uint64_t seq = atomic_load_explicit(&slot->seq, memory_order_acquire);\n    int64_t  diff = (int64_t)seq - (int64_t)(pos + 1);\n    if (diff != 0) return 0;       /* not yet published */\n\n    *out = slot->payload;\n    /* Mark the slot free for the producer that wraps around to\n     * position (pos + RING_SIZE). */\n    atomic_store_explicit(&slot->seq, pos + EQ_RING_SIZE,\n                          memory_order_release);\n    atomic_store_explicit(&q->dequeue_pos, pos + 1,\n                          memory_order_relaxed);\n    atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&q->pending, 1, memory_order_relaxed);\n    /* Wake any producer that was blocked waiting for space. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n    pthread_cond_signal(&q->has_space);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ write_one() — serialize one event through jsonl_emit_* */\nstatic void write_one(event_queue_t *q, const event_payload_t *n)\n{\n    switch (n->kind) {\n        case EV_RUN_START:\n            jsonl_emit_run_start(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                 n->u.run_start.map,\n                                 n->u.run_start.n_workers);\n            break;\n        case EV_TASK_SUBMIT:\n            jsonl_emit_task_submit(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                   n->u.task_submit.task_id,\n                                   n->u.task_submit.box_id,\n                                   n->u.task_submit.worker_idx);\n            break;\n        case EV_TASK_START:\n            jsonl_emit_task_start(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                  n->u.task_start.task_id,\n                                  n->u.task_start.worker_idx);\n            break;\n        case EV_TASK_END:\n            jsonl_emit_task_end(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                n->u.task_end.task_id,\n                                n->u.task_end.worker_idx,\n                                n->u.task_end.duration_us,\n                                n->u.task_end.output_size);\n            break;\n        case EV_RUN_END:\n            jsonl_emit_run_end(q->writer, n->ts,\n                               n->u.run_end.duration_us,\n                               n->u.run_end.n_tasks);\n            break;\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ writer_main() — drain loop.\n *\n * Two-state loop: drain everything you can see, then park on\n * has_data until a producer (or the destroy path) wakes you. The\n * recheck under the mutex avoids lost wakeups — the producer\n * publishes seq with release ordering BEFORE locking-and-signaling,\n * so a consumer that acquires the same lock after the producer\n * unlocks is guaranteed to observe the publish. */\nstatic void *writer_main(void *arg)\n{\n    event_queue_t *q = (event_queue_t *)arg;\n    event_payload_t payload;\n    for (;;) {\n        while (dequeue_ring(q, &payload)) {\n            write_one(q, &payload);\n        }\n        pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n        /* Recheck pending under the lock — if a producer\n         * published between the dequeue-empty and the lock, the\n         * recheck catches it. */\n        while (atomic_load_explicit(&q->pending,\n                                    memory_order_acquire) == 0\n               && !atomic_load_explicit(&q->shutdown,\n                                        memory_order_acquire)) {\n            pthread_cond_wait(&q->has_data, &q->mtx);\n        }\n        int shutting = atomic_load_explicit(&q->shutdown,\n                                            memory_order_acquire);\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n        if (shutting) {\n            /* Final drain — anything still on the ring lands in\n             * the file before the thread exits. */\n            while (dequeue_ring(q, &payload)) {\n                write_one(q, &payload);\n            }\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ event_queue_create() */\nevent_queue_t *event_queue_create(const char *path)\n{\n    if (!path) return NULL;\n    event_queue_t *q = calloc(1, sizeof *q);\n    if (!q) return NULL;\n\n    q->writer = jsonl_writer_open(path);\n    if (!q->writer) { free(q); return NULL; }\n\n    /* Seed each slot's seq to its own index — the slot is ready\n     * for the producer at position == index (and at position ==\n     * index + RING_SIZE, etc.). */\n    for (uint64_t i = 0; i < EQ_RING_SIZE; i++) {\n        atomic_init(&q->ring[i].seq, i);\n    }\n    atomic_init(&q->enqueue_pos, 0);\n    atomic_init(&q->dequeue_pos, 0);\n\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&q->mtx, NULL) != 0)         goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&q->has_data,  NULL) != 0)   goto fail_data;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&q->has_space, NULL) != 0)   goto fail_space;\n    atomic_init(&q->shutdown, 0);\n    atomic_init(&q->pending,  0);\n\n    if (pthread_create(&q->writer_thread, NULL, writer_main, q) != 0)\n        goto fail_thread;\n    return q;\n\nfail_thread:\n    pthread_cond_destroy(&q->has_space);\nfail_space:\n    pthread_cond_destroy(&q->has_data);\nfail_data:\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&q->mtx);\nfail:\n    jsonl_writer_close(q->writer);\n    free(q);\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ event_queue_destroy() */\nvoid event_queue_destroy(event_queue_t *q)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    /* Signal shutdown and wake the writer if it's parked on\n     * has_data. Also wake any producer blocked on has_space —\n     * once shutdown is set, producers that find the ring full\n     * will fall through their wait loop rather than blocking\n     * indefinitely. */\n    atomic_store_explicit(&q->shutdown, 1, memory_order_release);\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&q->has_data);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&q->has_space);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n\n    pthread_join(q->writer_thread, NULL);\n\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&q->mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&q->has_data);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&q->has_space);\n    jsonl_writer_close(q->writer);\n    free(q);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ event_queue_pending() */\nint event_queue_pending(const event_queue_t *q)\n{\n    return q ? atomic_load_explicit(&q->pending,\n                                    memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emit functions */\nvoid event_queue_run_start(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                           const char *map, int n_workers)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_payload_t p = {0};\n    p.kind = EV_RUN_START;\n    p.ts   = ts;\n    copy_str_bounded(p.u.run_start.map, map, MAP_BUF_SZ);\n    p.u.run_start.n_workers = n_workers;\n    enqueue_ring(q, &p);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_task_submit(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, const char *box_id, int worker_idx)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_payload_t p = {0};\n    p.kind = EV_TASK_SUBMIT;\n    p.ts   = ts;\n    p.u.task_submit.task_id    = task_id;\n    copy_str_bounded(p.u.task_submit.box_id, box_id, BOX_ID_BUF_SZ);\n    p.u.task_submit.worker_idx = worker_idx;\n    enqueue_ring(q, &p);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_task_start(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            int task_id, int worker_idx)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_payload_t p = {0};\n    p.kind = EV_TASK_START;\n    p.ts   = ts;\n    p.u.task_start.task_id    = task_id;\n    p.u.task_start.worker_idx = worker_idx;\n    enqueue_ring(q, &p);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_task_end(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                          int task_id, int worker_idx,\n                          long duration_us, int output_size)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_payload_t p = {0};\n    p.kind = EV_TASK_END;\n    p.ts   = ts;\n    p.u.task_end.task_id     = task_id;\n    p.u.task_end.worker_idx  = worker_idx;\n    p.u.task_end.duration_us = duration_us;\n    p.u.task_end.output_size = output_size;\n    enqueue_ring(q, &p);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_run_end(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                         long duration_us, int n_tasks)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_payload_t p = {0};\n    p.kind = EV_RUN_END;\n    p.ts   = ts;\n    p.u.run_end.duration_us = duration_us;\n    p.u.run_end.n_tasks     = n_tasks;\n    enqueue_ring(q, &p);\n}\n\n/* Verbose events go straight through the jsonl_writer's mutex\n * rather than the event queue. The data payload can be up to\n * 4 KB each, so embedding them in a ring slot is wasteful;\n * verbose mode is opt-in and infrequent enough that the writer's\n * own mutex is fine. */\nvoid event_queue_task_input(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            int task_id, int port_index,\n                            const char *data, int size)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_task_input(q->writer, ts, task_id, port_index, data, size);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_task_output(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, const char *data, int size)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_task_output(q->writer, ts, task_id, data, size);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_slot_alloc(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            int slot_id, int cell_capacity, int n_cells,\n                            const char *owner_box, const char *owner_port)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_slot_alloc(q->writer, ts, slot_id, cell_capacity, n_cells,\n                          owner_box, owner_port);\n}\n\n/* Runtime mutation events (issue 319 / 248 self-construction). Same\n * direct-write path as the verbose events — graph mutations are\n * infrequent and the payload is variable-length string data that\n * doesn't fit cleanly into a fixed-size queue record. */\nvoid event_queue_box_create(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            const char *box_id, const char *kind,\n                            const char *lang, const char *ref,\n                            const char *fn)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_box_create(q->writer, ts, box_id, kind, lang, ref, fn);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_wire_add(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                          const char *from_box, const char *from_branch,\n                          const char *to_box, const char *to_input)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_wire_add(q->writer, ts, from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_push(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                      const char *from_box, const char *to_box,\n                      const char *to_input, int slot_id,\n                      int n_bytes, const char *result)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    jsonl_emit_push(q->writer, ts, from_box, to_box, to_input,\n                    slot_id, n_bytes, result);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

        "activeForm":"Extending slot store with third reconfigure ring",
        "status":"pending"

        "status":"pending"

        "name":"Edit",
        "input":{
          "old_string":"/* {{{ test_pending_count() */",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_high_contention_burst() — MPSC ring stress\n *\n * Drives much more parallelism than test_concurrent_burst:\n * 32 producer threads × 4000 events each = 128 000 lines, each\n * thread firing back-to-back with no sleeps. This exists to\n * exercise the Vyukov-style ring's CAS retry path and the\n * has_data / has_space CV interplay under heavy contention.\n *\n * Validation: line count must equal n_threads × per_thread, and\n * every line must parse as valid JSON. Within-thread ordering is\n * preserved by the ring (the task_id field counts up monotonically\n * per producer worker_idx). */\nstruct stress_args { event_queue_t *q; int n; int worker_idx; };\n\nstatic void *stress_producer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct stress_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        /* task_id == i so the consumer can verify per-thread\n         * monotonicity if it cares. */\n        event_queue_task_start(a->q, (double)i, i, a->worker_idx);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_high_contention_burst(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n    ASSERT(q);\n\n    enum { N_PROD = 32, PER = 4000 };\n    pthread_t threads[N_PROD];\n    struct stress_args args[N_PROD];\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_PROD; t++) {\n        args[t].q = q; args[t].n = PER; args[t].worker_idx = t;\n        pthread_create(&threads[t], NULL, stress_producer, &args[t]);\n    }\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_PROD; t++) pthread_join(threads[t], NULL);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    int lines = count_lines(body, len);\n    ASSERT(lines == N_PROD * PER);\n\n    /* Verify per-thread monotonicity: scan every line, group by\n     * worker_idx, check each group's task_id sequence is\n     * monotonically non-decreasing. (Cross-thread interleaving is\n     * allowed and expected; within a single producer the ring\n     * must preserve emit order.) */\n    int last_task_id[N_PROD];\n    int seen_count  [N_PROD];\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++) { last_task_id[i] = -1; seen_count[i] = 0; }\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    char *p = body;\n    while (*p) {\n        char *nl = strchr(p, '\\n');\n        if (!nl) break;\n        *nl = '\\0';\n        json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, p, NULL, NULL);\n        ASSERT(n);\n        int widx = (int)json_number_value(json_object_get(n, \"worker_idx\"));\n        int tid  = (int)json_number_value(json_object_get(n, \"task_id\"));\n        ASSERT(widx >= 0 && widx < N_PROD);\n        ASSERT(tid >= last_task_id[widx]);\n        last_task_id[widx] = tid;\n        seen_count[widx]++;\n        p = nl + 1;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++) ASSERT(seen_count[i] == PER);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_ring_full_blocks_producer() — exercise has_space CV\n *\n * Fills the ring beyond capacity from a single producer with no\n * consumer drain pressure (the writer thread is slow because it's\n * doing fwrite per line). The producer must block on has_space\n * rather than dropping events, and every emitted event must\n * eventually land in the file.\n *\n * 10 000 events exceeds the 4096-slot ring capacity by ~2.4x, so\n * the producer will hit the full-ring path multiple times. */\nstatic int test_ring_full_blocks_producer(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n    ASSERT(q);\n\n    const int N = 10000;\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {\n        event_queue_task_start(q, (double)i, i, 0);\n    }\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    ASSERT(count_lines(body, len) == N);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_pending_count() */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/014-event-queue-test.c"
        },

    "originalFile":"/* tests/014-event-queue-test.c — concurrent producer + dedicated\n * writer thread tests.\n *\n * Single-producer sanity, multi-thread burst, ordering check\n * (within a producer, events stay in submission order), shutdown\n * drain (events queued at shutdown still hit the file).\n */\n\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ tmp_path() / slurp_file() */\nstatic void tmp_path(char *out, size_t cap)\n{\n    snprintf(out, cap, \"/tmp/soramech-evq-%d-XXXXXX\", (int)getpid());\n    int fd = mkstemp(out);\n    if (fd >= 0) close(fd);\n}\n\nstatic char *slurp_file(const char *path, size_t *out_len)\n{\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"r\");\n    if (!fp) return NULL;\n    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END);\n    long sz = ftell(fp);\n    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);\n    char *buf = malloc((size_t)sz + 1);\n    fread(buf, 1, (size_t)sz, fp);\n    buf[sz] = '\\0';\n    fclose(fp);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = (size_t)sz;\n    return buf;\n}\n\nstatic int count_lines(const char *body, size_t len)\n{\n    int n = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < len; i++) if (body[i] == '\\n') n++;\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_single_producer() */\nstatic int test_single_producer(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n    ASSERT(q);\n\n    event_queue_run_start  (q, 1.0, \"calc\", 4);\n    event_queue_task_submit(q, 1.1, 0, \"add\", -1);\n    event_queue_task_start (q, 1.2, 0, 2);\n    event_queue_task_end   (q, 1.3, 0, 2, 127, 2);\n    event_queue_run_end    (q, 1.4, 1850, 1);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);   /* drain + join */\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    ASSERT(count_lines(body, len) == 5);\n\n    /* Spot-check by parsing the first and last line. */\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    char *first_nl = strchr(body, '\\n');\n    *first_nl = '\\0';\n    json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, body, NULL, NULL);\n    ASSERT(n);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"event\")), \"run_start\") == 0);\n    *first_nl = '\\n';\n\n    /* Find the last line (skip trailing newline). */\n    char *p = body + len - 1;\n    if (*p == '\\n') p--;\n    while (p > body && *p != '\\n') p--;\n    if (*p == '\\n') p++;\n    n = json_parse(a, p, NULL, NULL);\n    ASSERT(n);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"event\")), \"run_end\") == 0);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_burst() — many producers, one writer */\nstruct producer_args { event_queue_t *q; int n; int worker_idx; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        event_queue_task_start(a->q, (double)i, i, a->worker_idx);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_burst(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n    ASSERT(q);\n\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 250 };\n    pthread_t threads[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args[N_PROD];\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_PROD; t++) {\n        args[t].q = q; args[t].n = PER; args[t].worker_idx = t;\n        pthread_create(&threads[t], NULL, producer_thread, &args[t]);\n    }\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_PROD; t++) pthread_join(threads[t], NULL);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    int lines = count_lines(body, len);\n    ASSERT(lines == N_PROD * PER);\n\n    /* Every line must be parsable JSON. */\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    char *p = body;\n    int ok = 0;\n    while (*p) {\n        char *nl = strchr(p, '\\n');\n        if (!nl) break;\n        *nl = '\\0';\n        json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, p, NULL, NULL);\n        ASSERT(n);\n        ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"event\")),\n                      \"task_start\") == 0);\n        ok++;\n        p = nl + 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(ok == N_PROD * PER);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_shutdown_drains_late_events() */\n/* Emit events right before destroy; they must end up in the file. */\nstatic int test_shutdown_drains_late_events(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n\n    /* Emit a small burst without giving the writer time to drain\n     * before destroy. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n        event_queue_task_start(q, (double)i, i, 0);\n    }\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    ASSERT(count_lines(body, len) == 50);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_pending_count() */\nstatic int test_pending_count(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n\n    /* pending is best-effort; the writer might drain between emit\n     * and our read. Just verify it's a small bounded value. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) event_queue_task_start(q, 0.0, i, 0);\n    int pending = event_queue_pending(q);\n    ASSERT(pending >= 0);\n    ASSERT(pending <= 10);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n    ASSERT(event_queue_pending(NULL) == 0);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"014-event-queue-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(single_producer);\n    RUN(concurrent_burst);\n    RUN(shutdown_drains_late_events);\n    RUN(pending_count);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "oldString":"/* {{{ test_pending_count() */",
    "newString":"/* {{{ test_high_contention_burst() — MPSC ring stress\n *\n * Drives much more parallelism than test_concurrent_burst:\n * 32 producer threads × 4000 events each = 128 000 lines, each\n * thread firing back-to-back with no sleeps. This exists to\n * exercise the Vyukov-style ring's CAS retry path and the\n * has_data / has_space CV interplay under heavy contention.\n *\n * Validation: line count must equal n_threads × per_thread, and\n * every line must parse as valid JSON. Within-thread ordering is\n * preserved by the ring (the task_id field counts up monotonically\n * per producer worker_idx). */\nstruct stress_args { event_queue_t *q; int n; int worker_idx; };\n\nstatic void *stress_producer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct stress_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        /* task_id == i so the consumer can verify per-thread\n         * monotonicity if it cares. */\n        event_queue_task_start(a->q, (double)i, i, a->worker_idx);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_high_contention_burst(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n    ASSERT(q);\n\n    enum { N_PROD = 32, PER = 4000 };\n    pthread_t threads[N_PROD];\n    struct stress_args args[N_PROD];\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_PROD; t++) {\n        args[t].q = q; args[t].n = PER; args[t].worker_idx = t;\n        pthread_create(&threads[t], NULL, stress_producer, &args[t]);\n    }\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_PROD; t++) pthread_join(threads[t], NULL);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    int lines = count_lines(body, len);\n    ASSERT(lines == N_PROD * PER);\n\n    /* Verify per-thread monotonicity: scan every line, group by\n     * worker_idx, check each group's task_id sequence is\n     * monotonically non-decreasing.     "originalFile":"/* tests/014-event-queue-test.c — concurrent producer + dedicated\n * writer thread tests.\n *\n * Single-producer sanity, multi-thread burst, ordering check\n * (within a producer, events stay in submission order), shutdown\n * drain (events queued at shutdown still hit the file).\n */\n\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ tmp_path() / slurp_file() */\nstatic void tmp_path(char *out, size_t cap)\n{\n    snprintf(out, cap, \"/tmp/soramech-evq-%d-XXXXXX\", (int)getpid());\n    int fd = mkstemp(out);\n    if (fd >= 0) close(fd);\n}\n\nstatic char *slurp_file(const char *path, size_t *out_len)\n{\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"r\");\n    if (!fp) return NULL;\n    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END);\n    long sz = ftell(fp);\n    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);\n    char *buf = malloc((size_t)sz + 1);\n    fread(buf, 1, (size_t)sz, fp);\n    buf[sz] = '\\0';\n    fclose(fp);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = (size_t)sz;\n    return buf;\n}\n\nstatic int count_lines(const char *body, size_t len)\n{\n    int n = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < len; i++) if (body[i] == '\\n') n++;\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_single_producer() */\nstatic int test_single_producer(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n    ASSERT(q);\n\n    event_queue_run_start  (q, 1.0, \"calc\", 4);\n    event_queue_task_submit(q, 1.1, 0, \"add\", -1);\n    event_queue_task_start (q, 1.2, 0, 2);\n    event_queue_task_end   (q, 1.3, 0, 2, 127, 2);\n    event_queue_run_end    (q, 1.4, 1850, 1);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q); (Cross-thread interleaving is\n     * allowed and expected; within a single producer the ring\n     * must preserve emit order.) */\n    int last_task_id[N_PROD];\n    int seen_count  [N_PROD];\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++) { last_task_id[i] = -1; seen_count[i] = 0; }\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    char *p = body;\n    while (*p) {\n        char *nl = strchr(p, '\\n');\n        if (!nl) break;\n        *nl = '\\0';\n        json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, p, NULL, NULL);\n        ASSERT(n);\n        int widx = (int)json_number_value(json_object_get(n, \"worker_idx\"));\n        int tid  = (int)json_number_value(json_object_get(n, \"task_id\"));\n        ASSERT(widx >= 0 && widx < N_PROD);\n        ASSERT(tid >= last_task_id[widx]);\n        last_task_id[widx] = tid;\n        seen_count[widx]++;\n        p = nl + 1;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++) ASSERT(seen_count[i] == PER);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_ring_full_blocks_producer() — exercise has_space CV\n *\n * Fills the ring beyond capacity from a single producer with no\n * consumer drain pressure (the writer thread is slow because it's\n * doing fwrite per line).         "content":"1\t#!/bin/bash\n2\t# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n3\t#\n4\t# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n5\t# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n6\t# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n7\t# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n8\t# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n9\t#\n10\t# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n11\t# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n12\t# relative to ${DIR}.\n13\t\n14\tset -u\n15\t\n16\tDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n17\tif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n18\t    DIR=\"$1\"\n19\tfi\n20\t\n21\tcd \"$DIR\"\n22\t\n23\tpass=0\n24\tfail=0\n25\tfailures=()\n26\t\n27\t# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\n28\tcheck_map() {\n29\t    local map=\"$1\"\n30\t    shift\n31\t    local expected=(\"$@\")\n32\t\n33\t    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n34\t\n35\t    local output\n36\t    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n37\t    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n38\t    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n39\t    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n40\t    # the same worker).\n41\t    local workers_env=\"\"\n42\t    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n43\t        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n44\t    fi\n45\t    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n46\t        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n47\t    else\n48\t        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n49\t    fi\n50\t    local rc=$?\n51\t\n52\t    local missing=\"\"\n53\t    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n54\t        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n55\t    fi\n56\t    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n57\t        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n58\t            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n59\t        fi\n60\t    done\n61\t\n62\t    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n63\t        printf \"ok\\n\"\n64\t        pass=$((pass + 1))\n65\t    else\n66\t        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n67\t        fail=$((fail + 1))\n68\t        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n69\t    fi\n70\t}\n71\t# }}}\n72\t\n73\t# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\n74\tpipeline_output_check() {\n75\t    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n76\t    rm -f \"$file\"\n77\t    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n78\t    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n79\t    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n80\t        local content\n81\t        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n82\t        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n83\t            printf \"ok\\n\"\n84\t            pass=$((pass + 1))\n85\t        else\n86\t            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n87\t            fail=$((fail + 1))\n88\t            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n89\t        fi\n90\t    else\n91\t        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n92\t        fail=$((fail + 1))\n93\t        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n94\t    fi\n95\t}\n96\t# }}}\n97\t\n98\t# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n99\t# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n100\t# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n101\t# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n102\t# output as the source map.\n103\tcompile_pipeline_check() {\n104\t    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n105\t    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n106\t    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n107\t\n108\t    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n109\t\n110\t    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n111\t    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n112\t        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n113\t        fail=$((fail + 1))\n114\t        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n115\t        return\n116\t    fi\n117\t    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n118\t        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n119\t        fail=$((fail + 1))\n120\t        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n121\t        return\n122\t    fi\n123\t\n124\t    rm -f \"$file\"\n125\t    local output\n126\t    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n127\t\n128\t    local content=\"\"\n129\t    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n130\t\n131\t    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n132\t        printf \"ok\\n\"\n133\t        pass=$((pass + 1))\n134\t    else\n135\t        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n136\t        fail=$((fail + 1))\n137\t        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n138\t    fi\n139\t}\n140\t# }}}\n141\t\n142\t# {{{ run all fixtures\n143\techo \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n144\t\n145\tcheck_map \"calc\" \\\n146\t    \"add → 42\"\n147\t\n148\tcheck_map \"hello\" \\\n149\t    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n150\t\n151\tcheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n152\t    \"classify → 8\" \\\n153\t    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n154\t    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n155\t    \"mid → (no output)\"\n156\t\n157\tcheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n158\t    \"iter → hi\" \\\n159\t    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n160\t    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n161\t    \"c → (no output)\"\n162\t\n163\t# Issue 240 — randomizer routing. Hash(counter=0) mod 3 = 0, so\n164\t# the first invocation deterministically lands on branch 0;\n165\t# tagger_0 fires, tagger_1 and tagger_2 stay silent.\n166\tcheck_map \"randomizer-route\" \\\n167\t    \"tagger_0 → got_0:hi\" \\\n168\t    \"tagger_1 → (no output)\" \\\n169\t    \"tagger_2 → (no output)\"\n170\t\n171\t# Issue 241 — weighted routing. weights = [1, 0, 0] puts all\n172\t# probability mass on branch 0; the cumulative-band lookup\n173\t# always picks tagger_0, the other two never fire.\n174\tcheck_map \"weighted-route\" \\\n175\t    \"tagger_0 → got_0:hi\" \\\n176\t    \"tagger_1 → (no output)\" \\\n177\t    \"tagger_2 → (no output)\"\n178\t\n179\t# Issue 242 — distributor routing. All downstream slots empty\n180\t# means the argmin sees a tie; the tiebreaker counter at 0\n181\t# picks branch 0. Subsequent calls would rotate via the\n182\t# counter; this fixture exercises the first call only.\n183\tcheck_map \"distributor-route\" \\\n184\t    \"tagger_0 → got_0:hi\" \\\n185\t    \"tagger_1 → (no output)\" \\\n186\t    \"tagger_2 → (no output)\"\n187\t\n188\t# Issue 243 — multi-band comparator. Thresholds [3, 7] carve\n189\t# three bands. Seed value 5 lands strictly between 3 and 7, so\n190\t# only the between_3_7 branch fires (tagger_1). The picker also\n191\t# proves the band-name formatter matches between dispatch and\n192\t# the wire's from_branch string.\n193\tcheck_map \"multi-band-comparator-route\" \\\n194\t    \"tagger_0 → (no output)\" \\\n195\t    \"tagger_1 → got_1:5\" \\\n196\t    \"tagger_2 → (no output)\"\n197\t\n198\t# Issue 253 — nonlinearity refactor. The routing kind grew an\n199\t# auto-calibrating ring buffer for bounds, dropped the variant\n200\t# names in favour of a `range` toggle, and the output is now\n201\t# v × score (gated linear unit) rather than score alone.       "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n    # the same worker).\n    local workers_env=\"\"\n    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n    fi\n    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    else\n        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    fi\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\n# Issue 240 — randomizer routing. Hash(counter=0) mod 3 = 0, so\n# the first invocation deterministically lands on branch 0;\n# tagger_0 fires, tagger_1 and tagger_2 stay silent.\ncheck_map \"randomizer-route\" \\\n    \"tagger_0 → got_0:hi\" \\\n    \"tagger_1 → (no output)\" \\\n    \"tagger_2 → (no output)\"\n\n# Issue 241 — weighted routing. weights = [1, 0, 0] puts all\n# probability mass on branch 0; the cumulative-band lookup\n# always picks tagger_0, the other two never fire.\ncheck_map \"weighted-route\" \\\n    \"tagger_0 → got_0:hi\" \\\n    \"tagger_1 → (no output)\" \\\n    \"tagger_2 → (no output)\"\n\n# Issue 242 — distributor routing.
